confirmed.title: Login's decoy hash runs at test cost (N=4096) while real passwords are N=131072, turning the "equalised work" path into a 30x timing oracle for account existence and lockout state
confirmed.evidence: auth-service.ts:983-985 — `const DECOY_HASH = "scrypt$4096$8$1$AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==$" + "Ki2N...Zg==";` (N=4096). password.ts:56-79 — `verifyPassword` parses N/r/p FROM THE ENCODED STRING (`const N = Number(parts[1])`) and calls scrypt with them, so the decoy costs N=4096 work. password.ts:30 — `DEFAULT_SCRYPT_PARAMS = { N: 1 << 17 /* 131072 */, r: 8, p: 1 }`. backend/src/index.ts:214 — production builds `new AuthService(db, { sessionTtlMs: ... })` with NO `scryptParams`, so every stored user hash is `scrypt$131072$8$1$...`. auth-service.ts:380 — `const encoded = locked ? DECOY_HASH : (row?.passwordHash ?? DECOY_HASH);`. The decoy's 64-byte digest is well-formed (verified: base64 decodes to exactly 64 bytes, so the `expected.length !== KEY_LENGTH` early-return at password.ts:71 does NOT fire and scrypt really runs). Measured on this machine with node: N=4096 -> 7.6 ms average, N=131072 -> 226.8 ms average, ratio 29.9x. Test blind spot, proven by grep: every AuthService in the suite is built with `TEST_SCRYPT_PARAMS` (= { N: 1 << 12 } = 4096, password.ts:33) — `grep -rn "scryptParams" backend/` shows test-app.ts:162 and auth-service.test.ts:22,117,140,274 all use it — which is the SAME N as the decoy, so tests see zero cost difference; and `grep -rn "decoy|DECOY|timing" backend/packages/security/src backend/src` returns only comments and `timingSafeEqual`, no timing assertion anywhere.
confirmed.why_it_matters: This is precisely the oracle ADR-125 and the code's own comment claim to prevent ("verifying against a decoy hash keeps the timing of 'unknown email' and 'locked' close to 'wrong password'. Skipping the verification for a locked account would replace the message oracle with a timing one."). In production, POST /api/v1/auth/login answers in ~227 ms for a registered, unlocked address and ~8 ms for an unknown address or a LOCKED one — a ~219 ms gap readable over any network with one request per guess. So (a) the endpoint is a user-enumeration oracle despite every denial returning the identical string INVALID_CREDENTIALS, and (b) an attacker who has tripped the lockout can see exactly when it expires, which restores the attack ADR-125 was written to close. The docstring at auth-service.ts:973-975 ("A real scrypt hash of a random value... Generated once at module load so login timing does not depend on account existence") is false twice over: it is a hardcoded literal, not generated at module load, and it does not equalise the work. The defect cannot be caught by the suite by construction, because TEST_SCRYPT_PARAMS.N happens to equal the decoy's N.
confirmed.fix: Derive the decoy at module load (or lazily per-instance) using the same params real hashes are written with — e.g. `const DECOY_HASH_PROMISE = hashPassword(randomBytes(32).toString('hex'), this.scryptParams)` cached on the AuthService — so its N/r/p always track `DEFAULT_SCRYPT_PARAMS` / the configured params. Add a test that asserts the decoy's parsed N equals the params the service hashes with (that single assertion fails today and would have caught this).
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — I can restate the defect from the code. auth-service.ts:983-985 defines DECOY_HASH as a hardcoded literal beginning "scrypt$4096$8$1$..." (N=4096). password.ts:56-79 shows verifyPassword parses N/r/p FROM the encoded string (`const N = Number(parts[1])`) and passes them to scrypt, so verifying against the decoy costs N=4096 work regardless of policy. I parsed the literal exactly as verifyPassword does: 6 parts, alg "scrypt", N=4096/r=8/p=1, salt 16 bytes, digest exactly 64 bytes — so the `expected.length !== KEY_LENGTH` early-return at password.ts:71 does NOT fire and scrypt really runs. Meanwhile password.ts:30 sets DEFAULT_SCRYPT_PARAMS N = 1<<17 (131072), auth-service.ts:93 stores `this.scryptParams = options.scryptParams` (undefined in prod), and `grep -rn "new AuthService" backend/src/` returns exactly two sites: index.ts:214 `new AuthService(db, { sessionTtlMs: ... })` with NO scryptParams, and test-app.ts:162 with TEST params. So hashPassword (lines 148, 514) falls through to DEFAULT_SCRYPT_PARAMS and every production hash is scrypt$131072$8$1$..., while auth-service.ts:380 `const encoded = locked ? DECOY_HASH : (row?.passwordHash ?? DECOY_HASH)` sends the unknown-email AND locked paths through the cheap decoy.

Measured on this machine with the same maxmem formula as maxmemFor(): N=4096 -> 8.8 ms avg, N=131072 -> 297.4 ms avg, a ~34x / ~289 ms gap (slightly worse than the reported 30x). That is not a statistical timing attack; it is a two-orders-of-magnitude difference readable in a single request.

Reachability traced: routes/v1/auth.ts:81-86 registers POST /api/v1/auth/login calling ctx.auth.login directly. It is rate-limited at authRateLimitMax*2 per 10 minutes (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX default 5, config.ts:262), i.e. 10 attempts per IP per 10 min — that throttles bulk enumeration but does not remove the oracle, since probing one address or checking lockout expiry costs one request.

The test blind spot is real: TEST_SCRYPT_PARAMS = { N: 1<<12 } = 4096, the SAME N as the decoy, and `grep -rn "scryptParams" backend/` shows every test AuthService built with it (test-app.ts:162, auth-service.test.ts:22/117/140/274, account-deletion.test.ts:39). `grep -rn "decoy\|DECOY" backend/ --include=*.ts` (excluding node_modules/dist) returns only three source lines — the comment at 377, the use at 380, the definition at 983 — no test references the decoy and no test asserts timing.

Not already fixed: ADR-125 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2063-2067) states the intent verbatim ("The verification still runs against a decoy hash when locked: skipping the work would have replaced a message oracle with a timing one") and no ADR through ADR-143 touches the decoy's cost parameters.

Two corrections to the report, neither fatal. (1) The docstring it quotes ("A real scrypt hash of a random value... Generated once at module load", lines 972-975) actually sits above the INVALID_CREDENTIALS docstring and const, not directly above DECOY_HASH — it is an orphaned comment, but it does describe the decoy and it is still false. (2) "restores the attack ADR-125 was written to close" overstates part (b): ADR-125's attack was reading the correct password off the differing message, and that remains closed; what leaks here is lockout state/expiry, a lesser but real leak. Part (a) — a user-enumeration oracle despite every denial returning the identical INVALID_CREDENTIALS string — is exactly right and is precisely what the comment at auth-service.ts:376-379 claims to prevent.

Severity stays P1: unauthenticated and exploitable now, a shipped security control that is documented as working and is entirely non-functional, but it discloses account existence and lock state rather than credentials, so not P0.

confirmed.title: An API key can list and revoke the account owner's browser sessions, though the route group's docstring says "Session credential only"; the test named for that property sends no credential at all
confirmed.evidence: backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:160-174 — `app.get("/api/v1/auth/sessions", async (request) => { const user = requireUser(request); return { sessions: await ctx.auth.listSessions(user.id) }; })` and `app.delete("/api/v1/auth/sessions/:sessionId", ...)` both call ONLY `requireUser`, which accepts either credential type (plugins/auth.ts:130-133). `grep -n 'method !== "session"' backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts` returns exactly two lines — 139 (POST /api/v1/auth/password) and 265 (DELETE /api/v1/auth/account) — not four. The docstring that heads this group, auth.ts:110-124, is titled "Changing your own password, and seeing who else is signed in" and states at :120 "Session credential only, like account deletion (ADR-108): an API key is a project-scoped automation credential and must not be able to take over the account that owns it." The covering test, backend/src/routes/v1/password-and-sessions.test.ts:216-226, `it("requires a session credential, not an API key")`, injects BOTH requests with no `headers` at all — no cookie, no bearer — so the 401 it asserts is produced by the deny-by-default plugin (plugins/auth.ts:79-91) regardless of what either route checks. No API key is created or presented anywhere in that file.
confirmed.why_it_matters: An API key is bound to exactly one project (`authenticate` returns `projectId: row.key.projectId`, auth-service.ts:678) and is documented throughout as a project-scoped automation credential — the kind of secret that lives in CI, in a contractor's script, or in a third-party service. These two routes are ACCOUNT-scoped, so the key escapes its stated blast radius: it can enumerate every live session of the user who created it, complete with `ipAddress` and `userAgent` (auth-service.ts:540-551 — exactly the fields ADR-127 says are there so a human can recognise a browser), and revoke all of them, logging the owner out of every browser they own. Bearer requests are deliberately exempt from CSRF (plugins/auth.ts:66-69), so nothing else stands in the way. The reasoning ADR-108 gives for refusing API keys on account deletion applies verbatim here and was simply not applied; and the one test that would have caught it asserts a condition that cannot fail.
confirmed.fix: Add the same `if (request.auth?.method !== "session") throw new PermissionError(...)` guard used at auth.ts:139 and :265 to both `GET /api/v1/auth/sessions` and `DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/:sessionId`. Rewrite password-and-sessions.test.ts:216 to actually mint an API key (POST /api/v1/api-keys) and present it as `Authorization: Bearer aip_...` against all three routes; that version fails today on two of the three.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and reproduced empirically. auth.ts:160-176 — GET /api/v1/auth/sessions and DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/:sessionId call only requireUser(), which accepts either credential type (plugins/auth.ts:129-132). `grep -n 'method !== \"session\"' backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts` returns exactly two lines, 139 and 265; a repo-wide grep for auth.method finds no other guard. The group docstring at auth.ts:113-124 is titled \"Changing your own password, and seeing who else is signed in\" and asserts at :120 \"Session credential only, like account deletion (ADR-108)\" — two of the three routes it heads do not honour it. No ADR fixes this: ADR-127 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2093) introduces the routes and never mentions credential scope; ADR-108's session-only rule was applied to account deletion and password change only.

I proved it by running a temporary probe test (backend/src/routes/v1, vitest, then deleted; git status is back to its prior state): minted a key via POST /api/v1/api-keys from a session, then with ONLY `Authorization: Bearer aip_...` — GET /api/v1/auth/sessions returned 200 with the owner's sessions; DELETE /api/v1/auth/sessions/<id> returned 200; GET /api/v1/auth/me with the owner's cookie then returned 401, i.e. the project-scoped key logged the account owner out of a browser. POST /api/v1/auth/password correctly returned 403, exactly as the finding states. listSessions (auth-service.ts:539-556) does return ipAddress/userAgent/lastUsedAt, and bearer requests skip CSRF (plugins/auth.ts:65-71), so nothing else intervenes.

The vacuous-test claim is also correct: password-and-sessions.test.ts:216-226, it(\"requires a session credential, not an API key\"), injects both requests with no `headers` at all, so the 401s are produced by the deny-by-default hook (plugins/auth.ts:84-92) regardless of either route's check; no API key is created anywhere in the file, and the DELETE route is not covered at all.

One correction to the finding's framing, which does not change the verdict: docs/API.md:119-120 does document these routes as \"session or API key\", but API.md is generated by scraping the route files (API.md:3, \"do not hand-edit\") and api-contract.test.ts asserts it against the live server, so it mirrors the bug rather than stating intent. The code docstring is the only statement of intent, and the code violates it.

Severity stays P1, not P0: exploitation requires possession of an API key the account owner minted (the leaked-CI/contractor case the docstring itself names), and the escape does not reach password change or account deletion — both guarded. The real impact is a project-scoped automation credential reading account-scoped session metadata (IP, user agent, last used) and revoking every session, signing the owner out of all browsers. A real defect in a shipped capability, not exploitable without an already-compromised key.

confirmed.title: The viewer/editor project-role system is unreachable from the product: the only route that can create a non-admin member, and the audit trail scoped to project admins, have no client anywhere
confirmed.evidence: `POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members` (auth.ts:216, `project:admin`) and `GET /api/v1/audit` (auth.ts:376, `project:admin`) have no caller outside the backend. Greps stated: `grep -rn "members" frontend/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v node_modules` returns only three unrelated comment lines about the Memory screen; `grep -rn "api/v1/audit" frontend/` returns nothing; `grep -rn "v1/audit|/members|addProjectMember" frontend/app/lib/api.ts frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts` returns nothing. `grep -rn "/api/v1/audit" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.md .` (excl. node_modules, dist) returns only the route definition and docs/API.md:104-108 — not even a backend test. Every other membership write hardcodes the top role: auth-service.ts:196 (signup) inserts `projectMembers` with `role: "admin"`, auth-service.ts:786 (createProject) inserts `role: "admin"`, and auth-service.ts:188 is the ONLY `insert(organizationMembers)` in the tree and writes `role: "owner"`.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Every user the product can create is `admin` on every project they can see, so `viewer`, `editor`, `ORG_ROLE_PERMISSIONS.member = []`, and every read/write split in shared/src/auth.ts (`files:read` vs `files:write`, `chat:write`, `agent:approve`, `apikey:manage`, `project:admin`) can never differ for anyone reached through the UI — the RBAC table is decorative in practice. SECURITY.md:96-98 presents it as a live control ("A `viewer` cannot spend money — no `chat:write`, `agent:run` or `media:generate`"), and frontend/app/settings/page.tsx:314 carries the comment "`apikey:manage` is an admin permission, so an ordinary member gets a 403 here" — describing a user the product has no way to create. Separately, SECURITY.md §8's guarantee that "Denials are recorded, not just grants" is scoped to `project:admin` via GET /api/v1/audit, which nothing in the product, and no test, ever calls. This is not a privilege bug — the members route works via curl or an API key and the backend tests exercise `addProjectMember` directly (auth-service.test.ts:206, account-deletion.test.ts:137) — it is capability that exists, is tested, and has no door.
confirmed.fix: Either give Settings a project-members card (invite by email + role, plus an audit view for project admins) so the roles the permission table defines can actually be assigned and the audit trail read, or record in docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md that collaboration is API-only today and that every UI-created user is a project admin — and soften SECURITY.md:96-98 and the settings comment accordingly.
confirmed.verdict:
VERIFIED REAL at P2, with two evidence claims corrected.

Restated from the code myself:
- backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:214-221 registers POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members behind requireProject(..., "project:admin") -> ctx.auth.addProjectMember(authCtx, email, role). auth.ts:376-379 registers GET /api/v1/audit behind "project:admin" -> ctx.auth.listAudit(authCtx).
- backend/packages/security/src/auth-service.ts:810 (addProjectMember) is the ONLY role-parameterized membership write in the tree. Every other membership insert hardcodes the top role: :199 (signup) role:"admin", :786 (createProject) role:"admin", and :184 -- the only insert(organizationMembers) anywhere -- role:"owner". Confirmed by `grep -rn "insert(projectMembers)\|insert(organizationMembers)" --include=*.ts backend/` (excl. node_modules, dist), which returns exactly those four sites.
- No product UI reaches either route. `grep -rni "invite\|collaborat\|projectRole\|\"viewer\"\|'viewer'\|\"editor\"\|'editor'" frontend/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (excl. node_modules) returns ZERO lines. `grep -rn "members" frontend/ ...` returns only three unrelated Memory-screen comments. `grep -rni "audit" frontend/` returns only ADR-citation comments, never the endpoint. frontend/app/lib/api.ts exports only uploadFile and assetUrl as functions -- nothing for members or audit. `find frontend/app -name page.tsx` lists 18 pages (agent, ask, audio, chat, coding, files, images, login, memory, root, platform, settings, signup, tasks, usage, videos) -- no members or audit screen.

Impact that follows: every user the product can create is `admin` on every project they can see, so viewer/editor and every read/write split in shared/src/auth.ts cannot differ for any UI-reached user. SECURITY.md:96-98 presents this as a live control ("A `viewer` cannot spend money -- no `chat:write`, `agent:run` or `media:generate`"), frontend/app/settings/page.tsx:314-315 carries the comment "`apikey:manage` is an admin permission, so an ordinary member gets a 403 here" -- describing a user the product has no way to create -- and docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md records NO such limitation (grep for member/viewer/editor/collaborat/invite/role returns only the RESOLVED ADR-049 RBAC row and two unrelated rows). No ADR in 123..143 addresses this; ADR-143 is the unrelated tools/:id/enable button case.

TWO EVIDENCE CLAIMS IN THE FINDING ARE WRONG and overstate it:
1. "not even a backend test" calls GET /api/v1/audit is FALSE. backend/src/routes/api-contract.test.ts parses docs/API.md into rows (asserting rows.length >= 50) and sends EVERY row anonymously (expect 401) and again with viewer headers (expect 403 naming exactly the documented permission). /api/v1/audit is docs/API.md:108, so the route is exercised twice on every run. The finding's literal-string grep missed it because the test drives paths from the doc rather than from literals -- exactly the failure mode the audit rules warn about. listAudit is also directly tested at auth-service.test.ts:286 and :305.
2. "the members route has no caller outside the backend" / "the RBAC table is decorative in practice" is overstated. api-contract.test.ts:81-89 invites a real viewer THROUGH THE REAL ROUTE ("A real viewer, invited through the real members route", expect 201), then asserts that viewer's 403 against every protected documented row. The role table is therefore enforced and re-proved on every test run, and is assignable by session or API key as docs/API.md documents.

Net: the headline defect survives -- a shipped, documented, tested capability (assigning viewer/editor, reading the project audit trail) has no door in the product, and two shipped doc/comment claims describe a user state the product cannot produce, with nothing in the risks doc recording it. That matches the target shapes "a route with no UI" and "a claim in a comment/doc that the code does not honour". It is not a privilege, isolation or authorization bug -- the backend refuses correctly and is tested doing so. Severity P2 as reported is correct: real, non-blocking, nothing exploitable, no core capability broken. The finding's suggested fix (a members/audit card in Settings, or a risks-doc entry plus softened SECURITY.md wording) is appropriate; only its "no test" evidence line should be dropped.

confirmed.title: The human-in-the-loop Approve / Reject / Cancel buttons report nothing at all when the API refuses them — and a project viewer is shown all three
confirmed.evidence:
`grep -c catch frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx` -> `0`. The component has exactly three `useState` calls (lines 29, 239 — `busyNodeId` and the tab), none for an error. handleApprove (L33-41) and handleReject (L42-50) are `try { await approveNode(...) } finally { setBusyNodeId(null) }` — no catch; handleCancel (L51-53) is a bare `await cancelTask(taskId)`. They are invoked as floating promises: `onClick={() => handleApprove(waitingApproval.id)}` (L139), `onClick={() => handleReject(...)}` (L142), `onClick={handleCancel}` (L67). A rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the screen is unchanged.
The authorization gap: the page is reached through `GET /api/v1/agent/tasks/:id`, documented `project:read` (docs/API.md:75), while approve/reject need `agent:approve` (API.md:76,79) and cancel needs `agent:run` (API.md:77). `shared/src/auth.ts:49` — `const VIEWER: Permission[] = ["project:read", "files:read", "memory:read", "usage:read"]` — holds none of the agent permissions. `backend/src/routes/api-contract.test.ts:78-92` creates a real viewer through the real members route, so the role is live.
No test covers the press: `frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.test.tsx` renders the card and asserts on text only; it never clicks Approve.
confirmed.why_it_matters: This is the approval gate the whole trust boundary rests on (ADR-133/135), on destructive tool calls — the only kind that reaches it. A viewer opening a parked task sees a fully-enabled Approve button; pressing it 403s and the card does not move, does not say why, and does not say who can approve. The approver cannot distinguish 'the API refused me', 'someone else already decided this node' (404 from `resolveDecisionTarget`), and 'my network dropped' from 'the button does nothing'. ADR-123 fixed exactly this silent-failure shape for chat send and ADR-143 fixed exactly this refuses-the-user-who-can-see-it shape for the MCP Enable button; neither pass reached this screen.
confirmed.fix: Add an error state to TaskDetail and catch in all three handlers, rendering the message next to the buttons (the pattern `MemoryView`/`SettingsView` already use). Separately, gate the controls on the permission the way ADR-143 gated the Enable button: derive the caller's project role from `useSession().projects` and, for a viewer, render an explanatory line instead of Approve/Reject/Cancel.
confirmed.verdict:
VERIFIED REAL, severity lowered P0 -> P1.

Restated from the code myself:

(1) Silent failure - confirmed. frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx has exactly two useState calls in the component (busyNodeId L29; the L239 tab state belongs to CodingTabs), none for an error. handleApprove (L33-41) and handleReject (L42-50) are `try { await ... } finally { setBusyNodeId(null) }` with no catch; handleCancel (L51-53) is a bare `await cancelTask(taskId)`. `grep -c catch frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx` -> 0. All three are called as floating promises from onClick (L67, L139, L142). apiFetch throws ApiError on every non-2xx (frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts:129-137), so a refusal becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Proven absent globally: `grep -rn "unhandledrejection|ErrorBoundary|global-error" frontend/app` -> no hits, and there is no error.tsx anywhere under frontend/app. It is an outlier rather than house style: memory/page.tsx 3 catches / 7 setError, settings/page.tsx 7/16, tasks/page.tsx catches on both load and create.

(2) Viewer gap - confirmed and reachable. backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts: GET /api/v1/agent/tasks/:id requires project:read (L105); /approve and /reject require agent:approve (L163, L175); /cancel requires agent:run (L186, with the comment "a viewer must not be able to halt another member's work"). shared/src/auth.ts:49 VIEWER = ["project:read","files:read","memory:read","usage:read"]; agent:run/agent:approve first appear in EDITOR (L50-58). requireProject -> requirePermission (backend/src/plugins/auth.ts:165) throws PermissionError. Navigation path is live for a viewer: app-chrome.tsx:9 shows the Tasks link to every authenticated user, tasks/page.tsx:44 links each row to /agent/:id, and agent/[id]/page.tsx wraps only in RequireSession (no role gate). TaskDetail renders Approve/Reject (L139-144) and Cancel (L67) unconditionally. The viewer role is live, not hypothetical (backend/src/routes/api-contract.test.ts:78-92 invites one through the real members route).

(3) Untested - confirmed. `grep -n "Approve|click|fireEvent|userEvent|approveNode" frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.test.tsx` matches only a prose comment at line 13. `grep -rn approve frontend/e2e/` -> nothing.

(4) No ADR covers it. ADR-135 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2199) fixed WHAT the card displays, not what happens on press. ADR-143 (:2303) gated the MCP Enable button on SYSTEM ADMIN via SystemAdminOnly; session-context.tsx exposes no project-role helper at all (`grep -n role frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx` -> no hits), so nothing generalized to this screen.

Why P1 and not P0: the finding's P0 rationale does not follow from the code. The backend enforces authorization correctly - a viewer is refused server-side - so nothing is exploitable and no tenant/authz boundary is bypassed. The happy path for a legitimate approver works end to end: approve succeeds and the card clears via the SSE stream (useTaskEvents). What is broken is the failure path only (three controls that report nothing when refused, so 403 vs 404-already-decided vs network loss vs "the button does nothing" are indistinguishable) plus a misleading affordance shown to a user who can never use it. That is a real defect in a shipped capability - top of P1 because of where it sits - not a broken core capability or an exploitable hole.

confirmed.title: The Platform screen can never show why an MCP server failed: it reads `server.error`, the API returns `lastError`
confirmed.evidence: frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:38-43 declares `interface McpRow { id; status; toolCount?; error?: string | null }` and line 249 renders `{server.error ? {server.error} : null}`. The route emits a different field name — backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:127-145 maps `servers` to `{ id, status, transport, toolCount, toolIds, refusedToolIds, lastError, connectedAt }` (L141: `lastError: server.lastError,`). `grep -c lastError frontend/app/platform/page.tsx` -> `0`. `server.error` is `undefined` on every row, so the ternary is always false. There is no `frontend/app/platform/page.test.tsx` (the only frontend page tests are ask, audio, tasks, videos, ChatView, TaskDetail), so nothing exercises it.
confirmed.why_it_matters: A dropped or refused MCP server renders as `<id> — error` with the reason permanently invisible, on the one screen whose own docstring says 'Everything here reports degraded states explicitly rather than hiding them' (platform/page.tsx:16-18). backend/packages/mcp/src/client.ts:328-337 goes to some length to make `lastError` carry the real cause (e.g. `HTTP 401`, `ENOENT`) and notes it is deliberately readable by anyone with `project:read` — and no reader exists. The operator is left with a status word and told to go read boot logs, which is what ADR-074 built this screen to avoid.
confirmed.fix: Rename the field on `McpRow` to `lastError` and render `server.lastError`. The same page has three other declared-but-unrendered fields that should be checked against the route while there (`ModelRow.capabilities` is typed `string[]` but the route returns a capability object; `ToolRow.source` does not exist on the route, which returns `origin`).
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED by reading the code. frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:39-44 declares `McpRow` with `error?: string | null` and line 249 renders `{server.error ? {server.error} : null}`. The sole producer, backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:127-145, maps `ctx.mcp.status()` to `{ id, status, transport, toolCount, toolIds, refusedToolIds, lastError, connectedAt }` — line 141 `lastError: server.lastError` — with no `error` key. backend/packages/mcp/src/manager.ts:39-54 (`McpServerState`) likewise has `lastError` and no `error`, and `status()` (manager.ts:118) returns the states verbatim, so nothing renames it. `apiFetch` (frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts:102-127) returns the parsed JSON unchanged and the shape comes from an unchecked generic `apiFetch<{ servers: McpRow[] }>`, so the compiler never compares the two. `grep -rn "lastError" frontend/` hits only app/lib/api.ts:259 and app/videos/[id]/page.tsx:177 — zero in the platform page; `grep -rn "server\.error" frontend/` hits only platform/page.tsx:249. So `server.error` is undefined on every row and the ternary is permanently false. Untested: `ls frontend/app/platform/` shows only page.tsx, and the two e2e specs that visit /platform (auth-and-isolation.spec.ts:119-152, admin-boundary.spec.ts:105-131) assert Health text, the MOCK model cell, fs.read_file, dead-letter text and the Reconnect button only — never an MCP error string. Not already fixed: `grep -n "lastError" docs/` hits only docs/07_LONG_RUNNING_JOB_ARCHITECTURE.md; ADR-074 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1125) and ADR-123..ADR-143 do not address it, and `git diff` shows line 249 untouched by the in-flight ADR-144 reconnect work. Additional evidence the finding missed: platform.ts:137-139 comments that `refusedToolIds` is "Shown, not just logged", yet `grep -rn "refusedToolIds" frontend/app` returns nothing — a second dropped diagnostic with an explicit comment claiming it is displayed. The fix note's secondary claims also check out (registry.ts:13 types `capabilities` as the object `ProviderCapabilities`, not `string[]`; the route returns `origin`, not `source`) but those fields are never rendered, so they are informational. Severity lowered from P1 to P2: the defect is total within its render path, but non-blocking — the operator still sees the server id, its `failed`/`disconnected` status and a working Reconnect; what is lost is the cause string (`HTTP 401` vs `ENOENT`) that backend/packages/mcp/src/client.ts:320-337 deliberately constructs. That is degraded diagnosis against ADR-074's intent, not a broken capability.

confirmed.title: A cancelled image generation is rendered as "Generating…" forever — the client's status union omits `cancelled`, which ADR-122 made reachable
confirmed.evidence:
api.ts:187 `status: "pending" | "processing" | "succeeded" | "failed";` for `ImageGeneration`. The server has a fifth value: backend/packages/database/src/repositories/image-generation-repository.ts:6 `export type ImageGenerationStatus = "pending" | "processing" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled";`, written by backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:53 `updateStatus(projectId, generationId, "cancelled", ...)`. frontend/app/images/page.tsx:87-91 is `g.status === "succeeded" && g.resultAssetId ? :
{g.status === "failed" ? "Failed" : "Generating…"}
`, and the Cancel button is gated on `pending|processing` (L98), so it disappears. The tile therefore reads "Generating…" beside a `cancelled` StatusBadge, indefinitely. Same omission twice more, for statuses ADR-122/ADR-140 added server-side: api.ts:232 `VideoProject.status` omits `cancelled` (set by backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:351), api.ts:255 `VideoScene.status` omits `cancelled` (set at video-orchestration.ts:222). Contrast api.ts:74, where `AudioGeneration` does list `cancelled` and frontend/app/audio/page.tsx renders it correctly — so this is an inconsistency, not a convention.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The user presses Cancel, the worker honours it, and the screen keeps saying the work is still running. That is the opposite of what ADR-122 was for, and it is the one state where a user might reasonably conclude they are still being billed. Because the union is wrong rather than missing, TypeScript actively prevents the fix being noticed: `g.status === "cancelled"` is a compile error today.
confirmed.fix: Add `"cancelled"` to `ImageGeneration.status` (api.ts:187), `VideoProject.status` (api.ts:232) and `VideoScene.status` (api.ts:255), then branch on it in images/page.tsx:91 (and check videos/[id]/page.tsx's scene placeholder, which renders `{scene.status}` raw and is therefore already correct).
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED from the code, with the impact narrowed.

Verified: frontend/app/lib/api.ts:187 declares ImageGeneration.status as "pending"|"processing"|"succeeded"|"failed"; `grep -rn "cancelled" frontend/app/lib/api.ts` returns only line 74 (AudioGeneration), so ImageGeneration, VideoProject (L232) and VideoScene (L255) all omit it. The server value exists and is reachable: backend/packages/database/src/repositories/image-generation-repository.ts:6 includes "cancelled"; backend/src/routes/v1/images.ts:114 (POST /api/v1/images/:id/cancel) calls requestCancel (repo L126, gated on pending|processing); backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:52-56 sets status "cancelled" when cancelRequestedAt is present; repo list() (L152) has no status filter, so the row stays in the gallery. frontend/app/images/page.tsx:87-93 renders the else-branch placeholder as "Generating…" for any non-succeeded, non-failed status, and the Cancel button (L98) disappears — so a cancelled generation shows "Generating…" indefinitely. No ADR addresses it: docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-122 (L2022-2026) and ADR-140 (L2264-2270) only created the state server-side, and there is no images page test (`ls frontend/app/images/` -> page.tsx only).

Downgraded from P1 to P2 for three reasons the finding overstates:
1. The card is contradictory, not silent. images/page.tsx:97 renders StatusBadge, and frontend/app/lib/status-badge.tsx:2 puts "cancelled" in the DANGER set, so a red "cancelled" chip shows; L115 renders g.errorMessage, which the worker set to "Cancelled before generation started." The user gets two correct signals beside the wrong placeholder, so the "might conclude they are still being billed" argument does not hold as stated.
2. The video half has zero user-visible effect. frontend/app/videos/page.tsx:123-124 and frontend/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx:64,157,176 render status generically via StatusBadge (which takes `status: string`) or raw `{scene.status}`, so cancelled projects/scenes already display correctly. Those are type-accuracy nits only. (The finding also missed that VideoProject.status omits "planning", which video-project-repository.ts:6-13 lists as an in-flight status.)
3. Trigger is narrower than implied: image-generation.ts checks cancelRequestedAt only before the provider call, so "cancelled" is only reached when cancel lands while the job is queued (or on a pg-boss re-claim); Cancel pressed during `processing` settles succeeded/failed and never reaches this render path.

Real defect in a shipped capability, one code path, cosmetic/mislabelling effect, no billing, authorization, isolation or quota consequence -> P2. The proposed fix (add "cancelled" to api.ts:187 and branch at images/page.tsx:91) is correct.

confirmed.title: Switching project leaves /tasks and the chat sidebar showing the previous project's rows, and opening one 404s
confirmed.evidence:
frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx:63 `useEffect(refresh, []);` — empty deps, and no polling interval on this screen. frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx:32-36 `useEffect(() => { listConversations().then(...).catch(() => {}); }, [conversationId]);` — `conversationId` does not change when the project does.
The project switcher is rendered on every authenticated screen (frontend/app/lib/app-chrome.tsx:60-73, `onChange={(e) => selectProject(e.target.value)}`). Screens that handle it correctly all declare the dependency: memory/page.tsx:62 `[refresh, projectId]`, usage/page.tsx:50 `[load, projectId]`, platform/page.tsx:137-139 `[load, projectId]`.
Both listings are project-scoped server-side: `GET /api/v1/agent/tasks` -> `ctx.tasks.list(scopedProjectId(authCtx))` (backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:99-101) and `GET /api/v1/conversations` -> `ctx.conversations.list(...)` (backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:53-56). `GET /api/v1/agent/tasks/:id` and `/conversations/:id/messages` re-scope, so a click on a stale row is a `NotFoundError`.
(images/videos/audio/files self-heal because they poll every 2s and `apiFetch` re-reads `localStorage` per request; /tasks and /chat do not poll.)
confirmed.why_it_matters: After switching project, the Tasks screen shows another project's task list and the chat sidebar another project's conversations — the exact cross-tenant impression the scoping work exists to prevent, even though the click that follows fails closed with a 404. The user's only recovery is a hard reload, and nothing on screen says the list is stale. ChatView.tsx:36's `.catch(() => {})` additionally swallows a failed conversation list entirely, so the sidebar silently renders 'No conversations yet.' for an outage.
confirmed.fix: Take `projectId` from `useSession()` in both and put it in the effect's dependency array (`useEffect(refresh, [projectId])`, `[conversationId, projectId]`), matching memory/usage/platform. Replace ChatView.tsx:36's empty catch with a visible message.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED mechanics, DOWNGRADED severity (P1 -> P2) and the category is mislabelled.

Restated from the code myself:
- frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx:63 is literally `useEffect(refresh, []);` — empty deps. `refresh()` is the only caller of `listTasks()` besides `handleCreate`, and I grepped `setInterval` across frontend/app/tasks/ and frontend/app/chat/ -> zero hits, so there is no poll to self-heal.
- frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx:33-37 depends on `[conversationId]`, a route prop that does not change when the project does.
- frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx `selectProject` is only `setProjectId(next); setSelectedProjectId(next);`. I grepped `router.refresh|location.reload` across frontend/app/ -> zero hits, and `key={projectId}` -> only settings/page.tsx:86. So a project switch remounts nothing on these two screens.
- I grepped `useSession` in frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx and frontend/app/chat/: the only hit is tasks/page.tsx:173 inside `McpToolGate`, reading `user`. Neither top-level component subscribes to `projectId` at all.
- The comparison screens do it right: memory/page.tsx:61 `[refresh, projectId]`, usage/page.tsx:51 `[load, projectId]`, platform/page.tsx:163 `[load, projectId]`.
- frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts:116 confirms apiFetch re-reads `getSelectedProjectId()` per request, so the NEXT call would be scoped correctly — these screens just never make one.
- Backend scoping confirmed: backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:99-101 and backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:53-56 list by `scopedProjectId(authCtx)`; agent.ts:104-113 and chat.ts:58-68 re-scope the :id reads and throw NotFoundError, so a stale row click really does 404.
- docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-120..143: no ADR addresses this. Not already fixed.

Extra corroboration the finding missed: neither /tasks nor /chat is wrapped in `RequireSession` (grep shows it on agent, ask, memory, platform, settings, usage only). frontend/app/agent/task-detail-loader.tsx:16-20 states the exact rule these two screens break — "fetching before the session resolves would send a stale project from a previous login."

Why P2 and not P1:
1. The "tenant-scoping" / "cross-tenant impression" framing does not hold. `projects` in the switcher comes from `fetchSession()` -> `session.projects`, i.e. projects this same account may read. Every stale row is data the user is entitled to see. No isolation, quota or authz boundary is crossed, and the follow-up click fails CLOSED with a 404 from a correctly re-scoping route.
2. "The user's only recovery is a hard reload" is false. These are App Router page segments with no `key` pinning them; any client-side navigation away and back unmounts and remounts the component, re-running the effect. Tasks -> Chat -> Tasks recovers without a reload.

What genuinely survives, and is worth fixing: the global project switcher (app-chrome.tsx:60-73, rendered on every authenticated screen) is inert on two of the app's most-used screens — the list silently shows the previous project's rows with nothing on screen saying so, and every row click errors. Separately real: ChatView.tsx:36's `.catch(() => {})` swallows a failed `listConversations()` entirely, so an API outage renders the sidebar's "No conversations yet." empty state (line 134) — a false negative of the same class ADR-123 was written about. Both are real correctness defects in shipped screens, but non-blocking, fail-closed and self-recovering on navigation.

confirmed.title: Self-service account and data deletion (NFR-008 / ADR-102) has no control anywhere in the app
confirmed.evidence:
The route exists and is documented: docs/API.md:114 `| DELETE | /api/v1/auth/account | session only · authentication only | 5 / 15 minutes per user |`, implemented at backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:243ff with the comment 'It is self-service rather than an operator ticket because a privacy requirement satisfied only by asking someone else is not satisfied.'
Absence proven: `grep -rn 'method: "DELETE"' frontend/app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` returns exactly three lines — api.ts:367 (api-keys), api.ts:383 (sessions), api.ts:395 (memory). `grep -rn 'auth/account' frontend` returns nothing. `grep -rni 'delete.*account' frontend/app` returns one hit, settings/page.tsx:107, which is a comment saying a user with a compromised password 'had nothing to do about it but delete the account'.
`docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md` records related deletion caveats (line 53, started jobs) but nowhere records that deletion has no UI, so this is not an accepted limitation.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The Settings screen is the account screen — it has Password, Sessions, Projects, API keys and even a pointer to Memory — and the one action the route's own docstring insists must not require asking someone else is the one action it does not offer. The route also went to real trouble (session-only credential, current password, typed confirmation, per-user rate limit) to be safe for a human to drive, and no human can reach it from the product. Its own comment is the claim the code does not honour.
confirmed.fix: Add a danger-zone card to frontend/app/settings/page.tsx that posts the three fields the route requires and reports the response's `deleted`/`storageObjectsNotRemoved` counts, then signs out. `frontend/e2e/account-security.spec.ts` already drives the neighbouring password journey and is the natural place to cover it.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and the unreachability argument is stronger than the finding made it. backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:243 registers DELETE /api/v1/auth/account and refuses any credential that is not an interactive session (`if (request.auth?.method !== "session") throw new PermissionError(...)`); cookie-authenticated mutations also require the x-csrf-token header (backend/src/plugins/auth.ts:120-124). So the ONLY client that can ever authenticate to this route is the browser app — and the browser app never calls it. Absence proven by greps I ran: `grep -rn "auth/account" frontend --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` exits 1 with no hits; `grep -rn "DELETE_ACCOUNT_CONFIRMATION" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx .` (repo minus node_modules) returns only shared/src/auth.ts:149,152 and shared/dist/auth.d.ts:89, i.e. the exported confirmation literal has zero frontend consumers; `grep -rn 'method: "DELETE"' frontend` returns exactly three lines, all frontend/app/lib/api.ts (367 revokeApiKey, 383 revokeSession, 395 deleteMemory); `find frontend -name "*.tsx" -not -path "frontend/app/*"` is empty, so no component lives outside app/. frontend/app/settings/page.tsx is the account screen (Password, Sessions, Projects, API keys, Memory link) with no danger zone — its only "delete the account" string is the ADR-127 docstring at line 107 describing the prior state. No CLI exists (no "bin" in package.json, no cli.ts) and the docs themselves say "No operator-initiated deletion".

I specifically tried to kill this finding two ways and could not. (1) ADRs: ADR-102 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1676) and its ADR-107/108/109 amendments are entirely backend-side (per-project ownership, workspaces, queued jobs, audit scrubbing, session-only, per-user rate limit). Nothing in ADR-123..143 adds a control; ADR-127 built the neighbouring password card and its own docstring names account deletion as the thing users were reduced to. (2) Accepted-limitation check: the `no` column in docs/FINAL_PROJECT_AUDIT.md:101 and docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md:63 is Production Verified (header `| Dimension | I | T | RV | PV | Blocked | Remaining |`), NOT a UI column; the Remaining cells list only operator-initiated deletion and export-before-delete, and docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md:53 records only the started-jobs caveat. So the gap is nowhere accepted.

Severity P1 is right. NFR-008 (docs/01_REQUIREMENTS.md:85) is a P1 privacy requirement — "User can delete their account and associated data" — and docs/29_FEATURE_MATRIX.md row 39 marks it DONE while docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md marks it VERIFIED, so this is also a doc/comment claim the product does not honour (the route's own comment: "a privacy requirement satisfied only by asking someone else is not satisfied"). Not P0: the deletion machinery is correct and covered by 23 tests, nothing is exploitable, and a technically sophisticated user could still hand-drive it from devtools using the CSRF cookie — the capability is unreachable as a product feature, not broken.

Two small corrections to the finding as written: the request body has TWO fields (password, confirm: "DELETE MY ACCOUNT" — shared/src/auth.ts:150-152), not the "three fields" its fix section says (three guards, one of which is the session); and the strongest evidence is the orphaned DELETE_ACCOUNT_CONFIRMATION constant, which the finding did not cite.

confirmed.title: Ingested documents can never be deleted from the interface — `DELETE /api/v1/files/:id` has no client function and no control
confirmed.evidence:
Route: docs/API.md:142 `| DELETE | /api/v1/files/:id | session or API key · files:write |`, backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:246-258, with a docstring explaining that the chunk delete is 'the half a user would actually notice… leaving those behind would mean a "deleted" document kept being quoted back into answers'.
Absence proven: the only `/api/v1/files/` client in frontend/app/lib/api.ts is `getFile` at line 295 (a GET); there is no `deleteFile`, and `grep -rn 'method: "DELETE"' frontend/app` lists only api-keys, sessions and memory. frontend/app/files/page.tsx:96-119 renders each document as a non-interactive `<div className="card card-row">` with a filename, scan badge and status badge — no button.
confirmed.why_it_matters: A user can upload a document, have it embedded and indexed, and then has no way to take it back out: every subsequent /ask answer can keep quoting it. That is the asymmetry the Memory screen was built to close for memory items (each row there has a Forget button, memory/page.tsx:158-166) and it is still open for documents, which are the larger and more sensitive store. Removal is the remedy for an upload made in error, and it currently requires curl.
confirmed.fix: Add `deleteFile = (id) => request<{ok:true}>(`/api/v1/files/${id}`, { method: "DELETE" })` to api.ts and a Remove button per row in files/page.tsx, mirroring the Forget button in memory/page.tsx (busy state + `refresh()` + error line).
confirmed.verdict: Verified from the code, not the write-up. backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:246-255 registers DELETE /api/v1/files/:id (files:write) and it is real: ctx.documentChunks.deleteByDocument (backend/packages/database/src/repositories/document-chunk-repository.ts:220) then ctx.documents.softDelete (document-repository.ts:195), with registerRagRoutes wired at backend/src/server.ts:209 and the row published at docs/API.md:142. The client side is absent: `grep -rn "/api/v1/files" frontend/` yields only listFiles (api.ts:291), ingestFile (293, POST), getFile (295, GET) and uploadFile (315, POST upload) — no deleteFile; `grep -rn 'method: "DELETE"' frontend/` yields exactly three hits, all non-file (revokeApiKey 367, revokeSession 383, deleteMemory 395). I read frontend/app/files/page.tsx in full: the document list is lines 102-123 (the finding's line 96 is off — that is the ingest form) and renders a non-interactive div per document with filename, scan text and StatusBadge; the page's only buttons are Upload (81) and Ingest (93). frontend/app/memory/page.tsx does carry the per-row Forget button, so the asymmetry is as described. No ADR addresses it: `grep -n "^## ADR-1[3-4][0-9]" docs/26_DECISIONS.md` lists ADR-130..143 and none concerns document removal or the Files screen's controls (ADR-143 is the inverse shape). Extra support the finding missed: the route has no backend test either — `grep -rn 'method: "DELETE"' backend/src` shows rag.test.ts:241 exercises only DELETE /api/v1/memory/:id. Impact holds with one softening: a user can mint an API key from /settings rather than literally needing curl, but either way removal is impossible from the product's own UI while upload is UI-only, so an uploaded document keeps being retrievable by /ask and by answer_from_documents. Severity stays P2: a real gap in a shipped screen, not exploitable, no requirement violated (FR-031 is upload+ask; FR-032 is memory-only and is honoured), and the capability is reachable through the documented API — so not P1.

confirmed.title: Every tool call writes an audit row (ADR-139) and nothing in the product can read one — `GET /api/v1/audit` has no consumer
confirmed.evidence:
`app.get("/api/v1/audit", ...)` at backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:376-379 (`project:admin`, `ctx.auth.listAudit(authCtx)` — backend/packages/security/src/auth-service.ts:945). Documented at docs/API.md:108.
Absence proven: `grep -rni "audit" frontend/app --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts"` returns only prose — ChatView.tsx:75, ChatView.test.tsx:148, auth-client.test.ts:199, chat-stream.test.ts:5, tasks/page.tsx:26, tasks/page.test.tsx:12, usage/page.tsx:11 — every hit is a comment about a past code audit. No call, no screen, no nav entry (frontend/app/lib/app-chrome.tsx:7-21 lists eleven links; none is an audit or activity view).
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-139's decision line is 'Every tool call leaves a durable record… including the refusals', and ADR-127/ADR-102 add auth events to the same table. The records are written, scoped and queryable, and the product has no way to answer 'what did the agent actually do in my project, and what was it refused?' for the project admin the route is scoped to. A durable record no one can read is the same shape as the MCP Enable button before ADR-136: a governance feature reachable only from a terminal.
confirmed.fix: Either add an Activity/Audit section to the Platform screen behind the project-admin role (the screen already loads five listings in one `Promise.allSettled`), or record in docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md that the audit trail is deliberately API-only.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED from the code. backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:376-379 defines GET /api/v1/audit behind requireProject(..., "project:admin") returning ctx.auth.listAudit(authCtx); listAudit is backend/packages/security/src/auth-service.ts:945-952 (project-scoped select from audit_log, desc, limit min(n,500)). Greps I ran: `grep -rn "api/v1/audit" . --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.md --include=*.json --include=*.sh --include=*.py` (node_modules excluded) returns exactly three hits — the route, docs/API.md:104/108, and gaps-batch-a.json (a prior audit's findings file committed at af08771). `grep -rn "listAudit"` (dist excluded) returns the route plus two unit tests (auth-service.test.ts:286,305) and nothing else; `grep -rn "auditLog"` across backend src shows the only other touch is the deletion scrubber (account-deletion.ts:157-159), so listAudit is the single read path in the whole system. frontend/app/lib/app-chrome.tsx:7-23 lists eleven nav links with no audit/activity entry, and frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:93-101 fetches six endpoints (models, tools, mcp, jobs, jobs/dead-letter, admin/health) — audit is not one. Not already fixed: no ADR in 123-143 addresses it; ADR-074 (26_DECISIONS.md:1125) built /platform over the ADR-066 endpoints for precisely this "nothing ever called them" reason and excluded audit; docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md contains no acceptance that the trail is API-only, and no doc claims an audit screen exists (so nothing is falsified — it is a pure no-consumer gap, not a broken claim). Two adjustments. (1) The impact is slightly over-stated: frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx:157,245,324 does render tool_call/tool_result/verification entries for an agent run from the run's own transition log, so per-run agent activity IS visible in the product. What genuinely has no surface is the project-wide cross-run trail ToolRegistry.call writes under ADR-139 (including the refusals and the chat/MCP paths) and the auth events from ADR-127/ADR-102 — logins, password changes, key revocations, deletions. (2) This is a repeat of a prior audit's unfixed item, gaps-batch-a.json:111 ("The audit log and admin metrics/stats have no screen", also P2), whose siblings in that same file were fixed while this one was not; /api/v1/admin/metrics and /api/v1/admin/stats are likewise still consumer-less. Severity P2 is correct as filed: nothing is broken, no isolation/quota/authorization is bypassed, the rows are written and queryable, and a project admin with a session or API key can still reach them — it is a governance capability with no in-product reader, not a defect in a shipped user journey.

confirmed.title: The Platform screen offers Replay to every project member, but the replay route requires `project:write`
confirmed.evidence:
The dead-letter table and its Replay button are rendered unconditionally for anyone who can load the screen. The listing that populates it needs only `project:read` — docs/API.md:161 `GET /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter … project:read` — while the button's target needs more: docs/API.md:162 `POST /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/:queue/:id/replay … project:write` (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:212-219, `requireProject(request, ctx.auth, "project:write")`). `shared/src/auth.ts:49` shows `viewer` holds `project:read` and not `project:write`, and backend/src/routes/api-contract.test.ts:122-143 asserts a viewer gets a 403 naming the permission.
The replay handler is frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:141-153; it renders the failure into the page-level `error` banner, which is better than TaskDetail — but the button is still offered to a user who can never use it.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Same shape ADR-143 closed one screen earlier: a control offered to someone the backend refuses. Here it is worse than a wasted click — Replay re-runs paid provider work, so a viewer is being shown a spend action their role exists to withhold, and the only feedback is a permission error they cannot act on. The neighbouring Jobs table has the inverse gap: `POST /api/v1/jobs/:queue/:id/cancel` exists (docs/API.md:160) and has no control at all, so an operator who can see a stuck job cannot stop it (`grep -rn 'jobs/.*cancel' frontend` returns nothing).
confirmed.fix: Resolve the caller's role from `useSession().projects.find(p => p.id === projectId)?.role` and render Replay only for `editor`/`admin`, telling a viewer whose decision it is — the fallback pattern the new `SystemAdminOnly` component (session-context.tsx:185) already provides for the admin case. Add the missing Cancel control to the Jobs table while there.
confirmed.verdict:
Restated from the code: frontend/app/platform/page.tsx renders the dead-lettered work table and a per-row Replay button with no role guard (button at lines 357-364, handler `replay` at 165-177 — the finding's line 141 is stale, shifted by the newly added ADR-144 reconnect block). The listing that populates the table needs only `project:read` (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:196), but the button's target requires more: platform.ts:218 `await requireProject(request, ctx.auth, "project:write")`, documented at docs/API.md:162. shared/src/auth.ts defines `const VIEWER: Permission[] = ["project:read","files:read","memory:read","usage:read"]` — no `project:write` — and viewers are really assignable via `POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members` (backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:216), exercised with role "viewer" in backend/packages/security/src/auth-service.test.ts:206. The screen is reachable by any member: frontend/app/lib/app-chrome.tsx:21 lists /platform in NAV_LINKS unconditionally and the page is wrapped only in RequireSession. So a viewer loads the page, sees rows, and is offered a button that can only ever return 403 naming `project:write`.

Not already fixed. ADR-143 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2303) closed the Enable button on the Tasks screen only. The uncommitted ADR-144 machinery — SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES in frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx:164-170 and the source-walking test session-context.admin.test.tsx — checks only system-admin routes; replay is correctly not one of them, so nothing in that new guard covers this. No ADR mentions gating Replay by project role (grep for "Replay" in docs/26_DECISIONS.md hits ADR-072, ADR-074, ADR-119, ADR-127, ADR-130 — all backend behaviour, none about who is offered the control).

Two corrections. (1) Impact is overstated: the backend refuses, so no paid work runs and no quota is spent — it is a wasted click plus a permission error, not a spend or authorization bypass. The page-level `error` banner does surface the backend's message, so the user is at least told why. (2) Wider context the finding misses, which argues for P2 rather than higher: `grep -rn "editor\|viewer" frontend/app --include=*.tsx` returns nothing and no project-role gating component exists anywhere, so the frontend gates nothing on project role at all — Chat send, agent run, image/audio generate are offered to viewers on the same terms. Replay is one instance of a systemic affordance gap, not a singular defect.

The secondary observation is also confirmed: `grep -rn "cancel" frontend/app` finds callers for agent tasks, audio, images and videos, but none for `/api/v1/jobs/:queue/:id/cancel` (platform.ts:181, docs/API.md:160) — that route has no frontend caller, so the Jobs table shows a stuck job with no way to stop it. The proposed fix is feasible as written: `ProjectSummary.role` exists (frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts:29) and is already rendered at frontend/app/settings/page.tsx:267.

P2 is right: real, in shipped code, same class the tree already decided was worth closing one screen earlier, but not exploitable and not a broken core capability.

confirmed.title: `refusedToolIds` is documented as "Shown, not just logged" and no screen shows it
confirmed.evidence:
backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:136-140: '// Tools this server offered and was refused because the id was already taken. Shown,\n// not just logged: on a remote server that is what a name-squatting attempt looks\n// like, and a boot-time log line is not where anyone goes looking for it.' followed by `refusedToolIds: server.refusedToolIds,`.
Absence proven: `grep -rn refusedToolIds frontend` returns nothing — the field is not on `McpRow` (frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:38-43) and not rendered in the MCP list (L234-255). The only screen that reads `/api/v1/mcp` is this one.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The comment states a security-visibility decision as a fact about the system, and the only consumer of the endpoint drops the field. A remote MCP server trying to squat an existing tool id produces a signal that the route deliberately surfaces to the API and that no operator will ever see — which is precisely the 'a boot-time log line is not where anyone goes looking for it' failure the comment says it avoids. Paired with the `lastError` mismatch above, the MCP section shows a status word and nothing else.
confirmed.fix: Add `refusedToolIds?: string[]` to `McpRow` and render it beside `lastError`, or soften the comment to say the field is exposed for a future consumer.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed against the code, not the name. backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:137-140 emits `refusedToolIds` under a comment asserting it is "Shown, not just logged ... a boot-time log line is not where anyone goes looking for it." The value is real: backend/packages/mcp/src/client.ts:141-149 and :194 push an id whenever a server offers one that is already registered. The intent is stated twice more without the route comment's ambiguity — backend/packages/mcp/src/manager.ts:46-48 ("An operator needs to see these ... on a remote server it is the shape a name-squatting attempt takes") and docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-083 line 1321 ("both the transport and any refused ids are reported on /api/v1/mcp so an operator can see what a server tried to claim"). The only consumer drops it: frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:39-44 declares McpRow as {id, status, toolCount?, error?} and :245-268 renders id, status, tool count, server.error and the Reconnect button. Absence proven: ripgrep for /refused|Refused/i over frontend/ returns only unrelated auth/e2e comments, zero `refusedToolIds`; `grep -rn refusedToolIds --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.md .` (minus node_modules) hits only backend/packages/mcp/** and platform.ts:140; the sole caller of GET /api/v1/mcp is platform/page.tsx:101. Not already fixed: ADR-143 and ADR-144 both edit platform/page.tsx but I read ADR-144's text and the current file — it added only the SystemAdminOnly-guarded Reconnect control and left McpRow untouched. So the refusal signal reaches a human only via the boot-time WARN (client.ts:143, manager.ts:215 refused_tools) — the exact surface the comment disclaims — or an authenticated curl. Two corrections. (1) The route comment alone is defensible read narrowly as "shown in the API response"; manager.ts:46 and ADR-083 are the citations that actually make the claim unhonoured, and the finding should lean on those. (2) Impact is observability only, not exploitability: the collision IS refused (client.ts:141, the tool is never registered) and MCP tools arrive enabled:false, so no squat succeeds — what is lost is any chance of noticing one was attempted. The finding does not overclaim this, so P2 is right: real, a stated security-visibility decision the shipped UI does not deliver, but no broken control and nothing exploitable. The finding slightly understates scope — `transport` is dropped by the same McpRow despite its own "so an operator can see which wire" comment (manager.ts:34), and the sibling lastError/error name mismatch leaves server.error permanently undefined.

confirmed.title: The new ADR-144 admin-gate test is file-granular and its "can this fail" case re-implements the check instead of running it
confirmed.evidence:
Uncommitted working-tree addition (`git status --porcelain` shows `?? frontend/app/lib/session-context.admin.test.tsx` alongside modified api.ts, session-context.tsx, platform/page.tsx, tasks/page.tsx).
(1) Granularity: the check at L50-66 is `if (used.length === 0) continue; if (!/SystemAdminOnly/.test(source)) offenders.push(...)` — it asserts only that the FILE containing an admin-only call also contains the string `SystemAdminOnly` somewhere. frontend/app/platform/page.tsx and frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx now each contain that string, so any further admin-only control added to either file passes unexamined, including one placed outside the guard or mentioned only in a comment.
(2) The self-test at L92-105 ('fails when a control is added without the guard') does not call anything from the module under test: it declares a local template string `ungated`, then re-runs the same two expressions inline — `SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_CLIENTS.filter(fn => new RegExp(...).test(ungated))` and `/SystemAdminOnly/.test(ungated)`. Both operands are literals in the test file. No change to any screen in frontend/app can make it fail.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-144's stated value is that this walks the whole app so it 'covers screens nobody thought to write a test for'. What it actually enforces is one string per file, and the case written to prove the check can fail proves only that a regex matches a string the test wrote itself — the mutation is applied to the fixture, not to the checker. The first defect the check was built for (ADR-136's Enable button) lived in tasks/page.tsx, which now contains `SystemAdminOnly` for one control; a second ungated control in that same file would not be caught.
confirmed.fix: Extract the per-file logic into an exported function that returns offenders for a given source string, then have the 'can this fail' case call that function on the `ungated` fixture and assert it reports the offender. For granularity, scope the guard check to the component or JSX subtree containing the call (or require each admin-only call site to be lexically inside `<SystemAdminOnly>`), not the file.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by two mutations, each run against the real suite; frontend/ restored clean afterwards.

(2) The "can this fail" case does not exercise the checker — proven. I replaced the guard condition at frontend/app/lib/session-context.admin.test.tsx:59 (`if (!/SystemAdminOnly/.test(source)) {`) with `if (false) {`, fully disabling enforcement. All 5 tests still passed, including the one named "fails when a control is added without the guard". That case (L93-105) re-declares the regex and the /SystemAdminOnly/ test inline against a local template literal; `expect(/SystemAdminOnly/.test(ungated)).toBe(false)` is tautological against a string written 4 lines above. The mutation is applied to the fixture, never to the checker.

(1) File granularity — proven. I appended a second, fully ungated control to frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx (`export function SneakyUngatedControl({id}) { return <button onClick={() => void setToolEnabled(id, true)}>Enable (ungated)</button>; }`). All 5 tests stayed green, because that file already contains SystemAdminOnly at L235/L244 for a different control. This is the exact ADR-136 defect shape re-introduced in the exact file ADR-136's defect lived in. The check at L53-62 is `if (used.length === 0) continue; if (!/SystemAdminOnly/.test(source))` — one string per file, satisfiable by a bare import or a comment.

Doc claim not honoured: the test's own header (L17-19) says an admin-only call "must render it INSIDE SystemAdminOnly" and ADR-144 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2314) says it "fails if one is rendered outside SystemAdminOnly". Lexical containment is never checked, only co-occurrence in the same file.

CORRECTIONS to the finding (do not change the verdict):
- Its evidence header claims an uncommitted `?? frontend/app/lib/session-context.admin.test.tsx`. False: `git ls-files` shows it tracked, `git log -1 --` shows it committed in 9fea063 (ADR-144), and `git status --porcelain` was empty at session start.
- "Both operands are literals in the test file" is imprecise: SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_CLIENTS is imported from ./session-context, so `expect(used).toContain("setToolEnabled")` can fail if that constant changes. The operative claim — no change to any screen or to the checker can make it fail — holds.
- It understates residual value: I also created frontend/app/newscreen-tmp.tsx with an ungated setToolEnabled call and the check DID fail (1 failed | 4 passed). The walker is not vacuous for a brand-new screen; what escapes is a second control in an already-guarded file, a guard satisfied by an import/comment, and any mutation to the checker itself.

Severity P2 is correct, not higher. The backend is the real boundary (requireSystemAdmin / PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS in backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts) and session-context.tsx:182 states the component "is deliberately not a security control". frontend/e2e/admin-boundary.spec.ts exists and drives the unmocked boundary from both sides. Shipped state is currently correct: `grep -rn "setToolEnabled\|reconnectMcpServer" frontend/app --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts | grep -v "\.test\."` returns exactly two call sites (tasks/page.tsx:190, platform/page.tsx:150), each inside the guard. No user is over-privileged today; this is a defect in the safety net, demonstrated by a mutation that survives a green suite.

confirmed.title: AgentEngine.cancel() queues behind the per-task lock the run itself holds, so Cancel can never stop a run in flight — it returns 200 OK having done nothing
confirmed.evidence: engine.ts:320 `async cancel(taskId, actor) { await this.runExclusive(taskId, async () => { ... this.inFlight.get(node.id)?.abort(...) ...` — the abort is INSIDE the mutex. runExclusive (engine.ts:1433) is strictly FIFO: `const prior = this.locks.get(taskId) ?? Promise.resolve(); const next = prior.then(fn, fn);`. Every node execution runs inside that same mutex: createAndStart (engine.ts:249) does `this.runExclusive(task.id, () => this.planAndExecute(...))`, planAndExecute ends `await this.tick(taskId)` (engine.ts:284), and tick does `await Promise.all(ready.map((node) => this.executeNode(task, node, byId)))` (engine.ts:424), which for an autonomous task awaits executeReasoningNode for the whole run (planner.ts:112 sets `timeoutMs: 10 * 60_000`). Contrast failTimedOutNodes (engine.ts:1340), which deliberately calls `this.inFlight.get(node.id)?.abort(...)` BEFORE `runExclusive` — the sweep path got this right and cancel() did not. By the time cancel's callback runs, `executeReasoningNode`'s `finally { this.inFlight.delete(node.id) }` has already cleared the entry, and the first line of the callback `if (!task || isTerminalTask(task.state)) return;` sees COMPLETED/FAILED and returns. The route (backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:201 `await ctx.engine.cancel(...); return { ok: true };`) therefore blocks for the remainder of the run and then answers `{ok:true}`. The UI offers the button for every non-terminal task: frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx:51 `async function handleCancel() { await cancelTask(taskId); }` rendered at :67 under `{!TERMINAL_STATES.has(task.state) && <button className="btn btn-danger">Cancel</button>}`. Absence of coverage proven: `grep -rn "\.cancel(" --include=*.test.ts backend/` returns exactly one hit, engine.test.ts:330, and that test (engine.test.ts:324-335) cancels a `delete_sandbox_file` task already parked at WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL — a state in which executeNodeInSpan has already returned and the lock is free, so it cannot exercise an in-flight run.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The stop control on the platform's flagship autonomous agent is inert. A user who presses Cancel on a run that is writing files, running commands and streaming tokens gets a success response while the agent runs to completion — the model keeps generating and billing (the exact harm ADR-119/ADR-140 closed at the router and socket layers, re-opened one layer up), and every remaining tool side effect still lands. The comment on the very line that is dead says the opposite: "Stop the work, not just the bookkeeping: without this a cancelled node's tool call would keep running to completion and only its row would say otherwise." Secondarily, POST /api/v1/agent/tasks/:id/cancel holds an HTTP connection open for up to the node's 10-minute timeout.
confirmed.fix: Abort outside the mutex, the way failTimedOutNodes already does: read the task and its non-terminal nodes, call `this.inFlight.get(node.id)?.abort(...)` for each before entering runExclusive, and only then take the lock to write the `cancelled` rows and the task transition. Add an engine-level test that starts an autonomous run whose scripted provider blocks, calls cancel() while the node is `waiting_model`, and asserts the node reaches `cancelled` (not `completed`) and that the tool the model was about to call never ran.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by reading the code; every cited line matches. engine.ts:320 `cancel()` puts `this.inFlight.get(node.id)?.abort(...)` (line 329) INSIDE `runExclusive`. runExclusive (engine.ts:1433) is strictly FIFO with no preemption: `const prior = this.locks.get(taskId) ?? Promise.resolve(); const next = prior.then(fn, fn);`. The run holds that same per-task lock for its entire duration — createAndStart (engine.ts:246) wraps `planAndExecute` in it, planAndExecute ends `await this.tick(taskId)` (engine.ts:284), tick awaits `Promise.all(ready.map(node => this.executeNode(...)))` (engine.ts:424) and re-ticks until terminal (engine.ts:433), and executeReasoningNode is fully awaited with planner.ts:111 `timeoutMs: 10 * 60_000`. I reproduced the exact semantics in a standalone script replicating runExclusive plus an in-flight abort: the cancel call blocked 253ms for the simulated run, its callback found the task already terminal and returned having done nothing, and the work completed (toolRan = true). By then `finally { this.inFlight.delete(node.id) }` (engine.ts:978) has cleared the entry, so `?.abort` is a no-op on undefined, and the route (backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:201) returns `{ ok: true }` after blocking for the rest of the run.

The contrast the finding draws is real and deliberate: failTimedOutNodes (engine.ts:1340) aborts BEFORE entering runExclusive, with a comment explaining why. The abort machinery is otherwise fully wired, which makes this purely a lock-ordering defect: controller.signal reaches streamChat (engine.ts:787) and runReasoningLoop checks `options.signal?.aborted` per iteration (reasoning-loop.ts:128) and per stream event (:147, :191), returning finish("cancelled") — an abort delivered outside the mutex would stop the run within one token.

Coverage absence verified: `grep -rn "\.cancel(" --include=*.test.ts backend/` returns exactly one hit, engine.test.ts:330, and that test cancels a task parked at WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL, where executeNodeInSpan has returned and tick short-circuits on its own WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL guard (engine.ts:342) — the lock is free, so it cannot exercise an in-flight run. `grep -rln cancel frontend/e2e/` returns nothing. UI confirmed at frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx:51 and :67 (button shown for every non-terminal state).

No ADR fixes it: ADR-119 and ADR-140 are the ModelRouter/parseSseStream and video-project layers; ADR-122 is images/videos. ADR-064 (26_DECISIONS.md:979) states the opposite of the code — it unified the two agent paths so that "a human can approve, a run can be cancelled, ceilings hold" would hold on the single path, and ADR-119 reasons from "a cancelled agent node does the same", a premise the engine does not deliver. So this is also a doc/comment claim the code does not honour.

Two corrections, neither refuting it: (1) cancel is not inert in EVERY state — a run parked at WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL or in a `retrying` backoff frees the lock, so cancel lands there, just after the in-flight turn already completed; it is inert 100% of the time against work actually in flight, which is the only case the button exists for. (2) The same defect hits tool_call nodes (engine.ts:561-578), not just autonomous runs — an approved destructive tool call cannot be stopped either.

Severity kept at P0 under the stated rubric ("a core capability broken"): the stop control on the flagship autonomous agent does nothing while the agent runs, answers 200 OK, lets the model keep generating and billing, lets every remaining tool side effect land, and holds the HTTP connection open for up to the node's 10-minute timeout.

confirmed.title: Crash recovery re-runs a human-approved tool call: a reasoning node resumed from `waiting_model` still carries its `pendingCall`, and the resume path executes it with no approval gate
confirmed.evidence: resumeAll (engine.ts:1371): `if (node.status === "waiting_model") { await this.updateNode(node, { status: "pending", startedAt: null }, "system:crash-recovery"); }` — this branch does not distinguish `model_call` from `reasoning`. The re-dispatched reasoning node reaches executeReasoningNode, which reads `const resumed = readResumeState(node.output)` (engine.ts:627) and then, at engine.ts:678-685, `const approvedCall = resumed?.pendingCall; if (approvedCall) { const outcome = await this.deps.toolRegistry.call(approvedCall.name, approvedCall.arguments, {...}) }` — `toolRegistry.call`, never `approvalFor`. The resume state is still on the row: the approval park writes `output: { resume: {transcript}, pendingCall, pendingCalls, reason }` (engine.ts:930-940) and nothing clears it until `verifyAndAdvance` overwrites `output` on success; `handleNodeFailure` (engine.ts:1219) patches only status/attemptCount/errorMessage/failureClass/startedAt/nextAttemptAt, and PgTaskNodeRepository.update (backend/packages/database/src/repositories/task-node-repository.ts:115-137) only writes keys present in the patch, so `output` survives. `executeNodeInSpan` skips the gate on re-dispatch because `if (!node.approvedAt)` (engine.ts:465) is false — approve() set it. The engine's own policy for the equivalent tool_call case is the opposite: resumeAll's `waiting_tool` branch routes a non-read_only tool to `needs_reconciliation` and PAUSEs the task with "Non-atomic mutating call was in flight at crash time — outcome unknown. Never auto-retry (docs/11 §4.3, docs/10 §3.3)". `engine.resumeAll()` is wired at backend/src/index.ts:1295. Absence of coverage proven: the only crash-recovery test touching `waiting_model` is engine.test.ts:394, which sets an `echo_chat` model_call node; ADR-025's own summary (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:486) enumerates the three covered branches — "auto-resume (model call), no-auto-retry-surface-for-reconciliation (mutating tool call), and replan-from-scratch" — with no reasoning-node case.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Only tools at `always`/`first_use`/`risk_threshold` reach this path, i.e. destructive, financial and write_external tools — fs.delete_file and any MCP tool whose name matches /delete|remove|drop/ (backend/packages/mcp/src/client.ts:421). A process restart between the human's approval and the run's completion silently performs the irreversible action a second time, with no human asked. The same branch also restarts a non-approved autonomous run from its goal with `output` null, redoing every mutating tool call it had already made, while the deterministic tool_call path deliberately refuses to do exactly that.
confirmed.fix: In resumeAll, branch `waiting_model` on `node.kind`: for a `reasoning` node carrying `output.pendingCall`, treat it like the `waiting_tool` destructive case — `needs_reconciliation` + PAUSED — or clear `pendingCall`/`pendingCalls` so the resumed run re-enters the approval gate instead of executing. Separately, clear the resume state from `output` the moment the approved call returns, so a later failure cannot replay it.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED — I can restate the defect from the code. resumeAll (backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:1371) promotes every `waiting_model` node to `pending` with no test on node.kind, and waiting_model is in IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES (backend/packages/database/src/repositories/task-node-repository.ts:81). A `reasoning` node sits in `waiting_model` for its entire multi-turn run: executeReasoningNode writes that status at engine.ts:656 BEFORE executing the human-approved call at engine.ts:678-685, and keeps it until verifyAndAdvance.
