confirmed.title: document.ingest double-charges embedding spend on a duplicate delivery: the idempotency key contains a version the successful pass itself bumps
confirmed.evidence: backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:210-216 — `await deps.embeddingMeter?.record(document.projectId, chunks, { ... idempotencyKey: `embedding:ingest:${document.id}:${document.version}` })` under the comment "Keyed on the document AND its ingest generation: a retry of the same version must not double-charge". Twenty lines later, :228-231 — the SAME successful pass calls `replaceForDocument(..., { status: "ready", bumpVersion: true })`, and backend/packages/database/src/repositories/document-chunk-repository.ts:212 executes `version: sql`${documents.version} + 1``. backend/packages/database/src/schema/index.ts:369 — `version: integer("version").notNull().default(1)`. The worker re-reads the row on every attempt: backend/src/index.ts:771 `const document = await documents.get(projectId, documentId);` then :777 `processDocumentIngestion(..., document)`. `grep -n "status ===\|status !==" backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts` returns NOTHING — no terminal-state guard.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Pass 1 records key `...:1` and leaves version 2. Any duplicate delivery of the same job (stale-lock re-claim, or a worker killed after the handler resolved but before pg-boss wrote the completion) reads version 2, re-embeds every chunk, and writes key `...:2` — a DIFFERENT key, so the ledger's `onConflictDoNothing` does not deduplicate it. The project is charged a second time for one ingestion, and `embeddingMeter.check` consumes the budget twice as well. The key protects only a retry of a pass that failed BEFORE `replaceForDocument` — the opposite of what ADR-131 and the comment claim. Ingestion is described in that same ADR as "by far the largest" embedding spend in the platform, so this is the most expensive place to get it wrong.
confirmed.fix: Key the charge on something the pass does not mutate — the job id, or the version READ AT ENTRY captured before `replaceForDocument` bumps it (e.g. `const ingestGeneration = document.version;` at the top and use it in the key), and add a guard that returns early when `document.status === "ready"` and its chunks already match this generation.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by reading the code, with two framing corrections and a severity downgrade.

Verified mechanism: backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:210-215 keys the embedding charge on `embedding:ingest:${document.id}:${document.version}` using the row the worker read at entry (backend/src/index.ts:775-778). The same successful pass then calls replaceForDocument(..., {status:"ready", bumpVersion:true}) at ingest.ts:225-231, and document-chunk-repository.ts:209 executes `version: sql`${documents.version} + 1`` inside that transaction. The project's own test proves the mutation: rag.integration.test.ts:113 asserts version===2 after one pass, :199 asserts 3 after a second. So the key is built from an OUTPUT of the pass. usage-record-repository.ts:70 dedupes with onConflictDoNothing on the exact idempotencyKey string, so a second execution writing `...:N+1` does not conflict: a second ledger row, and because quota-manager.ts:124-128 sums those rows via sumEmbeddingTokensForTenantSince, permanent double consumption of the project's embedding budget.

No terminal-state guard: grep -n "status ===\|status !==" backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts returns nothing; the only `status` occurrences are the write `status:"ready"` (:226) and the `failed` write in the catch (:238). Its sibling in the same package HAS the guard — scan.ts:58 `if (document.status !== "scanning") return "already_handled";`.

Duplicate delivery is a live path the repo itself documents: index.ts:535 ensures document.ingest with {retryLimit:2, expireInSeconds:120}; queue.ts:328-331 states jobs sit active until expireInSeconds and burn a retry; ADR-128 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2112) is the exact precedent ("a slow worker is indistinguishable from a dead one… every real generation outran its window and was generated a second time") and its decision line is "a job that reached a terminal state is never redone", implemented as a guard in processImageGeneration and applied to images/video render but NOT to document.ingest. 120s is realistically outrun: chunks are 500 chars (chunking.ts:9) and every chunk goes in one un-timeouted HTTP POST (providers/llm-local/src/index.ts:305-318), so a 100-page PDF is ~600 chunks in a single local-runtime call.

Not already fixed: grep -n "idempoten\|double-charge" docs/26_DECISIONS.md has no hit after ADR-131 (:2159), and ingest.ts is not among the modified files in the working tree.

Corrections to the finding: (1) "the opposite of what the comment claims" overstates it — the comment is literally satisfied for the common retry, since a pass that throws before replaceForDocument keeps its version and IS deduped; the failure is narrower, namely that the one case where money was actually spent is the case the key stops covering. (2) "embeddingMeter.check consumes the budget twice" is imprecise — check is read-only (index.ts:432-437); the duplicate record row is what consumes budget on every later check. Also note a stable key alone would not stop the second provider call, since embeddings.embed(chunks) at :208 runs unconditionally before record — the root defect is the missing terminal-state guard ADR-128 already decided platform-wide, with the mutable key as the second defect layered on top. The finding's own fix field names both correctly.

Severity P1 rather than P0: real money and quota double-count in a shipped capability that contradicts ADR-131's stated guarantee, but it is not an authorization/tenant bypass, requires a slow or re-delivered job, is bounded at three executions by retryLimit:2, and leaves the document in a correct final state — ingestion itself is not broken.

confirmed.title: document.ingest's 120s claim window runs against an embedding call that has no timeout at all
confirmed.evidence: backend/src/index.ts:535 — `ensureQueueWithDeadLetter("document.ingest", { retryLimit: 2, expireInSeconds: 120 })`. backend/packages/providers/llm-local/src/index.ts:306-317 — `async embed(texts: string[])` calls `fetchImpl(...)` with `body: JSON.stringify({ model, input: texts })` and **no `signal`, no AbortController, no timeout**; `grep -n "timeout\|AbortController\|signal" backend/packages/providers/llm-local/src/index.ts | sed -n '/28[0-9]\|3[0-3][0-9]/p'` finds none in that class. backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:208 sends the ENTIRE document's chunks in that one request. backend/src/index.ts:367-384 — this provider is selected automatically whenever `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL` is set or a local runtime is detected (ADR-118 Ollama adoption), so it is the default on any machine running Ollama.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-128's stated rule is "the provider must always give up first", and every media queue was re-derived from its provider's deadline. `document.ingest` was never revisited: its provider has no deadline to derive from. A hundred-page PDF embedded against Ollama on CPU routinely exceeds 120 seconds, so the job is re-claimed mid-embed and a second worker embeds the same document concurrently — and with the version-keyed idempotency defect above, charges for it. A genuinely hung embedding endpoint loses the worker for the lifetime of the process, exactly the ffmpeg hang ADR-128 fixed, while pg-boss hands the document to the next worker every 120 seconds.
confirmed.fix: Give `LocalEmbeddingProvider.embed` an AbortController deadline (as `OpenAiSpeechProvider.synthesize` has at speech.ts:110-115), batch large documents, and derive `document.ingest`'s `expireInSeconds` from that deadline the way image.generate derives its own at index.ts:558-562.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED by reading the code. (1) backend/src/index.ts:535 sets document.ingest to expireInSeconds: 120 — the only queue in that block with a hand-picked constant; image.generate (558-562), video.render (582-585) and video.generate_scene (578) all derive/justify theirs from a provider deadline under ADR-128. (2) backend/packages/providers/llm-local/src/index.ts:305-317 — LocalEmbeddingProvider.embed calls fetchImpl with method/headers/body and no signal; grep for timeout|AbortController|signal on that file hits only lines 45,72,82,117-131,228, all inside the CHAT class LocalOpenAICompatibleProvider (which does have requestTimeoutMs ?? 300_000 + AbortController). The embedding class has no deadline. (3) Nothing wraps it: both construction sites (index.ts:369, :379) pass no fetchImpl, so production uses global fetch; EmbeddingService.embed (packages/embeddings/src/embedding-service.ts:52-64) forwards the array unchanged with no batching or timeout; grep AbortController|setTimeout over rag/src/ingest.ts and embedding-service.ts returns nothing (exit 1). (4) The whole document goes in one call: ingest.ts:208 `await deps.embeddings.embed(chunks)` with chunkText at 500 chars (chunking.ts:9) and no cap, against a 25 MiB upload limit (server.ts:26); ADR-131 itself calls ingestion "an entire document's chunks in one batch". (5) It is the default with Ollama running — index.ts:367-384 selects LocalEmbeddingProvider on EMBEDDING_BASE_URL+MODEL or on detectedRuntime.embeddingModel (ADR-118, whose verification log at 26_DECISIONS.md:1970 shows nomic-embed-text adopted with no .env); only HashEmbeddingProvider and LocalEmbeddingProvider implement the interface. (6) No ADR addresses it: ADR-128 (26_DECISIONS.md:2108-2112) names image.generate, video.render and ffmpeg only; ADR-131 touches ingestion for metering, not its claim window; grep for document.ingest in 26_DECISIONS.md finds no claim-window entry. (7) packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:328 confirms expireInSeconds semantics ("sat active until expireInSeconds elapsed, burning one retry"), and registerWorker at index.ts:767 passes no localConcurrency, so one stuck handler holds the slot. Restated defect: any ingest whose single batched embedding call exceeds 120s is re-claimed mid-embed, so a second (then third, retryLimit 2) worker embeds the same document concurrently against the same single-threaded runtime — each pass slowing the others — and the job dead-letters at ~360s even though the original attempt may later succeed and mark the document ready, leaving DLQ and document state disagreeing. Severity held at P1, not raised: it is a real defect in a shipped default path but not remotely exploitable and not a wholly broken capability. Two overstatements in the finding, neither fatal: (a) "charges for it" — the meter key is `embedding:ingest:${document.id}:${document.version}` and bumpVersion only happens on success, so the concurrent duplicate shares the key and the LEDGER row dedups; the provider is still genuinely called twice (CPU, or money when EMBEDDING_API_KEY is set), which is precisely ADR-128's "deduplicated the BILLING RECORD... made the double spend invisible rather than preventing it". (b) "loses the worker for the lifetime of the process" — undici's default headersTimeout (300s) will eventually reject, though that is still 2.5x the claim window. The fix citation's path is slightly off: the AbortController-deadline precedent is backend/packages/media/src/speech.ts:113-135, not backend/packages/providers/speech/.

confirmed.title: processVideoScene swallows every provider failure, so video.generate_scene can never retry and never dead-letters
confirmed.evidence: backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:282-288 — the catch records `updateStatus(scope, sceneId, "failed", { lastError, incrementRetry: true })` and then falls through to `await checkProjectCompletion(...)`. There is no rethrow: `grep -n "throw err;" backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts` returns only :332, which is inside `checkProjectCompletion`'s enqueue catch, a different function. The provider-said-no branch at :236-242 likewise records `failed` and does not throw. Compare image-generation.ts:99 `throw err;` and audio-generation.ts:99 `throw err;` ("Rethrown so the queue sees a failure and applies its own retry and dead-letter policy"). Configuration that therefore never fires: backend/src/index.ts:574 `ensureQueueWithDeadLetter("video.generate_scene", { retryLimit: 1, expireInSeconds: 900 })`.
confirmed.why_it_matters: A scene whose provider call fails completes its pg-boss job successfully. Consequences, all of them silent: (1) `retryLimit: 1` never applies — a transient provider outage, the exact case ADR-072's DLQ exists for, permanently fails the scene with no automatic retry; (2) `video.generate_scene.dlq` can never receive a provider failure, so `onDeadLetter` / `job_dead_letter_total` (index.ts:526) never counts one and the dead-letter screen never shows a failed scene; (3) the ADR-130 replay-pricing branch for `video.generate_scene` at backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:255-264 is unreachable for the failure it was written for; (4) `runJob` (index.ts:1630-1645) sees a resolved promise and emits `recordJobProcessed({ outcome: "success" })`, so `job_processed_total` reports every failed scene as a success. confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED by reading the code. backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:282-287 catches any provider exception, writes updateStatus(..., "failed", { lastError, incrementRetry: true }) and ends; `grep -n "throw" video-orchestration.ts` returns only 148, 210, 252 (a comment) and 332 (inside checkProjectCompletion's enqueue catch, a different function). Control then falls to `await checkProjectCompletion(...)` at :289, which after a failed scene takes the partially_succeeded path and cannot throw. The worker at backend/src/index.ts:929-1002 does not rethrow either (the finally records recordMediaJob failure, the usage block is skipped, the handler resolves), so runJob at index.ts:1644 emits recordJobProcessed({ outcome: "success" }) and pg-boss sees a completed job. `ensureQueueWithDeadLetter("video.generate_scene", { retryLimit: 1, expireInSeconds: 900 })` (index.ts:574) therefore cannot apply to a provider failure, and video.generate_scene.dlq cannot receive one.

It is the sole outlier among the four media processors: image-generation.ts:99, audio-generation.ts:99 ("Rethrown so the queue sees a failure and applies its own retry and dead-letter policy") and video-render.ts:468 all record the failure then `throw err;`. Strongest corroboration, which the finding did not cite: backend/packages/providers/video-replicate/src/index.ts:261-263 asserts in a comment that "`processVideoScene` catches the throw, marks the scene failed with `incrementRetry`, and pg-boss retries" — a documented claim the code does not honour. No compensating mechanism exists: scene.retryCount is written (video-scene-repository.ts:119) and read by nothing (`grep -rn "retryCount"` outside dist/ hits only pg-boss's own job metadata and the frontend job table), and orchestrateVideoProject's only callers are routes/v1/videos.ts:82 (create) and :160 (manual retry). No ADR covers it: `grep -i "rethrow|swallow" docs/26_DECISIONS.md` hits only ADR-133/139 contexts; ADR-085/128 are claim windows, ADR-130 is replay pricing, ADR-140 is the cancelled status. The test-coverage claim holds — video-pipeline.integration.test.ts:54-62's FlakyVideoProvider RETURNS {status:"failed"} (the :236 branch), never throws, and uses retryLimit: 0; jobs/src/dead-letter.test.ts uses synthetic queues only.

Two corrections to the finding. (1) "all of them silent" overstates the user-facing impact: checkProjectCompletion lands the project in partially_succeeded with "N of M scene(s) failed to generate. Re-run orchestration (POST /api/v1/videos/:id/retry)...", and that endpoint re-enqueues only the failed scenes, so nothing is lost or double-charged — the silence is at the ops layer (no automatic retry, no dead letter, and job_processed_total mislabelling failures as successes, which is precisely the metric ADR-082 says alerts are built on). recordMediaJob does report failure correctly, so observability is not wholly blind. (2) The provider-said-no branch at :236-242 not throwing is NOT a divergence — image-generation.ts:82-88 does the same; the only real divergence is the exception path at :282. Severity P1 (not P0): configured retry/dead-letter machinery that cannot fire for its queue's dominant failure mode is a shipped capability that does not work, but the project status is honest and a manual retry path exists.

confirmed.title: ADR-128's re-claim guard exists only for images: an audio or video-scene re-claim calls the paid provider twice and the ledger hides the second charge
confirmed.evidence: `grep -n "status ===\|status !==" backend/packages/media/src/{image-generation,audio-generation,video-orchestration,video-render}.ts backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts` returns the terminal-state guard at image-generation.ts:70 (`if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return;`) and NOWHERE else. audio-generation.ts:48-57 checks only `cancelRequestedAt`, then unconditionally `updateStatus(..., "processing", { incrementAttempt: true })` and calls `deps.speech.synthesize`. video-orchestration.ts:218-230 checks only `project.cancelRequestedAt`, then `updateStatus(scope, sceneId, "processing")` and calls `deps.provider.generateVideo`. Both charges use a stable key that deduplicates the ROW: backend/src/index.ts:911 `idempotencyKey: `audio.generate:${generationId}`` and index.ts:996 `idempotencyKey: `video.scene:${sceneId}``.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-128's own argument is that widening the window "removes the routine case but not a genuinely dead worker or a restart mid-generation", which is why `processImageGeneration` got the guard — and the guard was never applied to the other two paid media paths. A worker killed between handler resolution and pg-boss's completion write leaves the job `active`; it expires and a second worker re-runs a generation that is already `succeeded`, calling a billed TTS endpoint or video provider a second time and storing a second asset that overwrites `resultAssetId`/`assetId` (orphaning the first). Because the usage key is stable, the ledger records one charge — the double spend is invisible in the ledger while the provider was really paid twice, which ADR-128 names as "worse to find than to have".
confirmed.fix: Add the same early return to both: in `processAudioGeneration` before audio-generation.ts:57, `if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return { status: generation.status, assetId: generation.resultAssetId ?? null, durationSeconds: generation.durationSeconds ?? null };`, and in `processVideoScene` before video-orchestration.ts:226, `if (scene.status === "succeeded" || scene.status === "cancelled") return;`.
confirmed.verdict: Restated from the code: ADR-128's terminal-state guard exists at backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:70 and nowhere else. `processAudioGeneration` (audio-generation.ts:46-60) checks only `cancelRequestedAt`, then unconditionally sets "processing" (line 57) and calls `deps.speech.synthesize` (line 60). `processVideoScene` (video-orchestration.ts:202-230) checks only `project?.cancelRequestedAt`, then sets "processing" (line 226) and calls `deps.provider.generateVideo` (line 228). A non-test grep for `=== "succeeded"` across backend/packages/media/src returns only image-generation.ts:70 (the guard), video-orchestration.ts:156 (a different function, on the project row inside `orchestrateVideoProject`), 315/338 (completion counting) and video-render.ts:159 (scene filter) — no guard on re-entry into either paid path. No mitigation elsewhere: the workers in backend/src/index.ts (872-885, 929-945) call both functions with no status pre-check, and `PgAudioGenerationRepository.updateStatus` / `PgVideoSceneRepository.updateStatus` carry no terminal-state predicate in their WHERE (id + tenant scope only). The invisible-double-spend half is confirmed too: usage-record-repository.ts:65-72 inserts with `.onConflictDoNothing({ target: usageRecords.idempotencyKey })` and the keys are stable per row (`audio.generate:${generationId}` at index.ts:921, `video.scene:${sceneId}` at index.ts:999), so a second provider call produces no second ledger row. ADR-128 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2110-2118) argues the guard is needed because a widened window does not cover a dead worker or a restart, names only `processImageGeneration`, and lists only {image-generation,video-render}.ts in its Impact; no ADR 129-143 revisits it, and the only regression test is job-deadlines.test.ts:34 "a re-claimed image job does not pay twice". The trigger is in fact wider than the finding claims: both workers do post-success work after the row is already `succeeded` (videoScenes.get / videoProjects.get / usage.create / logging), and any throw there propagates out of runJob so pg-boss retries (retryLimit: 1 on both queues) straight back into the unguarded function — no worker death required. Both paths can reach billed providers (OpenAiSpeechProvider in speech.ts:80; packages/providers/video-replicate). Inaccuracies are cosmetic and do not change the verdict: the idempotency-key lines are index.ts:921 and 999 (not 911/996), and "orphaning the first asset" overstates it — the first asset row survives under the same project, it is only de-referenced from resultAssetId/assetId. P1 is correct: a real defect in a shipped billed capability, needing a crash or a post-success throw rather than being attacker-triggerable, so not P0.

confirmed.title: Replay's "cannot be replayed twice" guard is read-then-write, so N concurrent replays of one dead letter enqueue N paid jobs
confirmed.evidence: backend/packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:476-486 — `replayDeadLettered` runs `select data from pgboss.job where name=$1 and id=$2 and data->>'projectId'=$3 and state in ('created','retry')`, then `const replayedId = await this.boss.send(sourceQueueNameFor(deadLetterQueue), row.data);` and only THEN `await this.boss.cancel(deadLetterQueue, jobId);`. Nothing is atomic between the SELECT and the send. The route has no serialisation either: backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:266 calls it directly, behind only `{ config: { rateLimit: { max: 10, timeWindow: "1 minute" } } }` (:212). The queue's own docstring at queue.ts:39-43 records that pg-boss's default `standard` policy "ignores `singletonKey` entirely", so the duplicate sends are not deduplicated downstream. The test that claims to cover this — dead-letter.test.ts:187-203, "refuses to replay the same dead letter twice" — awaits the first replay before issuing the second, so it never exercises the race.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-130 states "the `state in ('created','retry')` predicate ... stops a dead letter being replayed twice". It stops a SEQUENTIAL second replay only. Two browser tabs, a double-click, or ten concurrent POSTs within the rate-limit window all pass the SELECT while the row is still `created`, and each one sends a real job to the live queue — up to ten paid image generations, speech syntheses or video scenes from one dead letter. The quota checks at platform.ts:237-264 are checks, not reservations, so all N pass together. For `image.generate` the N concurrent jobs all read `status: "failed"` before any writes, so the ADR-128 guard does not stop them either, and the single `image.generate:<id>` usage row means N-1 provider calls are charged with no ledger trace. The codebase already contains the correct pattern for exactly this shape — `claimRenderSlot`, a single `UPDATE ... WHERE render_requested_at IS NULL` that only one concurrent caller can match (video-orchestration.ts:300-304).
confirmed.fix: Make the consumption the claim: cancel (or conditionally UPDATE) the dead letter first and only send when that write reports one row affected — i.e. a single `update pgboss.job set state='cancelled' where name=$1 and id=$2 and data->>'projectId'=$3 and state in ('created','retry') returning data`, then `boss.send` the returned payload. Add a concurrent test (two un-awaited replays, assert exactly one truthy id).
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, with one part of the evidence corrected.

Restating the defect from the code: backend/packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:478-487 is a read-then-write. `this.query` issues a bare `select data from pgboss.job where name=$1 and id=$2 and data->>'projectId'=$3 and state in ('created','retry')` through a single `db.executeSql` (queue.ts:263-267) with no transaction, no FOR UPDATE and no lock; then `await this.boss.send(sourceQueueNameFor(deadLetterQueue), row.data)`; and only then `await this.boss.cancel(deadLetterQueue, jobId)`. The route calls it directly (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts, `POST /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/:queue/:id/replay`) behind only `{ config: { rateLimit: { max: 10, timeWindow: "1 minute" } } }`, with no serialisation. N concurrent POSTs for one dead letter all observe `created`, all pass, and each issues a real `boss.send` to the live source queue. Note the interleaving happens even on single-connection pglite, because each `await` yields.

Nothing deduplicates the duplicate sends. Every queue is created by `ensureQueueWithDeadLetter` in backend/src/index.ts:535-582 with only `retryLimit`/`expireInSeconds` — grep for `policy:` in index.ts returns nothing, so all queues are pg-boss `standard`, which the package's own docstring (queue.ts:51-54) states ignores `singletonKey` entirely. `replayDeadLettered` passes no options to `send` at all, and grep shows `singletonKey` appears only in the interface declaration (queue.ts:40) and never at a call site.

Not already fixed, and the ADR is the source of the false claim rather than a fix. docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2140 (ADR-130) asserts the `state in ('created','retry')` predicate "stops a dead letter being replayed twice" — it stops a SEQUENTIAL second replay only. The test ADR-130 cites, dead-letter.test.ts "refuses to replay the same dead letter twice", awaits the first replay before issuing the second, so it cannot exercise the race. Grepping ADR headings and replay mentions after line 2140 shows no later ADR (131-144) touches replay concurrency. The codebase contains both the correct pattern and the correct reasoning: `checkProjectCompletion`'s docstring in backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts (~line 300) says "A read-then-write guard cannot fix that (both callers read 'no render requested yet' before either writes), so the guard is the repository's `claimRenderSlot`: a single `UPDATE ... WHERE render_requested_at IS NULL` that exactly one concurrent caller can match."

The quota sub-claim holds: `checkImageGeneration` (quota-manager.ts:149-156), `checkVideoSeconds` (:158-166) and `checkSpeechCharacters` (:175-183) are count/sum-then-compare reads with no reservation, so all N concurrent checks pass together.

CORRECTION — the finding's image.generate reasoning is wrong, and it is the part it argued hardest. It claims "the N concurrent jobs all read `status: \"failed\"` before any writes, so the ADR-128 guard does not stop them either." In the shipped configuration it does. `processImageGeneration` returns early on `status === "succeeded" || "cancelled"` (backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:70); the image worker registers with no `WorkOptions` (backend/src/index.ts:795 — only `video.generate_scene` passes `{ localConcurrency: 3 }` at index.ts:1004), and the worker pool is `scaling_mode = "MANUAL"`, `manual_instance_count = 1` (infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:468-470). So duplicate image jobs are handled one at a time and #2..N short-circuit on `succeeded`. For images the damage is wasted queue slots, not N provider charges.

The duplicate-PAID-work impact nevertheless survives, via the two queues I checked directly, so the finding's severity stands on evidence it did not cite: `processAudioGeneration` (backend/packages/media/src/audio-generation.ts:46-57) has NO terminal-state guard at all — only `cancelRequestedAt`, then straight to `updateStatus(..., "processing")` and `deps.speech.synthesize` — so every duplicate re-synthesises even when processed strictly sequentially. `processVideoScene` (video-orchestration.ts:205-226) likewise has no terminal-state guard, only the project-level `cancelRequestedAt`, and its worker runs `localConcurrency: 3`, so up to three duplicates genuinely overlap inside `provider.generateVideo`.

Severity P1 is right, not P0: exercising it requires the caller to fire concurrent requests against their OWN tenant's dead letter holding `project:write`, bounded at 10 per minute by the route's rate limit. It is duplicate paid work and a violated documented guarantee within one tenant's own budget — a real defect in a shipped capability — not a cross-tenant, authorization or quota-ceiling bypass. The proposed fix (make the consumption the claim: a single `update pgboss.job set state='cancelled' where ... and state in ('created','retry') returning data`, then send the returned payload) is the right shape and matches `claimRenderSlot`.

confirmed.title: The embedding quota can never be configured, so `checkEmbeddingTokens` is a permanent no-op in every real deployment
confirmed.evidence:
backend/src/index.ts:410-417 constructs the only production `QuotaManager`:
```
const quota = new QuotaManager(usage, {
  dailyTokenLimit: config.DAILY_TOKEN_LIMIT,
  monthlyTokenLimit: config.MONTHLY_TOKEN_LIMIT,
  dailyImageLimit: config.DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT,
  dailySpeechCharacterLimit: config.DAILY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT,
  monthlySpeechCharacterLimit: config.MONTHLY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT,
  monthlyVideoSecondsLimit: config.MONTHLY_VIDEO_SECONDS_LIMIT,
});
```
`dailyEmbeddingTokenLimit` / `monthlyEmbeddingTokenLimit` are absent. Proof there is no env var to supply them: `grep -rn "EMBEDDING_TOKEN_LIMIT|dailyEmbeddingTokenLimit|monthlyEmbeddingTokenLimit" --include=*.ts --include=*.md --include=*.example --include=*.tf . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/` returns ONLY `backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:48,49,125` (the declarations) and two test files (`quota-manager.test.ts:201,286`, `spend-guards.test.ts:91`) that construct a `QuotaManager` by hand. `backend/src/config.ts:306-311` declares DAILY_TOKEN_LIMIT, MONTHLY_TOKEN_LIMIT, DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT, DAILY/MONTHLY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT, MONTHLY_VIDEO_SECONDS_LIMIT — and no embedding limit. `.env.example:84-89` lists the same six and no embedding limit.
Consequence at `backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:126`: `if (daily === undefined && monthly === undefined) return { allowed: true };` — taken unconditionally.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-119 and ADR-131 both headline "embedding spend is asked about before it happens". It is recorded, but the asking half can never say no. Every `EmbeddingMeter.check` call site — `backend/src/index.ts:435` (the meter used by document ingestion at `backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:206`, the agent's `rag.search_documents` at `backend/packages/rag/src/retrieve.ts:94`, and memory's three paths at `backend/packages/memory/src/memory-service.ts:325`) and `backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:295` — is a gate that always opens. So is the fail-CLOSED branch at quota-manager.ts:131-139 that ADR-131 argues for at length, and `PgUsageRecordRepository.sumEmbeddingTokensForTenantSince` is never reached in production. A hundred-page PDF ingest, or an agent that searches in a loop, spends unbounded embedding tokens no operator can cap. The whole suite stays green because both tests that exercise this path build the limit by hand rather than through config.
confirmed.fix: Add `DAILY_EMBEDDING_TOKEN_LIMIT` / `MONTHLY_EMBEDDING_TOKEN_LIMIT` to `backend/src/config.ts` and `.env.example`, pass them into the `QuotaManager` at `backend/src/index.ts:410`, and add a boot-level test that asserts the constructed manager carries every `QuotaLimits` key the config schema can supply (so a limit added to `QuotaLimits` but never wired is a failing test, not a silent no-op).
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — I restated the defect from the code independently. backend/src/index.ts:410-417 is the only production QuotaManager (grep 'new QuotaManager' over *.ts minus node_modules/dist: only index.ts:410, test-app.ts:213, and 5 test files) and passes exactly six limits: dailyTokenLimit, monthlyTokenLimit, dailyImageLimit, daily/monthlySpeechCharacterLimit, monthlyVideoSecondsLimit. Neither dailyEmbeddingTokenLimit nor monthlyEmbeddingTokenLimit is passed, and there is no way to supply them: backend/src/config.ts:306-311 declares the same six and no embedding var, .env.example:81-89 ("Cost & quota (ADR-038, FR-063)") lists the same six, and grep 'EMBEDDING_TOKEN_LIMIT|dailyEmbeddingTokenLimit|monthlyEmbeddingTokenLimit' over *.ts,*.tsx,*.md,*.example,*.tf,*.json,*.yml (minus node_modules/dist) returns ONLY the type declarations at quota-manager.ts:48,49,125 and three hand-built test constructions (quota-manager.test.ts:201,286; spend-guards.test.ts:91). So quota-manager.ts:126 `if (daily === undefined && monthly === undefined) return { allowed: true };` is taken unconditionally in every real deployment.

Consequence verified: the deny half of the embedding budget is unreachable in production. That covers the fail-CLOSED branch at quota-manager.ts:128-139 (which ADR-131 and the repository comment at usage-record-repository.ts:122-128 both argue for at length), PgUsageRecordRepository.sumEmbeddingTokensForTenantSince (usage-record-repository.ts:188 — grep shows its only other references are quota-manager.ts:128,134 and quota-manager.test.ts:290), and every EmbeddingMeter.check call site: index.ts:431-436 feeding rag ingest (ingest.ts:206), rag retrieve / the agent's rag.search_documents (retrieve.ts:94), memory (memory-service.ts, wired at index.ts:459), the agent tool registry (index.ts:506, 784), plus the direct check at routes/v1/rag.ts:295.

No other configured limit covers the gap: sumLlmTokensForTenantSince filters kind = 'llm' (usage-record-repository.ts:169-173), so embedding rows never count against DAILY_TOKEN_LIMIT. Embedding is the one billable dimension with no operator-settable ceiling, while llm/image/video/speech all have one.

Doc claims the code does not honour, confirmed by reading docs/26_DECISIONS.md: ADR-119 (line 1981) "a configured embedding limit made checkEmbeddingTokens fail closed"; ADR-126 (line 2082) "The same held for images, video-seconds, embedding tokens and speech characters"; ADR-131 (line 2153) "a project refused a single RAG query for being over its embedding limit could still ingest a hundred-page PDF". All describe a configured embedding limit as a reachable state. It is not. No ADR in 123..144 wires it — ADR-123's amendment (line 2045) corrected the fail-closed TEST onto a ledger with the aggregate stripped, which is exactly why the suite stays green over the unwired config.

Two calibrations to the finding, neither of which changes the verdict: (1) it omits that EmbeddingMeter.check also short-circuits when embeddings.isDeterministicFallback is true (index.ts:432), so the uncapped-spend harm materializes only where a real paid embedder is configured — which is precisely the deployment the gate exists for, so the impact stands; (2) spend is still RECORDED, so an operator can see embedding cost after the fact via the ledger, just never cap it (and routes/v1/usage.ts:70-75 does not report embedding limits either).

Severity held at P1, not raised to P0: nothing is exploitable across a trust boundary, no user-facing capability is broken, the default deployment uses the free local fallback embedder, and quotas are opt-in by design. It is a real defect in a shipped capability — an entire enforcement path (check-before-call, fail-closed branch, tenant-scoped SQL aggregate, meter plumbed into five call sites) that can never deny, with the config key that would arm it missing from the composition root.

confirmed.title: The video storyboard model call spends LLM tokens with no quota check and writes no usage row
confirmed.evidence:
`POST /api/v1/videos` checks only video-seconds — backend/src/routes/v1/videos.ts:59: `const quotaCheck = await ctx.quota.checkVideoSeconds(projectId, parsed.data.targetDurationSeconds);` — then at line 63-72 calls `createVideoProject({ ..., scriptModel: ctx.router })`. `backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:72` runs `const script = await writeVideoScript({ model: deps.scriptModel }, input.request);`, which reaches a real provider at `backend/packages/media/src/video-script.ts:194`: `for await (const event of model.streamChat({ messages }, { signal }))`.
Absence proof: `grep -rn "usage|quota|Meter" --include=*.ts backend/packages/media/src | grep -v '\.test\.ts'` returns exactly two hits, both prose comments (`video-orchestration.ts:136` and `:153`). There is no `usage.create`, no `checkLlmTokens` and no `EmbeddingMeter`/`ModelCallMeter` anywhere in the media package.

confirmed.fix: Estimate the storyboard prompt and call `ctx.quota.checkLlmTokens(projectId, estimate)` in `videos.ts` before `createVideoProject`, and have `writeVideoScript` report its terminal `done` usage back so the route writes a `kind: "llm"` row keyed on the video project id. confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED by reading the code. backend/src/routes/v1/videos.ts:59 checks only checkVideoSeconds, then line 71 passes scriptModel: ctx.router into createVideoProject; video-orchestration.ts:72 awaits writeVideoScript, which in video-script.ts drives a real provider via completeText -> model.streamChat(...) inline in the HTTP request. deps.model is never absent on this path: AppContext.router is non-optional (context.ts:35, wired index.ts:1316), so the deterministic fallback is only reached on error/timeout — the videos.ts comment claiming the model is "absent when no chat provider is configured" does not match the code. Nothing meters the call: the router's only instance-wide hook, onCall at index.ts:1117-1139, writes Prometheus counters (recordProviderCall/recordTokenUsage) and no ledger row; ADR-132 explicitly left ledger writes with the callers. Absence proofs I ran: grep -rn "checkLlmTokens" over backend+shared returns only chat.ts:175/275/605, rag.ts:378, index.ts:1161 (agent meter) and tests — nothing in videos.ts; grep for usage|quota|Meter in backend/packages/media/src (minus tests) returns only the two prose comments at video-orchestration.ts:136 and :153; the usage.create sites in backend/src are embedding (441), image (848), speech (909), kind:"video" per scene (985), agent (1179), chat.ts 206/445/637, rag.ts 307/408 — no kind:"llm" row on the video path. Not already fixed: ADR-137 (26_DECISIONS.md:2223) touched this same call but added only scenesWritten and a 25s deadline while noting it runs inside POST /api/v1/videos; ADR-119 closed the analogous rag.ts hole, ADR-131 added the EmbeddingMeter, ADR-132 is metrics-only; no ADR-123..144 covers storyboard token spend. Impact holds with one nuance the finding omits: checkVideoSeconds runs first, so an exhausted video-seconds budget does block the call — but that limit is optional (quota-manager.ts:158 returns allowed:true when monthlyVideoSecondsLimit is undefined), so by default only the 5/min rate limit stands between a caller and repeated unmetered model calls, and a tenant at its token ceiling (refused by /api/v1/chat and /api/v1/rag/query) still gets a storyboard call. The spend is never written to usage_records, so it never counts toward the next checkLlmTokens, never shows on /api/v1/usage, and is missing from estimatedCostUsdThisMonth (usage.ts:55-66). Not trivial in size: shared/src/video.ts:56-60 allows targetDurationSeconds up to 1800 with sceneClipSeconds as low as 2, i.e. one reply asked for up to 900 shot descriptions plus narration. confirmed.title: Narration synthesised inside a video scene job bypasses the speech quota and writes no speech usage row
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-114's stated rule is that "'generate audio' is not a free action just because this deployment runs piper", and `speech.ts` includes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP synthesiser that bills per character. A 600-second video is up to 150 scenes of narration; the whole of it is synthesised outside the speech budget and leaves no `kind: "speech"` row, so `checkSpeechCharacters` on the *next* `POST /api/v1/audio` under-counts what the tenant has already spent. `DAILY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT` therefore caps only the one route a user can reach directly, not the route that synthesises the most.
confirmed.fix: Give `processVideoScene` the same `EmbeddingMeter`-style injected interface the RAG package got in ADR-131 (a `SpeechMeter` with `check(projectId, characters)` / `record(...)`, implemented once in the composition root), so the media package stays billing-free while the narration is gated before synthesis and recorded as `kind: "speech"`, `units: narration.length`, keyed `video.scene.narration:${sceneId}`.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED from the code, and every cited line/grep is accurate. backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:256-258 calls deps.speech.synthesize(narration) inside processVideoScene with no budget check before it and no usage row after it. grep -rn 'checkSpeechCharacters' --include=*.ts . (minus node_modules//dist/) yields only the definition at backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:175 plus backend/src/routes/v1/audio.ts:56 and backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:247 (dead-letter replay) — nothing on the video path; backend/src/routes/v1/videos.ts mentions speech nowhere and gates only with checkVideoSeconds (lines 59, 155). grep -rn 'kind: "speech"' --include=*.ts . returns exactly ONE production write, backend/src/index.ts:913 in the audio.generate worker; the scene worker at backend/src/index.ts:985-1001 writes only kind "video", units scene.durationSeconds, key video.scene:${sceneId} (verified at lines 989/994/999). The aggregate behind the limit is sumTenantColumnSince(projectId, "speech", usageRecords.units, since) at backend/packages/database/src/repositories/usage-record-repository.ts:192, so narration characters are invisible to it. No metering wrapper exists anywhere: grep -rn 'Meter' over backend/ and shared/ (excluding tests) returns only ModelCallMeter, EmbeddingMeter and OTel's MeterProvider, and backend/src/index.ts:947 hands processVideoScene the raw SpeechProvider. No ADR fixes it: ADR-114 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1898) scopes the character budget to POST /api/v1/audio; ADR-130 (:2136) priced the video.generate_scene replay with checkVideoSeconds only; ADR-131 (:2149) is the identical shape one budget over and is the pattern the proposed fix cites; grep -n 'narration' docs/26_DECISIONS.md shows no decision on narration spend. One correction to the finding's framing: the video path is not entirely ungated — MONTHLY_VIDEO_SECONDS_LIMIT covers it — but that is a different ceiling in a different unit, and both it and DAILY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT are optional() with no default in backend/src/config.ts:309-311, so an operator who sets only the speech limit binds the one route a user reaches directly while POST /api/v1/videos (targetDurationSeconds up to 1800, sceneClipSeconds down to 2 => up to 900 scenes, <=25 words of narration each per video-script.ts:94) synthesises unbounded characters through the per-character-billed OpenAiSpeechProvider. The ledger defect holds regardless of limits: GET /api/v1/usage and the next checkSpeechCharacters both read a speech total that omits every narration the platform has spoken. P1 rather than P0: it requires an operator to have configured the speech ceiling (or to rely on ledger accuracy) rather than being exploitable against stock config, and the video route does carry its own budget.

confirmed.title: The agent's verification model call is ungated, unrecorded, and outside the run's own token budget
confirmed.evidence: The quota gate for a reasoning node wraps only `deps.streamChat` — engine.ts:755-761 defines `checkTurnQuota`, and engine.ts:783-787 is the only place it is applied. The `verify` hook at engine.ts:828-832 calls `this.verifyAutonomousAnswer(...)`, which at engine.ts:1104 calls the router directly: `for await (const event of this.deps.modelRouter.streamChat({ messages }, { signal }))` — no `checkTurnQuota`, and no `meter.record`. `grep -n "meter" backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts` returns 132, 756, 758, 765, 891, 892, 1009, 1011, 1026, 1029 — none inside `verifyAutonomousAnswer` (lines ~1078-1122). Usage rows for a reasoning node come only from the loop's `usage` event (engine.ts:891-908), which `reasoning-loop.ts:162` emits only from the `deps.streamChat` drain; `reasoning-loop.ts:160-161` likewise accumulates `maxTotalTokens` only there. `reasoning-loop.ts:243-244` shows `deps.verify` is genuinely invoked on every answered turn.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Every autonomous run makes at least one verifier call carrying the goal, the answer and up to 4000 characters of tool evidence (engine.ts:1060-1064), plus another after a self-correction. A task whose project is over its token ceiling is refused for its reasoning turns and still pays for verification. The tokens are absent from `usage_records`, so they do not count against the next check, do not appear on `/api/v1/usage`, and do not count toward `AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RUN` — an operator's per-run ceiling is quietly exceeded by the verifier's share on every run.
confirmed.fix: Route `verifyAutonomousAnswer` through the same `checkTurnQuota` + `meter.record` pair the turns use, with an idempotency key such as `agent.node:${node.id}:verify:${turn}`, and feed its usage back into the loop's `usage` accumulator so `maxTotalTokens` covers it.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED in substance, with the impact narrative overstated. engine.ts:1104 (`verifyAutonomousAnswer`, lines 1071-1122) calls `this.deps.modelRouter.streamChat` directly; the only quota gate (`checkTurnQuota`, engine.ts:755-763) is applied at engine.ts:784 inside the wrapper passed to `runReasoningLoop`, and the only ledger write (engine.ts:891-910) fires on the loop's `usage` event, which reasoning-loop.ts:158-162 emits only from its own `deps.streamChat` drain — the same lines that accumulate the `maxTotalTokens` budget checked at reasoning-loop.ts:132. `grep -n "meter" backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts` returns 132, 756, 758, 765, 891, 892, 1009, 1011, 1026, 1029: none inside verifyAutonomousAnswer. The path is live, not dead code — engine.ts:828-832 supplies `verify`, reasoning-loop.ts:243 invokes it on the answered turn, planner.ts:102/363 plan the reasoning node. Nothing else closes the gap: the composition root's `onCall` (backend/src/index.ts:1117-1139) only feeds Prometheus counters, while usage_records, /api/v1/usage and quota.checkLlmTokens come exclusively from `meter.record` (index.ts:1163-1200). No ADR covers it (ADR-133 wired the hook; ADR-046/131/132 metered other callers). TWO CLAIMS FAIL: (1) "plus another after a self-correction" is wrong — reasoning-loop.ts:243 guards with `!correctionUsed` and the correction branch sets it before `continue`, so at most one verifier call per loop entry; (2) "refused for its reasoning turns and still pays for verification" does not follow — checkTurnQuota throws before each turn's provider call and the throw propagates out of the loop to fail the node, so a quota-refused run never reaches the verify hook; verification only follows a turn that just passed the check. Severity lowered P1 -> P2: the defect is real and of the class this repo has repeatedly fixed ("every model call is counted"), but it is one bounded call per run (goal + answer + <=4000 chars of evidence, engine.ts:1060-1064), roughly 1-2k tokens against a 200k default AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RUN, with no amplification path — the verifier cannot be reached without first paying for a metered, quota-checked turn, and its prompt is capped. Real ledger/quota under-reporting, not an exploitable or blocking one.

confirmed.title: `/api/v1/usage` shows per-project usage against organization-wide limits, so the dashboard and the enforcement disagree
confirmed.evidence:
The route uses the PROJECT-scoped aggregates — backend/src/routes/v1/usage.ts:55-61 calls `ctx.usage.sumLlmTokensSince`, `countImagesSince`, `sumVideoSecondsSince`, `sumLlmCostUsdSince`, whose SQL is `eq(usageRecords.projectId, projectId)` (usage-record-repository.ts:196-206, `sumColumnSince`). The quota manager uses the TENANT-scoped ones — `QuotaUsageLedger` (quota-manager.ts:19-25) declares only `sumLlmTokensForTenantSince` / `countImagesForTenantSince` / `sumVideoSecondsForTenantSince`, implemented at usage-record-repository.ts:165-190 over `tenantProjects(projectId)`, which resolves to every project of the same `organizationId`.
The comment that is now false, usage.ts:42-45: "what is per-project is the *usage measured against them*, since every aggregate above and every `QuotaManager` check now filters on the project id." ADR-126 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2078) moved the checks to organization scope and this route was not revisited.
docs/22_COST_AND_QUOTA_STRATEGY.md:15: "Usage is decremented from the same `usage_records` table that powers the usage dashboard (`/api/v1/usage`), so quota state and displayed usage can never disagree."
The screen states it too — frontend/app/usage/page.tsx:70: "Everything this project has spent, for the selected project only" — and then renders `<Meter label="Tokens today" used={usage.llm.tokensToday} limit={limits.dailyTokenLimit} />` (page.tsx:75).
confirmed.why_it_matters: This is exactly the failure usage.ts's own opening comment (lines 13-18) was written to prevent: the endpoint says "800 tokens used of 200,000" while the quota manager refuses the next call on a different total. With `DAILY_TOKEN_LIMIT=200000` and three projects in one org, each project's Usage page shows a near-empty meter while the very next chat turn returns 429 in all three. The meter's percentage and progress bar are arithmetic between two different denominators, and the 429's message ("Daily token limit of 200000 would be exceeded (199950 used so far today)") names a number the screen never displays.
confirmed.fix: Either report the tenant totals the limits are actually enforced against (call the `ForTenantSince` aggregates and relabel the screen as organization spend, keeping a per-project breakdown as a secondary figure), or return both `projectUsage` and `organizationUsage` and meter the limits against the latter. Update usage.ts:42-45, docs/22:15 and frontend/app/usage/page.tsx:70 to match whichever is chosen.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, restated from the code. backend/src/routes/v1/usage.ts:55-61 calls the PROJECT-scoped aggregates (sumLlmTokensSince, countImagesSince, sumVideoSecondsSince, sumLlmCostUsdSince), whose SQL filters eq(usageRecords.projectId, projectId) — usage-record-repository.ts:209-225 (sumColumnSince) and :101-116 (countImagesSince). QuotaManager enforces against the TENANT-scoped aggregates only: quota-manager.ts:17-24 declares just sumLlmTokensForTenantSince/countImagesForTenantSince/sumVideoSecondsForTenantSince, and checkLlmTokens/checkImageGeneration/checkVideoSeconds (103-168) call them; those go through tenantProjects() (repository 155-168), an inArray over every project sharing the organizationId. So the route returns one project's spend and the same response's `limits` block is a ceiling enforced over the whole organization; the screen then divides one by the other (frontend/app/usage/page.tsx:75, pct = used/limit at :101).

Three claims the code no longer honours: usage.ts:44-45 ("every aggregate above and every QuotaManager check now filters on the project id" — the second clause is false since ADR-126), docs/22_COST_AND_QUOTA_STRATEGY.md:15 ("quota state and displayed usage can never disagree"), and frontend/app/usage/page.tsx:72 ("Everything this project has spent, for the selected project only"), which is true of the numerator and false of the denominator it is metered against.

Absence proven by grep: `grep -rn "ForTenantSince(" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v dist`, excluding packages/quota and the repository itself, returns nothing — no route or screen anywhere reports the totals the limits are actually enforced against. Not already fixed: `awk 'NR>=2078' docs/26_DECISIONS.md | grep "routes/v1/usage\|/api/v1/usage\|app/usage"` returns nothing (exit 1); ADR-126's Impact line (26_DECISIONS.md:2091) lists the repository, quota-manager, auth-service, auth.ts and docs/API.md, and ADR-127..ADR-144 never revisit the endpoint or the screen.

Why it survives green tests: backend/src/routes/v1/usage.test.ts runs against buildTestApp()'s single seeded project, and auth-service.ts:178-191 gives a new registration exactly one organization with exactly one project — with one project per org, project scope and tenant scope are the same set, so every assertion passes. The divergence needs 2+ projects in an org, which createProject supports (cap 100, auth-service.ts:749-795), POST /api/v1/projects exposes (auth.ts:195-213), and frontend/app/lib/app-chrome.tsx:64's selectProject switcher lets a user move between.

Corrections to the finding, none substantive: the repository line numbers drift (sumColumnSince is 209-225, not 196-206 — 196-207 is sumTenantColumnSince; the tenant aggregates are 170-194, not 165-190) and the frontend subtitle is page.tsx:72, not :70. The impact statement should also be scoped: a single-project organization, which is the state every new signup starts in, shows no discrepancy at all.

Severity stays P1, not raised or lowered. It is not exploitable and enforcement itself is correct — the error under-reports, so no charge is lost or duplicated — but the usage dashboard is a shipped, user-visible capability whose percentage and progress bar become arithmetic over two different denominators the moment an org holds a second project, and the 429's message names a running total ("199950 used so far today") that the screen never displays. P0 would overstate it (nothing is bypassable and no core capability is broken); P2 would understate a shipped screen that reports a wrong number against an explicit doc guarantee that it cannot.

confirmed.title: A cancelled provider call is counted as a success, directly contradicting the comment above it and ADR-132
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-132 exists because the old counters "showed a provider at 100% success during an outage". This reintroduces a milder version of the same dishonesty in the other direction: every user who hits Stop on a chat stream (ADR-123's stop button), and every cancelled agent node, increments `provider_request_count{status="success"}`. Provider success rate then tracks user behaviour, which is precisely what the ADR's "Cancellation is not failure" paragraph set out to avoid. No test catches it — `metrics.test.ts:70-71` only exercises `"error"` and `"timeout"`.
confirmed.fix: Return early for the counter when `call.status === "cancelled"` while still recording latency, e.g. split `recordProviderCall` into the counter and the histogram, or add an explicit `if (call.status !== "cancelled") recordProviderCall({...})` alongside an unconditional latency record. Add a metrics assertion that a cancelled call leaves `provider_request_count` unchanged.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the source. backend/src/index.ts:1124 is `status: call.status === "error" ? "error" : "success"` — a two-way ternary over a three-way union, so `cancelled` is counted as `success`, which is precisely what the three-line comment immediately above it (index.ts:1121-1123) says is NOT done and what ADR-132 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2172, "kept out of the success/error counter") promises. The cancelled status is genuinely produced, not theoretical: model-router/src/router.ts:65 declares `status: "success" | "error" | "cancelled"` and router.ts:355 does `settle(sawDone ? "success" : "cancelled")` inside the `finally` reached when a caller abandons the generator (router.test.ts exercises that path at the router level). recordProviderCall (observability/src/metrics.ts:178-189) types status as `"success" | "error" | "timeout"` and unconditionally increments `provider_request_count`, so the callsite is the only possible filter and it does not filter. The handler is the live one for chat: `grep -rn "onFallback\|onCall\|onRetry" backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts` returns only line 388 (onFallback), so router.ts:160's `callOptions.onCall ?? this.options.onCall` falls through to index.ts:1117 on every stop. Not already fixed: `git log -L1115,1130:backend/src/index.ts` shows the line landed in 6d92322 (the ADR-132 commit) and was never touched; grepping docs/26_DECISIONS.md past ADR-132 for "cancel" surfaces only ADR-140, which concerns parseSseStream reader release and VideoProjectStatus. Untested: `grep -rn "onCall" --include=*.ts backend/` (excluding node_modules/dist) hits only router.ts, router.test.ts and index.ts:1117, and metrics.test.ts:70-71 passes only "error" and "timeout". Severity P2, not higher: errors are still recorded as errors so an outage remains visible, only the denominator is inflated by user-initiated stops. The finding's `domain: "quota-billing"` tag is wrong — token/cost recording is in the separate `if (call.inputTokens !== undefined ...)` branch, and a stream abandoned before `done` carries no usage, so nothing is double-charged; the impact is a dishonest success rate only.

confirmed.title: `/api/v1/usage` reports no embedding or speech usage and no speech limits, and two repository aggregates have zero callers
confirmed.evidence: The response (usage.ts:64-76) carries `llm`, `images`, `video` and a `limits` block of exactly four fields; `getLimits()` returns eight (quota-manager.ts:45-56), so `dailySpeechCharacterLimit`, `monthlySpeechCharacterLimit` and both embedding limits are dropped. `grep -rn "sumEmbeddingTokensSince|sumSpeechCharactersSince" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/` returns only the two definitions (`usage-record-repository.ts:129` and `:134`) plus two prose mentions in `quota-manager.test.ts:47,54` — no call site anywhere, and neither method is declared on the `UsageRecordRepository` interface (usage-record-repository.ts:35-60). The frontend renders exactly the four meters it is given (frontend/app/usage/page.tsx:75-81).
confirmed.why_it_matters: A deployment that sets `DAILY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT` has a ceiling that returns 429 from `POST /api/v1/audio` (audio.ts:56) with a message naming a number that appears on no screen, and the Usage page shows no speech usage to explain it. Embedding spend — the largest single category once document ingestion runs (ADR-131's own argument) — is recorded in `usage_records` and reported nowhere at all, so the page's four meters are presented as the project's spend while silently omitting two of the five metered kinds.
confirmed.fix: Add `embedding` and `speech` usage blocks to the response using `sumEmbeddingTokensSince`/`sumSpeechCharactersSince` (declaring both on the `UsageRecordRepository` interface), include all eight fields from `getLimits()` in the `limits` block, and add the matching meters to `frontend/app/usage/page.tsx`.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED, restated from the code. usage.ts:55-76 awaits exactly five aggregates and returns usage.{llm,images,video} with a four-field limits block; getLimits() (quota-manager.ts:44-56, ~200) returns eight. `grep -rn "sumEmbeddingTokensSince|sumSpeechCharactersSince" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/` returns only the two definitions (usage-record-repository.ts:129,134) plus two prose mentions in quota-manager.test.ts:47,54 — no call site, and neither is on the UsageRecordRepository interface (lines 35-60). The orphaning cause the finding omits: ADR-126 moved quota onto the tenant-scoped variants (quota-manager.ts:128,178 bind sumEmbeddingTokensForTenantSince / sumSpeechCharactersForTenantSince), leaving ADR-119's per-project pair with the usage route as its only natural caller, which never adopted it. The data genuinely exists and is reported nowhere: speech rows are written at index.ts:913 (units = text.length), embedding rows at index.ts:445 and rag.ts:311. frontend/app/usage/page.tsx:14-25,75-81 types and renders exactly four meters, and `grep -rln "usage" frontend/app --include=*.tsx` returns only app-chrome.tsx and usage/page.tsx, so no other screen shows spend. No ADR addresses it — headings through ADR-144 in docs/26_DECISIONS.md cover enforcement (119/126) and recording (131), never the endpoint's response shape — and usage.test.ts:26-36 uses toMatchObject, so it is green and would stay green after a fix, which is why this survives the suite. The speech half of the impact holds exactly as written: .env.example:84-85 / config.ts:309-310 / index.ts:414-415 make DAILY_SPEECH_CHARACTER_LIMIT real, and audio.ts:56 throws QuotaExceededError naming a ceiling that appears on no screen beside usage that appears on no screen. One sub-claim is overstated and I am deducting for it rather than failing the finding: the two embedding limits are not meaningfully "dropped" — `grep EMBEDDING_TOKEN_LIMIT backend/src` returns nothing, config.ts defines no such variable and index.ts:410-417 never passes dailyEmbeddingTokenLimit/monthlyEmbeddingTokenLimit, so those two fields would serialize as null in every deployment anyway. P2 is right: the Usage page ships and works for the three kinds it covers, nothing is exploitable and no core capability is broken; it silently omits two of five metered kinds and two enforceable ceilings. (Separate, not this finding: usage.ts:42-47 still claims "every QuotaManager check now filters on the project id," which ADR-126 falsified — meters are per-project while enforcement is per-organization, so a meter can read under-limit while the request is refused.)

confirmed.title: The test named for speech dead-letter pricing always takes the 404 branch, so ADR-130's speech and video replay pricing is untested
confirmed.evidence: backend/src/routes/v1/spend-guards.test.ts, `it("refuses to replay a speech job when the speech budget is spent")`: it posts to `/api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/audio.generate.dlq/7d8f3c2e-.../replay` for an id that was never seeded, then asserts `expect([429, 404]).toContain(res.statusCode);`. The outcome is deterministic and it is 404: `getDeadLettered` (queue.ts:431-443) finds no row and returns `null`, so the route's audio branch `else if (sourceQueue === "audio.generate" && payload)` (platform.ts:243) is skipped entirely and `checkSpeechCharacters` never runs; `replayDeadLettered` then returns `null` (queue.ts:481) and the route throws `NotFoundError` (platform.ts:271). Even had the branch run, `characters = generation?.text.length ?? 0` would give `checkSpeechCharacters(projectId, 0)` against `dailySpeechCharacterLimit: 0`, and quota-manager.ts:186 evaluates `0 + 0 > 0` → false → allowed. There is no test anywhere for the `video.generate_scene` replay branch: `grep -rn "video.generate_scene" backend/src/routes/v1/spend-guards.test.ts backend/src/routes/v1/dead-letter.test.ts` returns nothing.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-130's headline claim is that "replaying a speech job or a video scene went through no budget at all" was fixed and "the referenced row is read and priced on what will really be re-run". The green suite contains no test that a real speech or video dead letter is ever priced — the one that carries the name passes on an assertion that accepts both outcomes and always gets the one that proves nothing. A regression that deleted the `audio.generate` and `video.generate_scene` branches from platform.ts:243-262 would leave the whole suite green.
confirmed.fix: Seed a real dead letter (an `audio.generate.dlq` row whose `data.projectId` matches and whose `generationId` points at a seeded audio generation with non-empty text) and assert a hard 429, then the mirror case for `video.generate_scene.dlq` with a seeded scene. Assert the exact status, not a set.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED, and I reproduced it. backend/src/routes/v1/spend-guards.test.ts:202-217 ("refuses to replay a speech job when the speech budget is spent") posts to /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/audio.generate.dlq/7d8f3c2e-1b4a-4c6d-9e8f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/replay for an id that is never seeded and asserts expect([429, 404]).toContain(res.statusCode). I ran a throwaway copy of that test (since deleted) with ctx.quota.checkSpeechCharacters wrapped in a counter: the run produced status=404 with NotFoundError thrown from backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:269, and the counter was 0. The speech pricing branch never executes. The mechanism is exactly as described: queue.ts:429-443 (getDeadLettered) and queue.ts:472-481 (replayDeadLettered) both require `state in ('created','retry')` and a matching data->>'projectId', so an unseeded id returns null from both; platform.ts:243 guards the audio branch with `&& payload`, so a null payload skips checkSpeechCharacters entirely, and the route then 404s. The finding's secondary point also holds: even with the branch entered at 0 characters, quota-manager.ts:181 evaluates 0 + 0 > 0 as false, so a zero limit would allow it. Absence re-proven with my own greps: "dead-letter" occurs in only three test files repo-wide (backend/src/routes/v1/spend-guards.test.ts, backend/packages/jobs/src/dead-letter.test.ts, backend/src/routes/api-contract.test.ts); backend/packages/jobs/src/dead-letter.test.ts contains no quota/pricing test (naming, DLQ movement, cross-project refusal, live-queue refusal, double-replay refusal, payload scoping); "video.generate_scene" appears in tests only in backend/packages/media/src/video-pipeline.integration.test.ts (queue send counts, not the replay route). No ADR after 130 through ADR-144 mentions replay or dead letters, so nothing later fixed this. Consequence as stated: deleting the audio.generate and video.generate_scene branches at platform.ts:243-262 would leave the suite green, so the pricing half of ADR-130 ("the referenced row is read and priced on what will really be re-run") has no regression guard. Two corrections. (1) The finding's grep cites backend/src/routes/v1/dead-letter.test.ts, which does not exist — the file is backend/packages/jobs/src/dead-letter.test.ts; the absence claim survives under a correct grep. (2) The shipped route is itself correct for a real dead letter — payload keys match the producers (audio.ts:67 enqueues generationId; video-orchestration.ts:175 enqueues projectId/videoProjectId/sceneId) and AudioGenerationRepository.get is the project-scoped read — so this is a test-coverage defect, not an exploitable fail-open. P2 is the right severity: it does not break a shipped capability today, it only removes the evidence that the capability works. Strictly, the test is not literally incapable of failing (a route that stopped 404-ing on unknown ids would fail it); its defect is that the assertion it does make is the same one already covered at spend-guards.test.ts:219-228, while the property in its name is never exercised.

confirmed.title: The audio and video-scene workers lack the ADR-128 'already terminal' guard, so a re-claimed job pays the provider twice with no ledger trace
confirmed.evidence:
`processImageGeneration` got the guard (backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:69: `if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return;`, with ADR-128's reasoning in the comment above it). `processAudioGeneration` (audio-generation.ts:45-56) checks only `generation.cancelRequestedAt` and then goes straight to `updateStatus(..., "processing")` and `deps.speech.synthesize(...)` — `grep -n 'status === "succeeded"' backend/packages/media/src/audio-generation.ts` returns nothing. `processVideoScene` (video-orchestration.ts:208-229) is the same: it checks `project?.cancelRequestedAt` and nothing about the scene's own terminal status before calling `deps.provider.generateVideo`. The queues are `audio.generate` with `expireInSeconds: 300` (backend/src/index.ts:565) and `video.generate_scene` with `900` (index.ts:574), both `retryLimit: 1`.
The ledger cannot show the second charge: the usage rows are keyed `audio.generate:${generationId}` (index.ts:917) and `video.scene:${sceneId}` (index.ts:1000), and `PgUsageRecordRepository.create` does `onConflictDoNothing` and returns the existing row (usage-record-repository.ts:66-78).
confirmed.why_it_matters: This is ADR-128's exact analysis — "the usage row's idempotency key made it worse to find than to have: it deduplicated the BILLING RECORD, so the second charge was invisible in the ledger while the provider had still been called and paid twice" — applied to the two queues ADR-128 did not revisit. The case that survives the widened window is the one ADR-128 names as the reason to keep the guard anyway: a worker that finished synthesis, stored the asset and marked the row `succeeded` but died before pg-boss completed the job. It is then re-claimed, and 5000 characters of hosted TTS or a full scene clip are bought a second time, with the ledger showing one.
confirmed.fix: Add the same early return to both: `if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return ...;` in `processAudioGeneration` before `updateStatus("processing")`, and the scene-status equivalent in `processVideoScene`. Cover each with the re-claim test shape ADR-128 used for images (`backend/packages/media/src/job-deadlines.test.ts`).
confirmed.verdict: Verified from the files, not the names. backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:70 carries the ADR-128 guard (`if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return;`) under a comment that cites ADR-128 by name. A grep for `status === "succeeded"`/`status === "cancelled"` across the three media workers returns only that line plus video-orchestration.ts:156 (a project-level guard inside `orchestrateVideoProject`, NOT the scene worker) and two counting lines in `checkProjectCompletion`. `processAudioGeneration` (audio-generation.ts:46-57) returns only on `cancelRequestedAt`, then goes straight to `updateStatus(..., "processing", {incrementAttempt: true})` and `deps.speech.synthesize(...)`. `processVideoScene` (video-orchestration.ts:203-231) returns only on `project?.cancelRequestedAt`, then `updateStatus(..., "processing")` and `deps.provider.generateVideo(...)`. Neither repository backs a guard in SQL: `PgAudioGenerationRepository.updateStatus` (audio-generation-repository.ts:96-115) and `PgVideoSceneRepository.updateStatus` (video-scene-repository.ts:100-122) are unconditional UPDATEs scoped only by id and tenant, so a `succeeded` row is driven back to `processing`. Both queues can re-claim: `audio.generate {retryLimit:1, expireInSeconds:300}` (index.ts:565) and `video.generate_scene {retryLimit:1, expireInSeconds:900}` (index.ts:574). The ledger cannot show the second charge: keys `audio.generate:${generationId}` (index.ts:921) and `video.scene:${sceneId}` (index.ts ~997) go through `PgUsageRecordRepository.create`, which does `onConflictDoNothing({target: idempotencyKey})` and returns the pre-existing row (usage-record-repository.ts:65-78). `grep -rn "processAudioGeneration|processVideoScene"` over backend/frontend/shared (excluding tests and dist) shows exactly one caller each, the queue workers at index.ts:878 and index.ts:938, with no status pre-check above them. Not already fixed: ADR-128 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2108) scopes itself to `image.generate` and `video.render`, ADR-129..ADR-144 never revisit these two workers, and job-deadlines.test.ts contains one re-claim describe block ("a re-claimed image job does not pay twice") with no audio or scene equivalent. Two points the finding understates: (a) a re-claimed run that FAILS overwrites the `succeeded` row with `failed` (audio-generation.ts:92-99), and a re-claimed run that succeeds overwrites `resultAssetId` with a second asset, orphaning the first — so it is not only a double charge, it destroys a good result; (b) the video half has a plausible non-crash overrun path, since video-replicate's `DEFAULT_DEADLINE_MS = 10*60_000` leaves 300s under the 900s window while the SAME job then runs narration synthesis (speech default timeoutMs 120_000) plus two asset uploads — the justifying comment at index.ts:566-573 says "room left for the download and the cancel" and does not account for the narration stage ADR-079 put in this job. Line-number drift only: the guard is at image-generation.ts:70 (not 69), the audio gap at 46-57, the video usage key near index.ts:997. Severity stays P2: it needs a worker death/restart between the terminal write and pg-boss completion (or an overrun), so it is not exploitable on demand and no shipped capability is broken in normal operation — but when it fires, provider money is spent twice with the ledger showing one charge.

confirmed.title: video.render's claim window is sized for ONE ffmpeg call while a render makes 2N+4 of them — a long-form render is re-claimed and composed twice
confirmed.evidence: backend/src/index.ts:576-582 sets `expireInSeconds: Math.ceil(DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000) + 300` = 900 + 300 = 1200s, with the comment "ffmpeg is now killed at DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS; this sits above it with room for the upload and the database write that follow." That comment describes a render that is one ffmpeg call. `grep -n "await ffmpeg(\[" backend/packages/media/src/video-render.ts` returns EIGHT call sites: 200 (normalise, per scene), 257 (tpad to slot, per scene), 278 (video concat), 315/329 (one audio segment per scene), 350 (audio concat), 363 (mux), 400 (subtitle mux) — i.e. 2N+4 to 3N+4 invocations per render, each independently allowed 900s by `const ffmpeg = (args) => runFfmpeg(ffmpegPath, args, deps.ffmpegTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS)` (video-render.ts:131). `grep -rn "ffmpegTimeoutMs" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/` returns only the declaration (video-render.ts:78) and that default — no caller, including backend/src/index.ts:1007-1014, ever sets it. `videoProjectRequestSchema` (shared/src/video.ts:56-60) allows targetDurationSeconds up to 1800 with sceneClipSeconds as low as 2, so N reaches 900 and a render can be ~2704 ffmpeg invocations inside a 1200s window. `processVideoRender` has no terminal-state guard: video-render.ts:132 reads the project and video-render.ts:139 writes `renderStatus: "processing"` unconditionally — there is no equivalent of image-generation.ts:70 (`if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return;`), which ADR-128 added for exactly this. No test covers a re-claimed render: `grep -n "it(" backend/packages/media/src/video-pipeline.integration.test.ts` shows guards for concurrent completion checks and for retries, none for a re-delivered render job.
confirmed.why_it_matters: pg-boss makes an `active` job claimable again after `expireInSeconds` (backend/packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:47-50), and `video.render` has `retryLimit: 1`, so one re-claim happens. Two workers then compose the same project concurrently: duplicate CPU, two `assetStore.store(... "video/mp4" ...)` calls (video-render.ts:442) so one final MP4 becomes an orphan asset nothing references, and the second worker's `updateRender(renderStatus: "processing")` at line 139 overwrites the first worker's `succeeded` — a user watching the detail page sees the finished video disappear back into a spinner. This is the same defect ADR-128 fixed for `image.generate` and for a single ffmpeg call, left open one level up.
confirmed.fix: Give `processVideoRender` the ADR-128 guard (return immediately when `project.renderStatus === "succeeded"`, or claim the run with a conditional UPDATE the way `claimRenderSlot` does), and size `video.render`'s `expireInSeconds` against a whole-render budget rather than a single invocation — or bound the render as a whole (one deadline shared across all eight call sites) so the worker always gives up before pg-boss re-claims it.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — I can restate it from the code. backend/src/index.ts:576-582 sets video.render's expireInSeconds to Math.ceil(DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS/1000)+300 = 1200s with retryLimit: 1, and its comment ("ffmpeg is now killed at DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS; this sits above it with room for the upload and the database write that follow") describes a render that is a single ffmpeg call. It is not one call: video-render.ts:78 documents ffmpegTimeoutMs as the ceiling for "any ONE ffmpeg invocation", line 131 binds it per call, and there are eight `await ffmpeg([...])` sites (200, 257, 278, 315, 329, 350, 363, 400), five of them inside per-scene loops — 2N+4 to 3N+4 invocations per render, each independently allowed 900s, with no whole-render deadline anywhere. `grep -rn "ffmpegTimeoutMs" --include=*.ts .` (excluding node_modules and /dist/) returns only the declaration (78) and the default (131): no caller sets it, including the worker at index.ts:1007-1014. N is uncapped — video-storyboard.ts:22 computes Math.ceil(targetDurationSeconds / sceneClipSeconds) and shared/src/video.ts bounds those at 1800 and 2, so N reaches 900. Total render wall-clock is therefore unbounded against a fixed 1200s claim window.

The guard is genuinely missing, and this is not something a prior ADR closed. processVideoRender reads the project at video-render.ts:132 and writes `renderStatus: "processing"` unconditionally at line 139; there is no equivalent of image-generation.ts:70 (`if (generation.status === "succeeded" || generation.status === "cancelled") return;`). ADR-128's decision line does say "a job that reached a terminal state is never redone", but its own prose ("so `processImageGeneration` returns immediately...") and its Impact confine the guard to images, and job-deadlines.test.ts matches: its three re-claim tests all drive processImageGeneration, while its video describe-block only exercises runFfmpegForTest's per-invocation deadline. claimRenderSlot (video-orchestration.ts:319) is not this guard either — it is a conditional UPDATE that de-duplicates the ENQUEUE among concurrently-settling scene workers, and it does not run when pg-boss re-delivers an already-claimed job. Re-claim on expiry is real in this repo, not theoretical: queue.test.ts:156-178 hangs a worker past expireInSeconds against real pg-boss and asserts a second worker picks the job up. And video.render's worker at index.ts:1007 is registered unconditionally, unlike video.generate_scene at 927 which sits behind `if (videoProvider)`, so it runs wherever the worker role runs. Consequence as reported: two concurrent full composes, a second assetStore.store(..., "video/mp4", ...) at video-render.ts:442 producing an MP4 asset no renderAssetId points at, and renderStatus thrash between processing and succeeded.

Two overstatements, neither fatal. (1) The title's "double-charges paid work" is wrong: ADR-130 explicitly leaves video.render ungated because "they spend CPU on work already generated, not a provider call", so no money is double-spent — the body correctly limits the cost to duplicate CPU and an orphan asset. (2) The specific interleaving claimed ("the second worker's processing overwrites the first's succeeded — the finished video disappears back into a spinner") is only one of two orderings; the second worker's `processing` write lands at re-claim time, generally before the still-running first worker's `succeeded`, in which case the damage is the orphaned MP4 from the second worker's later succeeded write instead.
