What actually survives is narrower than reported: the only seam no test drives is api.ts:175's path/body against the route, because statusOfEnableCall hardcodes the correct URL and body instead of exercising the app's own client. I checked both sides and they agree today — `/api/v1/tools/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/enable` with {enabled} matches backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:117 and enableToolSchema at line 98 — so nothing is broken now; a future drift there would pass both suites. ADR-144 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2314-2326) states this spec's contract as four checks (member not offered, admin offered, member 404, admin 200), none of which is pressing the button, so the spec meets its documented intent. Real as a comment-versus-code defect and a coverage seam worth knowing about; not a defect in a shipped capability, hence INFORMATIONAL rather than P2. The suggested fix (replace the raw-fetch state change with `await enable.click()` and keep statusOfEnableCall for the pure 404/200 authorization assertions) is still the right change.

confirmed.title: `/api/v1/mcp` returns `refusedToolIds` and `transport` "so an operator can see", and no interface reads either
confirmed.evidence: platform.ts:133 `// Which wire it came up on — stdio, Streamable HTTP, or the deprecated SSE fallback.` -> `transport: server.transport,` and lines 137-140 `// Tools this server offered and was refused because the id was already taken. Shown, not just logged: on a remote server that is what a name-squatting attempt looks like, and a boot-time log line is not where anyone goes looking for it.` -> `refusedToolIds: server.refusedToolIds,`. `grep -rn "refusedToolIds" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx frontend` returns nothing at all. `grep -rn "transport" --include=*.tsx frontend/app` returns only an unrelated comment in chat/ChatView.tsx:100. The frontend's `McpRow` (frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:39-44) declares only `id`, `status`, `toolCount`, `error` — the Platform screen is the sole consumer of this route.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-083's stated defence is that an id collision is "refused rather than resolved" AND "reported on `/api/v1/mcp` so an operator can see what a server tried to claim". Half of that is built: the refusal happens (client.ts:142-149), it is carried through the manager, it is serialised by the route — and it stops at the wire. A remote MCP server attempting to squat `mcp.a.b.read` produces a warn log at boot and an API field nobody renders, so in practice the detection is log-only, which is precisely what the comment says is not good enough. Same for `transport`: the SSE fallback is recorded distinctly "worth being able to see in /api/v1/mcp before the SDK drops it", and it is not visible anywhere.
confirmed.fix: Render both on the Platform screen's MCP list item — the transport as a label next to the status, and a non-empty `refusedToolIds` as a warning row naming the ids. Add them to `McpRow`.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code, not inferred. backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:127-145 serialises `transport` (line 134) and `refusedToolIds` (line 140), the latter under a comment stating it is "Shown, not just logged: … a boot-time log line is not where anyone goes looking for it." The machinery behind it is real: packages/mcp/src/client.ts:141-149 pushes the colliding id and emits a warn; manager.ts:205 carries it through; manager.ts:215 logs only a count, never the ids. Consumer absence proven by grep: `grep -rn "refusedToolIds" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx .` (excluding node_modules) yields 16 hits, all in backend/packages/mcp plus the one route line, zero in frontend/; `grep -rn "transport" frontend` yields only three unrelated comment/test lines; `grep -rn "v1/mcp" frontend` shows frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:101 as the sole consumer of the listing. That page's McpRow (lines 39-44) declares only id/status/toolCount/error and its render block (lines 240-269) prints id, status, tool count, error and the ADR-144 Reconnect button — neither field appears. ADR-083 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1321) states the defence as "both the transport and any refused ids are reported on /api/v1/mcp so an operator can see what a server tried to claim"; `grep -rn "refusedToolIds" docs/` returns nothing and no ADR through ADR-144 (tip commit) fixes it, so it is not already addressed. Impact follows as stated but no further: the refusal is enforced server-side, so there is no bypass — what is missing is the operator-facing half, making name-squatting detection log-only. P2 is correct; not P1, because no shipped user-facing capability is broken and no authorization boundary is weakened. Adjacent corroboration (not in the finding): the page renders `server.error` while the route emits `lastError` (platform.ts:141, no frontend `lastError` usage for MCP), so a failed server's error text is also never shown — the row is consuming a shape the route does not emit, which explains how the omissions survived typechecking.

confirmed.title: `PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` is dead: no test imports it, and it omits 5 of the 13 routes it claims to fully describe
confirmed.evidence: The docstring at lines 336-344 says "exported so a test can assert the surface is protected" and "It is spelled out here anyway so this table describes the whole surface: a route missing from it reads as unprotected, and silently omitting the admin routes would make the strongest guard the least visible." `grep -rn "PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx .` (excluding node_modules) returns exactly three hits: the definition at platform.ts:345, the generated `backend/dist/routes/v1/platform.d.ts:27`, and a prose mention in frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx:156. No test file imports it. The table holds 8 keys; `registerPlatformRoutes` registers 13 routes — missing are `GET /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter` (line 195), `POST /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/:queue/:id/replay` (line 212), and all three admin routes `GET /api/v1/admin/health` (290), `/admin/metrics` (320), `/admin/stats` (330).
confirmed.why_it_matters: Two claims in one docstring, neither honoured. The table is inert — nothing derives an assertion from it, so it cannot fail when a route is added without a guard. And the routes it does omit are exactly the ones the comment says must not be omitted: all three `/admin/*` routes. The new frontend list `SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES` (session-context.tsx:164-170) names `/api/v1/admin/health`, `/admin/metrics` and `/admin/stats` and calls itself "the frontend's half of a boundary ... (`requireSystemAdmin` ..., and the authority table `PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` beside it)" — but the backend half does not list those three at all, and nothing cross-checks the two lists, so they can drift silently in either direction.
confirmed.fix: Add the five missing entries, then write the test the docstring promises: enumerate `app.printRoutes()` (or the router's registered urls) for this module and assert every one appears in the table, and that each `system-admin` entry answers 404 to a non-admin session.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed on all counts from the source. platform.ts:336-344 claims the table is "exported so a test can assert the surface is protected" and that "a route missing from it reads as unprotected, and silently omitting the admin routes would make the strongest guard the least visible." Neither claim holds. (1) A repo-wide grep for PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS returns only three hits — the definition at platform.ts:345, the generated backend/dist/routes/v1/platform.d.ts:27, and a prose mention at frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx:156. No test imports it, so nothing derives an assertion from it and it cannot fail when a route is added. (2) grep -n "app\.\(get\|post\|put\|patch\|delete\)" on the file yields exactly 13 registrations (lines 24, 45, 82, 117, 127, 147, 168, 181, 195, 212, 290, 320, 330) against 8 table keys; the five missing are exactly the ones named — GET /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter (195), POST /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/:queue/:id/replay (212), and all three /admin/* routes (290, 320, 330), i.e. precisely the category the docstring says must not be omitted. (3) The asymmetry with the frontend is real: SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES (session-context.tsx:164) IS enforced — session-context.admin.test.tsx imports and walks it at lines 5, 71, 110 — while the backend half it cites at line 156 is not, and nothing cross-checks the two. (4) ADR-144 does not address this; I read it in full — it adds SystemAdminOnly, the frontend source-walk test and admin-boundary.spec.ts, touching session-context.tsx, api.ts, two pages and package.json, with no backend test over the table. It only references the table in the comment that now misdescribes it. Severity stays P2 rather than higher because there is no live hole: grep -n "requireProject(\|requireSystemAdmin(" returns 13 guard calls, one per route (28, 46, 83, 118, 128, 155, 169, 182, 196, 218, 291, 321, 331), so every route including the five omitted ones is actually guarded. This is inert machinery and an unhonoured comment claim — a drift detector that cannot detect drift — not an exploitable bypass, and the finding's why_it_matters correctly stops short of claiming one. Minor correction: the finding's own grep shape would have missed the generic app.post<{...}>( registrations, but its route count and its list of omissions are nonetheless correct.

confirmed.title: An MCP `tools/call` is issued with no timeout and is never cancelled, so the registry's per-tool timeout is not the effective bound
confirmed.evidence: client.ts:177 `const result = (await client.callTool({ name: tool.name, arguments: args })) as {...}` — no options object, so no `timeout`. The same file passes one everywhere else: `client.listTools(undefined, { timeout: requestTimeoutMs })` at line 135, and manager.ts:268 for the health probe. `node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/shared/protocol.js:8` defines `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC = 60000` and line 712 applies `options?.timeout ?? DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC`. The registry bounds the call at `entry.definition.timeoutMs` (backend/packages/tools/src/registry.ts:287-291) via a `Promise.race` that only abandons the promise — its own docstring at registry.ts:79-80 admits "A timeout here still only bounds the *promise*; killing the underlying work is the sandbox's job". For MCP tools `timeoutMs` comes from `PERMISSION_LEVEL_DEFAULTS` (client.ts:152): 30_000 for `read_only` and `write_local` (shared/src/tools.ts:38,42), against the SDK's 60_000. `retryPolicy.idempotencyRequired` is set only for `destructive`/`financial` (client.ts:168), and `handleNodeFailure` in backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:1226 retries on the default `retryable-execution` class up to `maxAttempts` (2 for `write_local`).
confirmed.why_it_matters: There is a 30-second window in which the platform has declared an MCP tool call failed while the remote is still executing it, with no `notifications/cancelled` sent (the SDK only emits one when ITS timer fires, at 60s). For a name-inferred `write_local` MCP tool — `write_file`, `edit_file`, `create_*`, per `inferPermissionLevel` at client.ts:422 — the caller above is allowed a second attempt with no idempotency requirement, so a slow remote write can be applied twice. The registry's class docstring (registry.ts:76-77) claims it "genuinely owns validation, approval policy, the enabled check and the timeout"; for MCP the timeout it owns is not the one the remote obeys.
confirmed.fix: Pass the tool's own bound through to the SDK: capture `definition.timeoutMs` in the closure and call `client.callTool({name, arguments: args}, undefined, { timeout: definition.timeoutMs })`, so the SDK's timer fires first and sends the spec's cancellation notification to the remote.
confirmed.verdict: Verified in the code, not inferred. backend/packages/mcp/src/client.ts:177 is the repo's only `callTool` (grep -rn "callTool" --include=*.ts backend, excluding node_modules, returns exactly that one line) and passes no RequestOptions, so the SDK falls back to DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC = 60000 (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/shared/protocol.js:8, applied at :712), while the same file passes an explicit timeout to listTools at client.ts:135 and manager.ts:268 does the same for the health probe. The registry bounds the call at definition.timeoutMs via a Promise.race (registry.ts:286-291) whose own docstring (registry.ts:79-80) concedes it only bounds the promise, and the MCP handler is `async (args) => ...` — it never accepts the ToolInvocationContext, so neither the registry's signal nor the node deadline's controller.abort (engine.ts:1148) can reach the in-flight request. For MCP tools timeoutMs comes from PERMISSION_LEVEL_DEFAULTS (client.ts:152/164): 30_000 for read_only and write_local (shared/src/tools.ts). So there is a 30s window in which the platform has declared failure while the remote is still working and no notifications/cancelled has been sent. The re-execution follows: the registry's timeout surfaces as {ok:false}, engine.ts:581 routes that to handleNodeFailure with the default "retryable-execution" class, which retries while attempts < maxAttempts (2 for write_local) and schedules it at engine.ts:1276-1291 for the listDueForRetry sweep at engine.ts:1386; separately engine.ts:806-818 hands the timeout string back to the model in the reasoning loop, which can re-issue the same write. inferPermissionLevel (client.ts:422) maps write|create|move|rename|edit to write_local, so mutating remote tools are precisely the ones with maxAttempts 2. No ADR addresses it: grep -n "callTool\|tools/call" docs/26_DECISIONS.md has no hits, and the MCP ADRs (019, 021, 067, 083, 089, 136, 143, 144) cover trust level, lifecycle, transport, id collisions and UI gating only. One correction to the finding's reasoning: retryPolicy.idempotencyRequired is dead — grep -rn "idempotencyRequired" over backend/shared/frontend shows only assignments and test fixtures, never a read — so it would not have prevented the retry either way; maxAttempts alone permits it. Severity stays P2 rather than P1 because reaching it requires an operator-configured MCP server, an explicit system-admin enable (tools register enabled:false, ADR-083/144) and a remote slower than 30s, so it is a real defect in a shipped path but not exploitable on a default deployment.

confirmed.title: The live agent-task SSE stream is an in-process EventEmitter, but the API runs up to 3 Cloud Run instances with no session affinity — the stream silently delivers nothing
confirmed.evidence: backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:187 `private readonly events = new EventEmitter();` and :204-211 `subscribe(taskId, listener) { this.events.on(taskId, listener) }` / `emit(taskId, event) { this.events.emit(taskId, event) }`. The engine runs IN the api process: backend/src/role.ts `case "api": return { http: true, workers: false }` with the comment "api: HTTP server, agent engine, MCP", and engine.ts:246-255 `void withSpan("agent.run", ..., () => this.runExclusive(task.id, () => this.planAndExecute(...)))` — the run executes in whichever instance served `POST /api/v1/agent/tasks`. The browser then opens `GET /api/v1/agent/tasks/:id/events` as a SEPARATE request (frontend/app/lib/use-task-events.ts:64-70, `new EventSource(url)`), which Cloud Run routes independently: infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:265-276 `resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service" "api"` with `min_instance_count = 0`, `max_instance_count = 3`. Proof of absence: `grep -rn "session_affinity" infrastructure/terraform/` → no matches; `grep -rn "Redis|pubsub|NOTIFY|LISTEN" backend/packages/agent-core/src backend/src --include=*.ts` → only three hits, all in backend/src/plugins/rate-limit-store.ts comments about why the RATE LIMITER is not Redis, none about the event bus; `grep -n "setInterval|setTimeout|poll" frontend/app/agent/*.tsx frontend/app/lib/use-task-events.ts` → no matches, so there is no polling fallback. docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md documents the per-instance SANDBOX and PGlite caveats but says nothing about the event bus (`grep -rn "instance" docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md` returns only the PGlite and sandbox rows).
confirmed.why_it_matters: On the only documented production topology this fails roughly (N-1)/N of the time and fails SILENTLY. The route replays `state` plus the current `node` rows (agent.ts:145-148) so the page looks healthy, then `ctx.engine.subscribe(task.id, send)` attaches to an emitter in the wrong process that will never fire for that task id. The user watches a task sit at EXECUTING forever with an empty Activity card and no error anywhere; because the TCP connection is perfectly healthy, EventSource never even reconnects, so it cannot self-heal. This is the fail-silent shape ADR-134 and ADR-142 were written to remove, reintroduced by the transport rather than the UI.
confirmed.fix: Either pin the live stream to a single instance (set `session_affinity = true` on the Cloud Run service AND route the subscribe to the owning instance — affinity alone does not guarantee the POST and the GET share an instance), or make the bus cross-instance: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY keyed by task id is already available (the deployment has Cloud SQL) and the `subscribe`/`emit` pair in engine.ts:204-211 is the whole coupling surface. Failing that, add a `?since=` polling fallback in `useTaskEvents` and state the single-instance constraint in docs/27_RISKS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md.
confirmed.verdict: Verified from source. engine.ts:187 is a bare in-process EventEmitter; subscribe/emit (204-211) are the whole bus and agent.ts:153 is its only non-test caller. The run is detached in whichever process served the POST (engine.ts:246-255) and the engine lives in the api role (role.ts). The SSE GET is an independent request, and main.tf:265-276 gives the api service min=0/max=3 instances. Proofs of absence hold: `grep -rn session_affinity infrastructure/terraform/*.tf` -> no match; `grep -rln "LISTEN|NOTIFY|pubsub|ioredis|createClient" backend/src backend/packages --include=*.ts` -> no match; use-task-events.ts has no polling and an intentionally empty onerror; docs/27 records the PGlite and SANDBOX_ROOT per-instance caveats but nothing about the event bus, and no ADR in docs/26 covers it. So the defect is real: the live stream silently requires the POST and the GET to share a process and nothing guarantees that. Severity lowered from P1 because the finding overstates impact three ways. (1) No max_instance_request_concurrency is set, so Cloud Run's default is 80 concurrent requests per instance with min=0/max=3 — under this product's light single-operator load both requests normally hit the one warm instance; it breaks on scale-out or instance recycling, not "(N-1)/N of the time". (2) The page is not permanently blind: the route replays state plus node rows on connect and TaskDetail.tsx:243 falls back to persistedActivityOf(nodes), so any reload shows real state and the persisted activity log — what is lost is liveness, not data. (3) The Cloud Run topology has never been deployed (docs/27 line 19, ADR-011: cloud deployment is IaC-only pending authorization); the topology actually shipped and run is single-process ROLE=all, where the bus is correct. Real defect, latent in an unshipped topology, undocumented where every sibling per-instance constraint is documented: P2.

confirmed.title: A finished agent run's persisted activity log is never rendered — `persistedActivityOf` is reachable only from the coding variant, contradicting ADR-134
confirmed.evidence:
TaskDetail.tsx:149 `{activity.length > 0 && (
Activity...` — the Activity card renders the LIVE feed only. `activity` comes from `useTaskEvents` (TaskDetail.tsx:28), which starts as `useState([])` (use-task-events.ts:60) and is only ever appended to by the `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`verification` SSE listeners; the endpoint replays only `state` and `node` (backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:145-148), so for a task opened after it finished `activity` is `[]` and the card does not render at all. `grep -rn "persistedActivityOf" frontend/app/` returns exactly two hits: TaskDetail.tsx:315 (its definition) and TaskDetail.tsx:243 (`const entries = activity.length > 0 ? activity : persistedActivityOf(nodes)`), inside `CodingTabs`, which is rendered only by TaskDetail.tsx:198 `{variant === "coding" && }`. frontend/app/agent/[id]/page.tsx:22 passes `variant="agent"`. The data itself exists: backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:960-974 persists `activity` onto the reasoning node's output with the comment "Persisted beside the answer, so 'what did this run do' is answerable after the fact and not only while someone happened to be watching (ADR-134)".
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-134's stated decision is "...persisted on the node as an activity log; the task screen renders them" and "The log is written beside the answer rather than streamed-only, so 'what did this run do' is answerable after the fact". For the autonomous/agent variant — the primary one — that is false: the rows are written to `node.output.activity` on every run and nothing on /agent/[id] ever reads them. An operator or auditor opening a completed autonomous task sees the plan and the final answer and no record of which tools ran with what arguments, which is exactly the black box the ADR says it closed. The parser to render it is already written, one `variant` check away.
confirmed.fix: In TaskDetail.tsx compute the entries once for both consumers — `const entries = activity.length > 0 ? activity : persistedActivityOf(nodes)` at component scope — and drive both the Activity card (line 149/155) and `CodingTabs` from it, so a finished run of either variant reads the persisted log.
confirmed.verdict: Restated from the code. TaskDetail.tsx:149 gates the Activity card on `activity.length > 0` and renders only that array; `activity` originates at use-task-events.ts:60 as `useState([])` and is appended solely by the tool_call/tool_result/verification SSE listeners — it is never seeded from `initialNodes`, unlike `task` and `nodesById`. The SSE endpoint's replay (backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:145-148) sends only one `state` event and one `node` event per node, so a task opened after it finished has `activity === []` and the card does not render at all. `grep -rn "persistedActivityOf" frontend/` returns exactly two hits: its definition (TaskDetail.tsx:315) and one call (TaskDetail.tsx:243) inside `CodingTabs`, which renders only under `{variant === "coding"}` (TaskDetail.tsx:198). frontend/app/agent/[id]/page.tsx:22 passes variant="agent", and frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx:44 routes everything except `fix_failing_test` there — so every autonomous run lands on the variant that never reads the persisted log. The data is really written (engine.ts:982 on success, :1266 on failure, with the ADR-134 comment). Not already fixed: ADR-134 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2188) claims "persisted on the node as an activity log; the task screen renders them" and "answerable after the fact"; ADR-142 (:2298) wired only the coding tabs to it; ADR-143/144 are unrelated; the in-flight ADR-145 references concern persisting on failure and tool-argument mistakes, not rendering. The green suite cannot catch it: TaskDetail.test.tsx:218 exercises the persisted path only with variant="coding", and every agent-variant activity test injects hookResult.activity directly with initialNodes=[]. Severity held at P1 rather than P0 because the run still completes and the plan and final answer render; what is broken is the post-hoc tool audit trail that is ADR-134's stated purpose, on the primary variant, with the parser already written.

confirmed.title: A provider that fails partway through a chat stream is recorded as a SUCCESS: no ERROR span, no error log, no usage row, no stored message
confirmed.evidence: backend/packages/model-router/src/router.ts:233-247: once a provider has committed (`this.recordSuccess(provider.name)`), a later `iterator.next()` throw is converted into an in-band event — `yield { type: "error", message: `The model provider failed partway through responding: ...` }; return;` — it is NOT thrown. chat.ts:414-417 handles it as an ordinary non-terminal event: `if (event.type !== "done") { send(event); continue; }`. The router then returns, the `for await` ends normally, `completed` stays false and `abort.signal.aborted` is false, so chat.ts:530 `if (abort.signal.aborted && !completed) logCancelled()` does nothing and the `catch` at :531 is never entered. Consequence: the span keeps `"gen_ai.system": "unknown"` from :360 and OK status (the `span.setAttributes` at :502 and `span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR })` at :544 are both in branches that are not reached); the `status: "error"` log line at :545-548 is never written; `ctx.messages.add` (:430) and `ctx.usage.create` (:445) are never reached. The comment at chat.ts:540-542 states the contract this path violates: "the span must still reflect ERROR, or a real failure would misleadingly read as a successful `gen_ai.chat` call in any trace view." No test covers it: `grep -rn "partway" backend/ frontend/ --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (excluding node_modules) returns only router.ts:243 itself, and there is no chat-route test file for the streaming path (`grep -rln "api/v1/chat" backend/src --include=*.test.ts` → chat-summary, memory-extraction, memory, usage only).
confirmed.why_it_matters: This is the exact failure mode ADR-044 and ADR-132 exist to make visible, and it is invisible. The provider has already streamed and billed real tokens (the router's own `settle("error", ...)` at router.ts:349 confirms the call happened), yet no `usage` ledger row is written — so the spend is lost from FR-061/FR-063 quota accounting and from cost attribution, silently under-billing in exactly the direction ADR-098 called out as "loses money quietly". Meanwhile the trace view and the request log both report a clean 200, so a provider degrading mid-stream produces zero signal for an operator.
confirmed.fix: Treat the router's in-band `error` event as terminal in the chat loop: on `event.type === "error"`, set the span status to ERROR and record the exception, emit the `status: "error"` log line, write a usage row for whatever the router reported through `onCall`, and persist the partial assistant text before `send(event)` and breaking out of the loop.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — I can restate it from the code.

Mechanism (verified by reading, not inference):
- `backend/packages/model-router/src/router.ts:231-247`: after `this.recordSuccess(provider.name)` the provider is "committed". Inside the `try`, a throw from `await iterator.next()` is caught and converted to an IN-BAND event — `yield { type: "error", message: "The model provider failed partway through responding: ..." }; return;` — it is not rethrown. The generator then ends normally.
- `backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:414-417`: `if (event.type !== "done") { send(event); continue; }`. The `error` event is treated as an ordinary non-terminal event. The `for await` then ends normally.
- `completed` (set only at :526 in the `done` branch) stays false; `abort.signal.aborted` is false, so `:530 if (abort.signal.aborted && !completed) logCancelled()` is a no-op and the `catch` at :531 is never entered.
- Consequences confirmed: the span keeps `"gen_ai.system": "unknown"` from the `withSpan` attributes at :360 and OK status (`span.setAttributes` :502 and `span.setStatus({code: ERROR})` :544 are both in unreached branches); the `status: "error"` log at :545-548 is never written; `ctx.messages.add` (:430) and `ctx.usage.create` (:445) are never reached, so the partial assistant text is discarded and no ledger row is written. The comment at :540-542 states exactly the contract this path breaks.

Corroborating: every OTHER consumer of the router treats the in-band error as terminal — `chat.ts:202` (the summary path, same file) `else if (event.type === "error") throw new Error(event.message)`, `agent-core/src/engine.ts:1562`, `media/src/video-script.ts:198`, `rag.ts:429`. The chat streaming loop is the lone outlier.

Coverage claim verified: `grep -rn "partway" backend frontend --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (excl. node_modules) hits only `router.ts:243`; `grep -rln "v1/chat" backend/src --include=*.test.ts` → chat-summary, memory-extraction, memory, usage only — none exercises the streaming loop with a mid-stream error. `spend-guards.test.ts:237` yields an error event but against `/api/v1/rag/query`, not chat.

No ADR fixes it: I scanned ADR-044, ADR-098, ADR-119, ADR-132, ADR-140..ADR-144 in docs/26_DECISIONS.md. ADR-132 moved metrics to the router and ADR-119 fixed iterator closure; neither touches the chat route's handling of the in-band error event.

Two corrections that do not change the verdict:
1. "zero signal for an operator" is overstated. `streamWithRetry`'s catch at router.ts:349 calls `settle("error", ...)` and rethrows, and `backend/src/index.ts:1117 onCall` turns that into `recordProviderCall({status: "error"})` plus latency. So an aggregate error counter IS incremented; what is missing is the per-request signal — the span, the correlated error log, the stored message and the ledger row.
2. The suggested fix's "write a usage row for whatever the router reported through onCall" is not achievable as stated: `usage` in `settle` is populated only from a `done` event, so on this path it is `{}` — the router has no token counts to write. The real loss is a discarded partial response and an unattributable spend, not a known-token row that was dropped.

Severity P1 is right: a shipped capability (chat streaming) records a genuine provider failure as a clean 200 with an OK `gen_ai.chat` span, and the user's partial answer is never persisted. Not P0 — nothing is exploitable and chat still works; the client does receive the error event and `frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx:89` handles it.

confirmed.title: A mid-stream error wipes the partial answer the user already received, and the backend never stored it
confirmed.evidence: ChatView.tsx:89-91: `} else if (event.type === "error") { setMessages((prev) => replaceLast(prev, { role: "assistant", content: event.message, isError: true })); }` — `assistantText`, accumulated from every `token` event at :62-65, is discarded. Compare the transport-failure path in the same function, ChatView.tsx:104-112, which deliberately keeps it: "What arrived before the stop is a real answer as far as it goes — keep it" / `content: partial || "Stopped before the model answered."`. The server side loses it too: backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:430 `ctx.messages.add({... role: "assistant", content: event.message.content ...})` sits inside the `event.type === "done"` branch only, so on the router's mid-stream `error` (router.ts:240-246) nothing is persisted. frontend/app/lib/chat-stream.test.ts has no case that yields tokens followed by an `error` frame.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The user watches an answer stream in, then sees it replaced by "The model provider failed partway through responding: ...". Reloading the conversation does not bring it back, because `messages.add` was never called. Paid-for, already-delivered output is destroyed at both layers — the same 'silently discarded valid stream' class the transport path was explicitly hardened against three lines away.
confirmed.fix: Mirror the catch-block treatment in the `error` branch: keep the accumulated `assistantText` and append the error as a separate flagged line rather than replacing the bubble. Pair it with the server-side fix so the partial turn is stored.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. ChatView.tsx:89-91's `error` branch replaces the bubble with `event.message` and never references `assistantText` (accumulated at :63-65), while the tool_call branch at :79-88 and the catch block at :106-121 both deliberately preserve it — an inconsistency inside one function. The mid-stream error is genuinely reachable after tokens: router.ts:231-247 yields `{type:"error", message:"The model provider failed partway through responding: ..."}` once a provider is committed, and chat.ts:411-413 forwards any non-`done` event straight to the socket, so that exact string reaches the browser. Server-side, `grep -n "messages.add" backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts` returns only line 103 (user message) and line 430 (inside the `event.type === "done"` branch), so nothing persists the partial assistant turn; the outer catch at :531-549 only sends an error. No test covers it: ChatView.test.tsx's "keeps the text that did arrive before the failure" (:68) uses `failingAfter`, which THROWS out of the generator (the catch path), and both chat-stream.test.ts error cases (:113, :129) emit the error with zero preceding tokens. No ADR addresses it — `grep -n "ChatView|partial|mid-stream" docs/26_DECISIONS.md` shows ADR-024 (:345-349) only permits a mid-stream failure to surface, ADR-123 (:2041) hardened the abort/catch path, ADR-141 the tool_call branch. Two corrections that do not change the verdict: (1) "paid-for" overstates it — `ctx.usage.create` is also only in the `done` branch, so the tenant is never charged; the cost is upstream only, no double-charge or quota leak; (2) the failure is not silent, the user sees a clear provider-failure message — what is lost is the delivered text, unrecoverably. P2 is correct: real defect in shipped chat, but it fires only when a committed provider stream breaks after its first event and the turn is already visibly failed. (Fix note: chat-history.ts:13 drops every `isError` message from subsequent request history, so keeping the partial inside an isError bubble preserves it on screen but not in the next prompt.)

confirmed.title: No SSE resume mechanism at all (no `id:` frames, no Last-Event-ID, no heartbeat) and a partial live feed permanently shadows the complete persisted log
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-134's own framing is "a task that spent ten minutes reading files and running commands". Such a run's stream is cut by the platform at five minutes; the endpoint's replay (agent.ts:145-148) resends only `state` and `node`, never past `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`verification`, so every activity entry emitted during the gap is gone from the live feed forever. Worse, because the surviving partial list is non-empty, `CodingTabs` keeps preferring it after the run completes and never falls back to the full persisted log that arrived on the final `node` event — so the reconnect converts a transient gap into a permanent one on the screen whose job is to show what the agent did.
confirmed.fix: Write an `id:` line per event and honour `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect by replaying the node's persisted activity from that point; send a `: keepalive` comment every ~20 s so an idle stream is not reaped; and change TaskDetail.tsx:243 to merge (prefer persisted when the task is in a terminal state, or union by `callId`) rather than to prefer live whenever it is non-empty.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:141 writes only `event:`/`data:` frames — no `id:` line — and the connect-time replay (lines 146-148) emits one `state` and one `node` per node, never past `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`verification`. The stated greps reproduce empty: no `last-event-id`/`lastEventId` anywhere in backend/src, backend/packages, frontend/app or shared/src, and no `heartbeat`/`: ping`/`retry:` in the two SSE routes or the hook. infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:265 sets no `template.timeout` on the api service, so Cloud Run's 300s default applies. Crucially, backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts builds `activity` in a local array (line 682) and only persists it to node.output at a terminal point (verifyAndAdvance line 982; handleNodeFailure lines 970/990 -> write at 1266-1267), so mid-run there is genuinely nothing for a reconnect to replay. On the client, frontend/app/lib/use-task-events.ts keeps `activity` append-only in state scoped to `useEffect(..., [taskId])` and its `source.onerror` body is empty, so EventSource's own auto-reconnect opens a new stream without resetting or refilling that array — the gap's entries are lost. frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx:243 then does `activity.length > 0 ? activity : persistedActivityOf(nodes)`, so one surviving live entry makes the truncated list win even after the final `node` event delivers the complete persisted `output.activity` that persistedActivityOf (line 315) is written to read. No ADR covers it: ADR-134, ADR-142 and ADR-145 touch this exact code and none adds ids, Last-Event-ID, keepalive, or changes that preference. Two corrections: "permanently" overstates it — the shadowing lasts only for the mounted component, and a page reload shows the full persisted log; and the Cloud Run 300s figure is a plausible trigger, not a precondition (any blip, idle proxy reap or sleep does it). P2 stands: a real completeness defect on the screen whose job is showing what the agent did, but non-blocking and refresh-recoverable.

confirmed.title: The task stream's `onerror` handler is empty and its comment describes behaviour EventSource does not have; a refused stream is invisible to the user
confirmed.evidence: use-task-events.ts:128-133: `source.onerror = () => { /* A closed/errored SSE connection just stops live updates; the page still shows the last known state, and a manual refresh re-fetches it — no retry loop needed for a single-operator dev tool like this. */ };` Both halves are wrong. On a transport failure EventSource sets readyState to CONNECTING and reconnects on its own (default ~3 s in browsers) — there IS a retry loop, and each retry re-runs `requireProject`, `ctx.tasks.get` and `ctx.taskNodes.listByRoot` (agent.ts:119-147), three DB round-trips per attempt, forever. On a non-2xx response EventSource does the opposite: readyState CLOSED, no retry — which is what a 400 from `scopedProjectId` or a 404 from `if (!task) throw new NotFoundError(...)` (agent.ts:123) produces, and nothing in the hook or in TaskDetail renders anything for it. The hook exposes no error state at all (`return { task, nodes, activity }`, line 147).
confirmed.why_it_matters: This is the defect the hook's own header comment says it fixed — "the stream never opened and the task screen showed whatever it was seeded with, frozen, with no error anywhere the user could see" — still present for every refusal other than the missing-projectId one. A task whose id 404s (wrong project selected mid-session, task deleted) or whose session has expired shows a frozen, plausible-looking screen. And when the connection merely blips, the code takes the retry path the comment says it does not have, against an endpoint with no rate limit of its own.
confirmed.fix: Track readyState in `onerror`: surface a "live updates disconnected" banner with a manual reconnect when readyState is CLOSED, and bound/backoff the CONNECTING case. Return the connection state from the hook so TaskDetail can render it.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the source. use-task-events.ts:128-132 has an empty `onerror` whose comment asserts "no retry loop needed"; the hook returns only `{ task, nodes, activity }` (line 147) and TaskDetail.tsx:28 consumes only those three — its only error UI is per-node `n.errorMessage` (line 200). Grep for `onerror` across frontend/ hits only this file and the FakeEventSource test double. agent.ts:116-123 runs `requireProject` and `if (!task) throw new NotFoundError(...)` before `reply.raw.writeHead(200, ...)`, so a 400/403/404 is a plain JSON error response; per spec EventSource then goes to CLOSED with no reconnect, and nothing renders it. task-detail-loader.tsx fetches once with no polling fallback, so the screen stays frozen on stale seed data — precisely the failure the hook's own header comment (lines 61-65) claims to have fixed, honoured only for the missing-projectId case. The comment's other half is wrong too: a transport failure does auto-reconnect (~3s) and re-runs requireProject/tasks.get/taskNodes.listByRoot each time. No ADR in docs/26_DECISIONS.md addresses it — grep for onerror|reconnect|disconnected|live update|EventSource returns only MCP-reconnect ADRs and ADR-123's CORS note. One correction: the finding's "endpoint with no rate limit of its own" overstates the retry half — server.ts:144-150 registers a global Postgres-backed 300/min limit and a browser reconnect is ~20/min, so it is a false comment, not a resource risk. The silent frozen screen carries the severity; P2 is right.

confirmed.title: The ADR-052 execution lease is dead code: nothing ever claims, renews or releases it, so N API instances all dispatch the same task
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn "claimLease|renewLease|releaseLease" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist --exclude-dir=.git | grep -v "repositories/task-repository.ts"` returns 0 lines — no caller anywhere, not even a test. The same grep for `leaseOwner|leaseExpiresAt|lease_owner` returns only task-repository.ts and schema/index.ts. The only write of those columns is the literal `leaseOwner: null, leaseExpiresAt: null` in `PgTaskRepository.create` (task-repository.ts:105-106), so `tasks.lease_owner` is permanently NULL and `tasks_lease_idx` (schema/index.ts:289) indexes an always-NULL column. Meanwhile schema/index.ts:274-279 states: "A process may only dispatch a task whose lease it holds... This is what makes two API instances against one database safe", and task-repository.ts:70-74 states "This is the entire reason two API instances can share one database without both dispatching the same task." The actual mutual exclusion is `AgentEngine.runExclusive` (backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:1433), an in-process `Map` of promises. `engine.resumeAll()` (backend/src/index.ts:1295) is unconditional on the HTTP path and calls `listNonTerminal()` (no tenancy, no lease) and re-dispatches every non-terminal task (engine.ts:1409-1421). infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:273-275 sets the api service to `min_instance_count = 0, max_instance_count = 3`.
confirmed.why_it_matters: With more than one api instance — which the deployed Cloud Run config explicitly permits — every instance that cold-starts re-dispatches every non-terminal task in every project. Two instances run `planAndExecute`/`tick` on the same task graph concurrently with no database-level guard, so the same `model_call` node makes two real paid provider calls and the same `tool_call` node runs a mutating tool twice. The in-process lock is per-process by construction and gives zero protection. The code that would prevent this exists, is well written, is documented as the load-bearing safety property, and is never invoked — so nothing in the test suite or in review can notice.
confirmed.fix: Have the engine actually take the lease: call `taskRepo.claimLease(taskId, ownerId, ttl)` before dispatching in `resumeAll`/`tick`/`planAndExecute` and skip the task when it returns false, `renewLease` on a heartbeat while a node is executing, and `releaseLease` in the finally. Until that is wired, either constrain the api service to one instance or state in the schema comment that the lease is unused and multi-instance dispatch is unguarded, rather than claiming the opposite.
confirmed.verdict: Verified independently. claimLease/renewLease/releaseLease (backend/packages/database/src/repositories/task-repository.ts:173,207,224) are correctly implemented single-statement conditional UPDATEs, and my own grep for claimLease|renewLease|releaseLease|leaseOwner|leaseExpiresAt|lease_owner over all .ts/.tsx excluding node_modules/dist returns hits only in task-repository.ts and packages/database/src/schema/index.ts — no caller in backend/src, agent-core, or any test. The sole write is the literal `leaseOwner: null, leaseExpiresAt: null` in PgTaskRepository.create (lines 105-106), so tasks.lease_owner is permanently NULL and tasks_lease_idx (schema/index.ts:289) indexes an always-NULL column. The comments at schema/index.ts:274-277 ("This is what makes two API instances against one database safe") and task-repository.ts:70-74 ("the entire reason two API instances can share one database without both dispatching the same task") are therefore claims the code does not honour. The only mutual exclusion is AgentEngine.runExclusive (engine.ts:1464), an in-process Map of promises. backend/src/index.ts:1295 calls engine.resumeAll() unconditionally on the http path (the worker role returns earlier at index.ts:1049), and resumeAll (engine.ts:1398-1457) re-dispatches planAndExecute/tick for every task from listNonTerminal() — no tenancy, no lease — skipping only WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL/PAUSED. infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:273-275 sets the api service to min_instance_count=0, max_instance_count=3. No ADR addresses this: ADR-052 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1462) is about commit-before-dispatch and only argues persisted startedAt makes reclaim possible; it never claims the lease is taken, and `grep -i lease docs/*.md` finds nothing else. Two corrections to the finding. (1) The impact is not "N instances always dispatch the same task": a task created over HTTP on instance A is dispatched only there. The concrete duplication is cold start — a second or third api instance booting while instance A is mid-run re-dispatches every non-terminal task in every project, so the same model_call node makes a second paid provider call and the same tool_call node re-runs a mutating tool. resumeAll's needs_reconciliation guard only covers waiting_tool nodes and cannot tell "crashed" from "another live instance is running it now". (2) Severity lowered from P0 to P1: the defect is real and unmitigated, but it requires an actual multi-instance deployment to manifest — the terraform permits three, nothing shows it deployed — and the window is boot-time resume rather than every dispatch. It becomes P0 as soon as the api service genuinely scales past one instance.

confirmed.title: `AgentEngine.startScheduler()` is never called, so the persisted retry deadline and node-timeout sweep only run once per process boot
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn "startScheduler" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist --exclude-dir=.git` returns only the definition at engine.ts:1320 — zero callers. `grep -rn "\.sweep("` over the same scope returns only engine.test.ts:520/525/535/537 (manual calls in tests), engine.ts:1323 (inside the never-called `startScheduler`) and engine.ts:1426 (one pass at the end of `resumeAll`). `grep -n "engine\." backend/src/index.ts backend/src/test-app.ts backend/src/server.ts` shows the only production engine call is `await engine.resumeAll()` at backend/src/index.ts:1295. `sweep()` is the sole consumer of `nodeRepo.listDueForRetry` and `nodeRepo.listTimedOut` (engine.ts:1335, 1355), which are the sole consumers of `task_nodes.next_attempt_at` (schema/index.ts:318, index `task_nodes_next_attempt_idx` at :329) and of the `started_at + timeout_ms` predicate. `tick` promotes a `retrying` node only when its deadline has already passed (engine.ts:357-363), and the planner sets `backoff: "fixed"` with `DEFAULT_RETRY_BACKOFF.baseDelayMs = 1_000` (engine.ts:94, planner.ts:179 and :264).
confirmed.why_it_matters: A node that fails retryably is written to `retrying` with a future `next_attempt_at`. The immediate re-tick at engine.ts:431-433 finds the deadline unexpired, `ready` is empty, and the node is not terminal so `finalizeTask` is skipped — the task sits in RETRYING forever. Nothing polls the deadline, so the declared backoff never fires and the task never finalizes until the process restarts. `answer_from_documents` is planned with `maxAttempts: 3` + `grounding_check` (planner.ts:258-264) precisely so a rejected ungrounded answer is re-prompted; in production that retry never happens. Node execution timeouts whose process died are likewise never swept. The suite is green because engine.test.ts:512-545 drives `engine.sweep()` by hand — it proves the mechanism works, not that anything runs it.
confirmed.fix: Call `engine.startScheduler()` in the composition root (backend/src/index.ts, next to `engine.resumeAll()` at :1295) and `stopScheduler()` from the graceful-shutdown steps. Add an assertion at the composition-root level, not the engine level, that a task left in `retrying` advances without an explicit `sweep()` call.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. `startScheduler` is defined at backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:1351 (finding cited 1320; the file has uncommitted edits that shifted lines) and a repo-wide grep for `startScheduler|stopScheduler` over .ts/.tsx excluding node_modules/dist returns only the two definitions plus five `harness.engine.stopScheduler()` calls in engine.test.ts afterEach — zero start callers. The composition root backend/src/index.ts builds the engine at :1145 and its only lifecycle call is `await engine.resumeAll()` at :1295; test-app.ts:140 likewise never starts it, and no pg-boss/cron job calls sweep or resumeAll (grep over backend/src returns only index.ts:1295). `sweep()` at :1339 is the sole consumer of listTimedOut/listDueForRetry and runs in production exactly once, at the end of resumeAll (:1457). Impact follows: handleNodeFailure (:1275-1291) writes `retrying` with nextAttemptAt = now + delay (fixed = 1000ms, DEFAULT_RETRY_BACKOFF at :94); tick promotes a retrying node only once that deadline has passed (:352-367); the immediate re-tick at :426-433 runs before the deadline, ready is empty, the node is non-terminal so finalizeTask is skipped, and nothing re-enters the task afterwards except a user approve/reject/cancel (backend/src/routes/v1/agent.ts:171/180/201) or a process restart. So the declared backoff never fires — including the `answer_from_documents` maxAttempts:3 + grounding_check re-prompt that planner.ts:258-264 exists for. Tests are green because engine.test.ts:512-545 calls engine.sweep() by hand. No ADR covers it: grep of docs/26_DECISIONS.md for scheduler/sweep/next_attempt/backoff yields only ADR-052's note at :1468 that next_attempt_at is persisted rather than held in a timer, which presupposes a poller. Minor overstatement: node timeouts are not entirely unswept — withNodeDeadline still fails in-process attempts, so only nodes stranded by a dead instance go unswept (the finding says as much). P1 is correct: retry-with-backoff is a shipped, documented, tested capability that never runs outside process boot, but the happy path works and no data is corrupted, so not P0.

confirmed.title: `agent.node:<nodeId>` idempotency key silently discards the usage row for every retry of a model_call node, so re-prompted work is unbilled
confirmed.evidence: engine.ts:1030-1040 records usage after every successful model call with ``idempotencyKey: `agent.node:${node.id}` `` and the comment "One model call per `model_call` node, so the node id alone is the natural key". That is false for a retried node: `verifyAndAdvance` (engine.ts:1200) routes a failed verification to `handleNodeFailure`, which sets the SAME node id to `retrying` with an incremented `attemptCount` (engine.ts:1246-1258); the node is then re-dispatched and `executeModelCall` makes a second real provider call. `usage_records` has `uniqueIndex("usage_idempotency_unique").on(t.idempotencyKey)` (backend/packages/database/src/schema/index.ts:638), and `PgUsageRecordRepository.create` uses `.onConflictDoNothing({ target: usageRecords.idempotencyKey })` then returns the pre-existing row when it is in the same project (usage-record-repository.ts:68-80) — no error, no log. planner.ts:258-264 plans the RAG answer node with `maxAttempts: 3` and `grounding_check` explicitly so a retry re-prompts. This is the same defect the neighbouring reasoning-loop path already fixed by putting the turn in the key (engine.ts:900-907, ``agent.node:${node.id}:turn:${turn}``, whose comment describes exactly this failure).
confirmed.why_it_matters: A node that costs three real model calls is charged for one. Quota is enforced from `usage_records` (`sumLlmTokensForTenantSince`), so the undercount both understates the ledger the /usage endpoint reports and quietly widens the tenant's remaining budget. It is invisible: the conflict path returns the winning row rather than raising. `PgUsageRecordRepository.create`'s only loud branch is the cross-project one, which a same-project retry never hits.
confirmed.fix: Include the attempt in the key, mirroring the reasoning-loop fix: `agent.node:${node.id}:attempt:${node.attemptCount}`. The crash-recovery case the current key was meant to cover (a `waiting_model` node reset to `pending` by `resumeAll`, engine.ts:1370-1372) does not increment `attemptCount`, so it stays deduplicated.
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed by reading the code, and I can restate it independently.

1. `backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:1041-1053` — after every successful `runModelToCompletion` in the `model_call` path, `this.deps.meter.record({... idempotencyKey: `agent.node:${node.id}` })` runs, with the comment "One model call per `model_call` node, so the node id alone is the natural key (ADR-054)". The key contains no attempt/turn component.

2. That premise is false for a retried node. `verifyAndAdvance` (engine.ts:~1206-1218) routes a failed verification to `handleNodeFailure`, which at `const attempts = node.attemptCount + 1` sets the SAME node id to `status: "retrying", attemptCount: attempts, nextAttemptAt` (engine.ts:1277-1290). `tick` promotes a due `retrying` node back to `pending` (engine.ts:358-364), and `executeNodeInSpan`'s dispatch (engine.ts:498-504: `tool_call` / `reasoning` / else → `executeModelNode`) re-runs the full model path — a second real provider call, with no cached-output short-circuit.

3. The second charge is silently dropped: `usageRecords` has `uniqueIndex("usage_idempotency_unique").on(t.idempotencyKey)` (packages/database/src/schema/index.ts:638), and `PgUsageRecordRepository.create` uses `.onConflictDoNothing({ target: usageRecords.idempotencyKey })`, then re-selects and returns the pre-existing row when it matches the same project — no throw, no log. Its only loud branch is the cross-project collision, which a same-project retry never reaches (usage-record-repository.ts:65-90).

4. It is reachable in shipped code: `planner.ts:236-264` plans the RAG answer node as `kind: "model_call"` with `verificationMethod: "grounding_check"` and `retryPolicy: { maxAttempts: 3 }`, with a comment that the retry deliberately re-prompts. So attempt 1 is billed and attempts 2-3 are discarded.

5. Not already fixed, and the neighbouring path proves the shape is understood: the reasoning loop keys `agent.node:${node.id}:turn:${turn}` (engine.ts:914) with a comment describing exactly this failure, and both that comment and `src/index.ts:1193-1198` plus the `ModelCallMeter.record` docstring (engine.ts:70-80) explicitly assert `agent.node:<nodeId>` "is right for a `model_call` node — one node, one call", which the retry path contradicts. Grep `grep -rn "agent\.node:" --include=*.ts backend` returns only engine.ts:914, engine.ts:1053 and the two comments; no attempt-aware variant exists. `grep -n "ADR-054" docs/26_DECISIONS.md` gives ADR-054 (line 1494), which records the per-turn reasoning fix only and repeats the "one node, one call" assumption for model_call; no later ADR covers the model_call retry.

Impact is as described but bounded: quota is enforced from `usage_records` (`sumLlmTokensForTenantSince`) so the undercount both understates /usage and quietly widens remaining budget, but the loss is capped at maxAttempts-1 extra calls on nodes that actually fail verification, which is the exceptional path, and it undercharges rather than double-charging or exposing data. P2 as filed is correct — a real defect in a shipped billing/quota capability, non-blocking. The proposed fix (`agent.node:${node.id}:attempt:${node.attemptCount}`) is also sound: the crash-recovery case ADR-054 wanted protected is `resumeAll` resetting `waiting_model` → `pending` without touching `attemptCount`, so that re-execution still dedupes.

confirmed.title: `projects.deleted_at` has no writer and there is no project-delete route, so the documented soft delete does not exist and the per-org project cap can never be freed
confirmed.evidence: schema/index.ts:101-102 documents the column: "Soft delete: a deleted project's content stays readable to an admin for audit." `grep -rn "deletedAt" --include=*.ts backend/packages/security backend/src | grep -i project` returns exactly two lines, both READS: auth-service.ts:673 (`isNull(projects.deletedAt)` in `authorizeProject`) and auth-service.ts:736 (`isNull(projects.deletedAt)` in `listProjectsForUser`). `grep -rn "update(projects)|delete(projects)" --include=*.ts backend/ --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist` returns one line — account-deletion.ts:145, a hard `tx.delete(projects)`. `grep -rn "api/v1/projects" --include=*.ts backend/src` shows only `GET /api/v1/projects` (auth.ts:180), `POST /api/v1/projects` (auth.ts:195) and `POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members` (auth.ts:216) — no DELETE. auth-service.ts:780 caps an organization at `maxProjectsPerOrganization` (default 100, auth-service.ts:92) counted over all rows for the org with no `deletedAt` exclusion.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Two consequences. (1) A project is permanent: the only way to remove one is for its last member to delete their entire account (account-deletion.ts). A tenant that creates a project by mistake cannot remove it or its content. (2) Because the cap counts every row ever created and nothing can ever reduce that count, an organization that reaches 100 projects is permanently unable to create another — the error message says "already has the maximum" with no remedy. The schema comment describes a capability that has no implementation on either side.
confirmed.fix: Either add `DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id` that sets `deleted_at` (and exclude `deleted_at IS NOT NULL` from the `createProject` count so a slot is genuinely freed), or drop the column and correct the comment to say projects are permanent until account deletion.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. schema/index.ts:101-102 documents projects.deletedAt as a soft delete; a repo-wide grep for deletedAt shows soft-delete WRITERS only for conversations (conversation-repository.ts:147), documents (document-repository.ts:202) and memoryItems (memory-item-repository.ts:315) — projects.deletedAt appears only in two READ predicates, auth-service.ts:673 (authorizeProject) and :736 (listProjectsForUser). grep for update(projects)/delete(projects) finds zero updates and one hard tx.delete(projects) in account-deletion.ts:145; there is no project repository file in packages/database/src/repositories at all. grep "app.delete" over backend/src/routes returns only auth sessions, auth account, api-keys, files and memory — no project delete — and docs/API.md:185-191 lists only GET /api/v1/projects, POST /api/v1/projects and POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members. auth-service.ts:773-784 caps creation with select(count()).from(projects).where(eq(projects.organizationId, organizationId)) and no deletedAt exclusion, throwing "already has the maximum of N projects". docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-126 introduces that cap and no ADR in 123..143 adds a delete path or a writer, so this is not already fixed. Both stated consequences follow: a project is permanent unless its last member deletes their whole account, and an org at the cap can never free a slot. P2 is correct — nothing is exploitable and the delete capability was never shipped; the defect is a schema comment describing behaviour the code does not implement plus a one-way cap.

confirmed.title: `createProject`'s project cap claims a transaction makes concurrent creates mutually exclusive; under READ COMMITTED it does not
confirmed.evidence: auth-service.ts:765-787: the comment states "The count and the insert share a transaction so two concurrent creates cannot both read 'one under the limit' and both proceed", and the body is `db.transaction(tx => { const [existing] = await tx.select({total: count()})...; if (total >= max) throw; await tx.insert(projects)... })`. No isolation level is requested (`grep -rn "isolationLevel|serializable|FOR UPDATE|pg_advisory" --include=*.ts backend/ --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist` returns exactly one hit — auth-service.ts:132, prose only). drizzle's `transaction()` uses the server default, READ COMMITTED, under which a plain `SELECT count(*)` takes no predicate lock; two transactions both see N and both insert. There is no unique constraint on `projects` to catch it. The same file gets this right 630 lines earlier: auth-service.ts:124-133 spells out for `bootstrapSystemAdmin` that "The check is a plain SELECT under the default READ COMMITTED isolation: two transactions can both see an empty table and both insert... closing it properly needs an advisory lock or a serializable transaction — which is a real change, deliberately not made here rather than described as already done."
confirmed.why_it_matters: The cap is bypassable by concurrent `POST /api/v1/projects` requests, which is the exact failure the comment asserts is impossible. The impact is bounded (ADR-126 moved quota to the tenant, so extra projects buy no extra budget) but the cap exists to bound database growth, and a reader auditing this file will trust the comment and not re-check. It is also a direct contradiction of the honest treatment the same author gave the identical pattern in `bootstrapSystemAdmin`.
confirmed.fix: Take a transaction-scoped advisory lock on the organization id (`select pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($orgId))`) before the count, or run the transaction at SERIALIZABLE and retry on 40001. Otherwise reword the comment to the standard this file already sets at line 124-133.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — I can restate the defect from the code.

`backend/packages/security/src/auth-service.ts:765-787`: the docblock on `createProject` says "The count and the insert share a transaction so two concurrent creates cannot both read 'one under the limit' and both proceed." The body is exactly what the finding quotes: `await this.db.transaction(async (tx) => { const [existing] = await tx.select({ total: count() }).from(projects).where(eq(projects.organizationId, organizationId)); if ((existing?.total ?? 0) >= this.maxProjectsPerOrganization) throw new ValidationError(...); await tx.insert(projects)...; await tx.insert(projectMembers)...; })`. No isolation level is requested, so drizzle uses the server default (READ COMMITTED). A plain aggregate SELECT takes no predicate/range lock there, so two transactions both read N and both insert. I re-ran the grep: `isolationLevel|serializable|FOR UPDATE|pg_advisory` over `backend/` (excluding node_modules/dist) returns exactly one hit, `auth-service.ts:132`, and it is prose inside the `bootstrapSystemAdmin` comment, not code.

No unique constraint catches it either. `backend/packages/database/src/schema/index.ts:92-105` defines `projects` with `id` as the only primary key and a single non-unique `index("projects_org_idx").on(t.organizationId)` — nothing per-organization that a second concurrent insert could collide on.

The internal contradiction the finding points at is real and is the strongest part of it: `auth-service.ts:124-133` spells out, for the identical shape in `bootstrapSystemAdmin`, that "It is NOT a mutual-exclusion guarantee, and an earlier version of this comment claimed it was. The check is a plain SELECT under the default READ COMMITTED isolation: two transactions can both see an empty table and both insert... closing it properly needs an advisory lock or a serializable transaction — which is a real change, deliberately not made here rather than described as already done." 630 lines later the same author makes precisely the claim he disowned there.

ADR check: ADR-126 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2078) is the ADR that introduced this cap, and it does not fix the race — it repeats the false claim in the decision record itself: "`createProject` counts inside the transaction that inserts (two concurrent creates cannot both read 'one under the limit')". So the wrong claim is in both the code and the doc; nothing later addresses it. Greps for `pg_advisory`/`serializable` confirm no subsequent ADR added a lock.

Severity P2 is correct, not higher. Two things bound the impact, and neither makes the finding wrong:
- ADR-126 moved every quota aggregate to the organization, so extra projects buy no extra budget — this is a database-growth bound, not a spend bound.
- `backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:194-203` rate-limits `POST /api/v1/projects` at 20 per 10 minutes keyed on `req.auth?.user.id`, so the achievable overshoot is a handful of rows past the cap per window, not unbounded. The finding's own "the impact is bounded" framing is accurate; I'd only add that the rate limit narrows it further than the finding says.

What survives as the actual defect is the comment/ADR claiming a guarantee the code does not provide, in a file that elsewhere makes a point of refusing to do exactly that — a reader auditing the cap will trust it and not re-check. The proposed fix (advisory xact lock on the org id, or SERIALIZABLE with 40001 retry, or reword to the standard set at line 124-133) is the right menu.

confirmed.title: scripts/verify-migrations.sh: the schema-drift check passes when drizzle-kit fails, and its required-table list is missing audio_generations
confirmed.evidence: Line 95: `GEN=$(npm run db:generate --workspace=@ai-platform/database 2>&1 || true)`; lines 94/96 capture `BEFORE`/`AFTER` as `ls migrations/*.sql | wc -l`; lines 98-100 report `ok "no schema drift"` whenever `BEFORE -eq AFTER`. The `|| true` means any failure of drizzle-kit (bad config, missing dev dependency, parse error, non-zero exit for any reason) leaves the file count unchanged and the step reports PASS — the check announces success precisely when it did not run. Separately, lines 77-80 enumerate the required tables and the list ends `...usage_records rate_limit_counters` with no `audio_generations`; `grep -n "audio_generations" scripts/verify-migrations.sh` returns nothing, while the table is created by migrations/0003_youthful_karen_page.sql and declared at schema/index.ts:466. Line 84 then prints `ok "all 22 application tables exist after migration"`. I ran the migrations against an empty in-memory PGlite and `information_schema.tables` returns 23 tables including `audio_generations`. This step runs in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:75-76).
confirmed.why_it_matters: The file's own header calls the drift check "the check that catches the hand-edit drift" and "the one that matters", and ADR-087 records it as the reason a hand-edited schema cannot reach a deployment. A check that reports PASS when its tool did not execute provides no protection while looking like it does. The stale table list means the whole ADR-114 speech feature's table is outside the guarantee the script prints, and the hardcoded "22" will keep drifting silently with every new table. (I verified there is no drift today: comparing meta/0004_snapshot.json against every `pgTable` column name in schema/index.ts shows no schema-only or migration-only column, and migrations apply from empty and re-apply as a no-op.)
confirmed.fix: Drop the `|| true` and fail the step on a non-zero exit from `db:generate`, or assert on drizzle-kit's own "No schema changes" output rather than on a file count. Derive the required-table list from the exported `pgTable` names (or from the snapshot) instead of hardcoding it, so a new table cannot be omitted, and drop the hardcoded "22".
confirmed.verdict: Restated from the code. scripts/verify-migrations.sh:94-99 decides "no schema drift" solely by comparing `ls backend/packages/database/migrations/*.sql | wc -l` before and after `GEN=$(npm run db:generate ... 2>&1 || true)`. The `|| true` discards drizzle-kit's exit status, so any failure to run (missing tool, bad config, parse error, interactive prompt) writes no file, leaves the counts equal, and prints PASS "no schema drift — the migrations describe the current schema" — the guard reports success exactly when it did not execute. (The `|| true` is load-bearing given `set -euo pipefail` at line 19, so the fix must add an explicit status check rather than just delete it.) Separately, lines 77-80 hardcode 22 table names; `grep -c audio_generations scripts/verify-migrations.sh` returns 0, while the schema declares 23 `pgTable(` tables including `audioGenerations` at backend/packages/database/src/schema/index.ts:478, created by migrations/0003_youthful_karen_page.sql:1. Line 84 prints "all 22 application tables exist", a count already wrong. ADR-087 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1354-1366) is the ADR that created this script and calls the drift check "the one that matters" — it is the claim being violated, not a prior fix; no later ADR touches verify-migrations.sh or db:generate. The step runs in CI at .github/workflows/ci.yml:75-76. P2 is correct: a shipped guard is weaker than it claims and one real table is outside its assertion, but drizzle-kit is a declared devDependency and there is no drift today, so the failure is latent rather than currently breaking a capability.

confirmed.title: `releaseRenderSlot`'s contract says it covers a skipped render; orchestration only releases on `failed`, and a skipped render is unreachable anyway
confirmed.evidence: video-project-repository.ts:161-164 documents `releaseRenderSlot` as "the explicit-retry path (`POST /api/v1/videos/:id/retry`) after a failed **or skipped** render. Without it the slot is a one-shot latch and a project whose render failed could never be re-rendered." The only production caller that implements that retry path is backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:163-165, which guards on `if (project.renderStatus === "failed")` only — `"skipped_no_ffmpeg"` is not released. It is moot in the other direction too: backend/packages/media/src/video-render.ts:143-150 sets `renderStatus: "skipped_no_ffmpeg"` and then `updateStatus(..., "succeeded")`, and video-orchestration.ts:156 returns early on `if (project.status === "succeeded") return;` before reaching the release at all.
confirmed.why_it_matters: A project rendered on a host without ffmpeg has `render_requested_at` set permanently. Once ffmpeg is installed, the documented retry endpoint cannot produce the MP4: `claimRenderSlot`'s `WHERE render_requested_at IS NULL` never matches again, so `checkProjectCompletion` returns silently and the user gets no error and no render. The docstring promises exactly the case that does not work, which is the kind of claim a future caller will build on.
confirmed.fix: Either release the slot for `renderStatus === "skipped_no_ffmpeg"` as well (and let the retry path past the `status === "succeeded"` early return for that case), or correct the docstring to say only a `failed` render releases the slot and that a skipped render is terminal.
confirmed.verdict: Restated from the code: video-project-repository.ts:160-165 documents releaseRenderSlot as the retry path "after a failed or skipped render", but grep for releaseRenderSlot across src (excluding node_modules/dist) yields exactly two production callers, both in video-orchestration.ts — line 164 under `if (project.renderStatus === "failed")`, and line 331 as the rollback when jobQueue.enqueue throws. "skipped_no_ffmpeg" is never released. It is moot in the other direction too: video-render.ts:141-150 writes renderStatus "skipped_no_ffmpeg" then updateStatus(..., "succeeded"), and video-orchestration.ts:156 `if (project.status === "succeeded") return;` precedes the release block, so POST /api/v1/videos/:id/retry (routes/v1/videos.ts:132-162, whose whole body after quota checks is orchestrateVideoProject) returns 202 having done nothing. claimRenderSlot's `WHERE render_requested_at IS NULL` then never matches again, so the MP4 cannot be produced once ffmpeg is installed. No ADR covers it: grep -n "renderRequestedAt|render slot|releaseRenderSlot|claimRenderSlot" docs/26_DECISIONS.md returns nothing. One imprecision in the finding — it says checkProjectCompletion "returns silently", when control actually never reaches it (the status==="succeeded" early return fires first); the evidence section states this correctly and the net effect (no error, no render) is unchanged. P2 stands: a false docstring plus a dead recovery path, but no shipped happy path breaks and every scene clip remains individually downloadable.

confirmed.title: No log line in the platform carries trace_id/span_id — currentTraceContext() has zero production callers
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn "currentTraceContext" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules` returns exactly 4 hits: the definition (tracing.ts:47), its own re-export in dist/tracing.d.ts, and two uses inside span-coverage.test.ts (lines 5, 131, 145). No file under backend/src, backend/packages/*/src (other than observability itself), frontend/ or shared/ imports it. `grep -rn "trace_id\|traceId" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx backend frontend shared --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns only tracing.ts:47 and tracing.ts:51 — i.e. the definition, and nothing else in the entire tree. Yet tracing.ts's module docstring (lines 10-13) states the module provides "real trace/span ids correlated into log lines", docs/20_OBSERVABILITY.md:140 requires "Correlate trace/span IDs into every structured log line (`trace_id`, `span_id` fields)", docs/20:231 lists `trace_id`/`span_id` among the ids that must be present, and docs/20:243 describes the operator workflow as "open one bad trace → pivot to its correlated logs by `trace_id`". span-coverage.test.ts:133 asserts the helper works and comments "This is what puts a trace id on a log line" — nothing does.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The stated purpose of having both spans and structured logs is the pivot between them. Spans go to a ConsoleSpanExporter and logs go to stdout as separate JSON with no shared id, so an operator holding a slow `agent.run` span has no way to find that run's log lines, and an operator holding an error log line has no way to find its trace. The test suite is green and the module docstring asserts the property, so nothing surfaces the gap. This is the same shape as ADR-088's finding (observeQueueDepth/recordDeadLetter imported and never called) applied to the tracing half of the package.
confirmed.fix: Bind the trace context into the log record: either add a Pino `mixin: () => currentTraceContext() ?? {}` in `createLogger` (so every line from the shared instance picks up whatever span is active on the AsyncLocalStorage context), or spread `currentTraceContext()` into the request/job child-logger bindings in server.ts's hook and index.ts's `runJob`. Then extend span-coverage.test.ts (or logger.test.ts) to assert a log line emitted inside `withSpan` actually contains the span's `traceId`.
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed from the code. `currentTraceContext()` at backend/packages/observability/src/tracing.ts:47 has zero production callers — grep for it across the tree (excluding node_modules) returns only the definition, its own dist/tracing.d.ts re-export, and three uses in span-coverage.test.ts. `createLogger` in logger.ts configures name/level/redact/timestamp and no Pino `mixin`, and a grep for trace_id|traceId|span_id|spanId across backend, frontend and shared (excluding node_modules/dist) returns only tracing.ts:47,51 and the observability package's own tests — no log line anywhere carries a trace id. The doc claims are real and unhonoured: tracing.ts's docstring (lines 10-13) asserts "real trace/span ids correlated into log lines", docs/20_OBSERVABILITY.md:139-140 requires trace_id/span_id on every structured log line, and §5 describes the operator pivot by trace_id. No ADR in docs/26_DECISIONS.md addresses it — ADR-033 and ADR-073 cover span creation and nesting only. So: dead machinery plus a docstring the code does not honour, exactly the shape claimed.

Severity lowered from P1 to P2 because the stated impact does not follow. docs/20 §5 lists five correlation ids and the other three ARE implemented on both sides: agent.run/agent.step carry task_id/project_id/user_id (engine.ts:249,449) while agent log lines carry task_id (backend/src/index.ts:1174,1203,1594; routes/v1/agent.ts:89; typed in logging.ts:50); runJob's job.process span and its success/failure log lines both carry job_id, request_id and project_id (backend/src/index.ts:1620-1660); gen_ai.chat carries request_id matching the request's log lines. An operator holding a slow agent.run therefore CAN find its log lines, by task_id — just not by the OTel-native trace_id the docs promise. Compounding this, spans go to a ConsoleSpanExporter with no Collector/Tempo/Grafana (deliberate, ADR-033), so there is no trace UI to pivot from today at all. Real defect in a documented property, non-blocking, with a working fallback path. The proposed fix (mixin: () => currentTraceContext() ?? {} in createLogger, plus a test asserting a line emitted inside withSpan carries the span's traceId) is correct.

confirmed.title: Media and document failures return raw provider/binary error text to tenants — the leak ADR-119 closed for RAG only
confirmed.evidence:
`processImageGeneration` persists `errorMessage: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)` (image-generation.ts:97) and `errorMessage: result.error` (line 86). Those messages are produced unsanitised by the adapters: image-openai/src/index.ts:194 → `Could not reach the image provider at ${this.baseUrl}: ${err.message}`; image-sdcpp/src/index.ts:165 returns `err.message`, which run() builds at line 203 as `stable-diffusion.cpp exited with code ${code}: ${stderr.trim().slice(-400)}` (400 bytes of the binary's stderr, which names the absolute model path) and at line 200 as `stable-diffusion.cpp could not be started: ${err.message}` (Node's `spawn ENOENT`). The frontend renders it directly: `frontend/app/images/page.tsx:115` → `{g.errorMessage &&

{g.errorMessage}

}`. Identical chains exist for audio (media/src/audio-generation.ts:96 → speech.ts:271 `Windows SAPI synthesis failed: ...` → routes/v1/audio.ts:81/89 → frontend/app/audio/page.tsx:129), video (media/src/video-orchestration.ts:271/284, providers/video-replicate/src/index.ts:599 `Could not reach Replicate at ${url}...` → frontend/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx:183) and documents (rag/src/ingest.ts:233/248 → routes/v1/rag.ts:215 → frontend/app/files/page.tsx:118; the ingest error can be llm-local/src/index.ts:318 `Local embedding request failed (${res.status}): ${truncate(body)}` — the upstream's response body). The permission needed to read any of these is only `project:read`.
confirmed.why_it_matters: docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1985 (ADR-119) closed exactly this for chat/RAG — "A provider's error text reached the caller. `ServiceUnavailableError(event.message)` handed a tenant whatever the upstream said — which can name its host, model and account. The caller gets a stable sentence and the request id; the detail goes to the log" — and backend/src/routes/v1/spend-guards.test.ts:229-257 enforces it for `POST /api/v1/rag/query`, asserting the response contains neither `api.internal.example`, `acct_9f3` nor `gpt-internal-7`.
