Simplest containment is a sanitiser at the persistence boundary in `processImageGeneration`/`processAudioGeneration`/`processVideoScene`/`processDocumentIngestion` that maps a provider failure to a fixed set of reasons, logging the detail at error level with `request_id`. Then extend spend-guards.test.ts with the same not-to-contain assertions against `GET /api/v1/images/:id`, `/api/v1/audio`, `/api/v1/videos/:id` and `/api/v1/files`.
confirmed.verdict:
Verified from the code, not the finding's prose. CONFIRMED chain (images): `processImageGeneration` (backend/packages/media/src/image-generation.ts:84-98) persists `errorMessage: result.error ?? "Provider returned no images."` and, in the catch, `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)` — unmodified. {g.errorMessage}

}`. Same shape confirmed for audio (backend/packages/media/src/audio-generation.ts:94-97, raw `err.message` into `errorMessage`) and documents (backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:233 `updateStatus(..., "failed", message)` with `message = err.message`, and :248). Not already fixed: ADR-119 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1975-1988) closed exactly this reasoning ("A provider's error text reached the caller… the caller gets a stable sentence and the request id; the detail goes to the log") but its Impact line names only `model-router`, `usage-record-repository`, `embedding-service`, `routes/v1/{rag,videos,platform}.ts` — it changed the thrown-error path, not the persisted column. `grep -rn "sanitiz\|safeErrorMessage\|redact" --include=*.ts backend/packages backend/src` (non-test) returns only Pino log-redaction in packages/observability and server.ts — there is no sanitiser anywhere near these persistence boundaries. confirmed.title: job_retry_total can never be emitted: registerWorker holds job.retryCount but never hands it to the handler
confirmed.evidence: `recordJobProcessed` only emits the counter under a guard: metrics.ts:240-242 `if (attrs.retryCount && attrs.retryCount > 0) { counter("job_retry_total", ...).add(1, ...) }`. `grep -rn "retryCount" --include=*.ts backend/src backend/packages/observability/src --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist` returns exactly three hits: metrics.ts:231 (the optional field), metrics.ts:240 (the guard), and metrics.test.ts:89 (the test passing `retryCount: 2`). Zero production call sites. The only two production callers are backend/src/index.ts:1645 and :1660, both `recordJobProcessed({ queue, outcome, durationMs })` with no `retryCount`. The value does exist upstream and is deliberately fetched — backend/packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:228-234 documents that `includeMetadata` "is what puts `retryCount`/`retryLimit`/`deadLetter` on the job" and line 237 reads `job.retryCount` for dead-lettering — but line 235 invokes the handler as `await handler(job.data, job.id)`, so `retryCount` never crosses into `runJob`. `grep -rn "job_retry_total" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v dist` returns only metrics.ts:241 and metrics.test.ts:95.

An operator querying `job_retry_total` on `/api/v1/admin/metrics` gets "no such metric" on a platform whose queues retry constantly, and cannot distinguish "nothing is retrying" from "this was never wired". metrics.test.ts:88-95 passes because it calls the recorder directly with a literal `retryCount: 2`, so the green suite is evidence of nothing. confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. metrics.ts:240-242 emits job_retry_total only under `if (attrs.retryCount && attrs.retryCount > 0)`, and counter() (metrics.ts:127-134) creates instruments lazily into a Map, so an unreached branch means the series never registers and never appears in OnDemandMetricReader.scrape() output — absent, not zero. The only two production callers are backend/src/index.ts:1645 and :1660 inside runJob, both passing only {queue, outcome, durationMs}; runJob's params type (index.ts:1616) has no retry field at all. queue.ts:225 declares the handler as (payload: T, jobId: string) and line 235 invokes `handler(job.data, job.id)`, discarding job.retryCount even though the comment at 228-231 documents fetching it via includeMetadata and line 237 uses it for dead-lettering. My greps: `grep -rn "retryCount" --include=*.ts backend frontend shared` hits only queue.ts:74/228/230/237/365, metrics.ts:231/240, metrics.test.ts:89 (plus the unrelated video_scenes.retry_count column); `grep -rn "job_retry_total" --include=*.ts .` returns only metrics.ts:241 and metrics.test.ts:95. Zero production call sites. metrics.test.ts:89 passes a literal retryCount: 2 straight into the recorder, so the green suite exercises the guard and not the wiring. No ADR in docs/26_DECISIONS.md mentions job_retry_total or retryCount. One correction to the write-up's rationale, which does not change the verdict: ADR-088 is about symlink containment in the filesystem tools, not observability, and its two named siblings are in fact wired — observeQueueDepth at index.ts:588 and recordDeadLetter at index.ts:528 via QueueClient's onDeadLetter hook (queue.ts:238). retryCount is the one parameter left unthreaded. confirmed.title: Provider/token/cost metrics are labelled with the configured model, not the model actually called
confirmed.evidence: `streamWithRetry` reports every completed call with `model: provider.model` (router.ts:297 on the throw path, router.ts:325 in `settle`) — the adapter's constructor-time default. But the adapters honour a per-request override: llm-local/src/index.ts:96 `const model = request.model ?? this.model;` (emitted on the `done` event at line 224), llm-openai/src/index.ts:118 and :155 `request.model ?? this.model`. `shared/src/chat.ts:54` makes `model` an optional caller-supplied field of `chatRequestSchema`, and backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:384-385 forwards it unchanged: `ctx.router.streamChat({ ...chatRequest, messages: promptMessages, conversationId: conversation.id }, ...)`. The composition root then uses the router's value for all four metrics and for pricing: backend/src/index.ts:1118-1138 — `recordProviderCall({ ..., model: call.model ?? "unknown" })`, `recordTokenUsage({ ..., model })`, and `estimatedCostUsd: estimateLlmCostUsd(call.provider, model, usage)` at line 1137. The ledger uses the other value: chat.ts:453/457 writes `model: event.model` and `estimateLlmCostUsd(event.provider, event.model, event.usage)` from the `done` event.
confirmed.why_it_matters: Whenever a client names a model, `provider_request_count`, `provider_latency_ms`, `token_usage_total` and `cost_estimate_usd_total` all attribute the call to a model that was not used, and `cost_estimate_usd_total` is priced at the wrong model's rate — so it silently disagrees with `usage_records.estimated_cost_usd` for the same call. docs/20 §2.2 makes `cost_estimate_usd_total` rate-of-change alerting priority 3 ("catches a runaway agent loop or an abuse pattern before the bill arrives"); a deployment whose configured default is cheap and whose callers request an expensive model under-reports exactly the spend that alert exists to catch. A p95 on `provider_latency_ms` also silently mixes two models into one series. Cardinality is unaffected, so nothing about this is visible from the exposition.
confirmed.fix: Carry the effective model on `ProviderCallOutcome` the same way token usage already is: capture it from the `done` event (`first.value.model` / `next.value.model`) into the `settle` closure, falling back to `provider.model` only when the stream never reported one. The label stays bounded (it is whatever the adapter actually used), and the metric and the ledger then agree by construction.

confirmed.title: stdio MCP connection failures are stored and served unsanitised, while the HTTP path was explicitly sanitised for that exact reason
confirmed.evidence: `openClient` sanitises only the HTTP branch. The HTTP failures go through `describeHttpFailure` (client.ts:339-348), whose own docstring at line 335-337 says: "Only origin + path go into the message. A URL can carry `user:password@` or a token in its query string, and `lastError` is readable by anyone with `project:read`." The stdio branch (client.ts:254-265) has no wrapper at all — `await client.connect(new StdioClientTransport({ command: config.command, args: config.args ?? [], env: config.env, cwd: config.cwd }), { timeout })` — so whatever Node/the SDK throws propagates verbatim. `McpManager.connectWithRetry` stores it: manager.ts:222 `const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);` → manager.ts:229 `lastError: message` (and manager.ts:270 for the health-check path). `GET /api/v1/mcp` serves it at backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:141 `lastError: server.lastError`, behind `await requireProject(request, ctx.auth, "project:read")` (platform.ts:127) — not `requireSystemAdmin`. The default stdio server is spawned with absolute host paths: backend/src/server.ts:181-183 `command: process.execPath, args: [fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve("@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem/dist/index.js")), sandboxRoot]`, so a spawn failure yields `spawn <absolute node path> ENOENT` and the operator's directory layout.
confirmed.why_it_matters: `ctx.mcp.status()` is process-global — every tenant on the deployment reads the same rows — and `lastError` is the one free-text field in them. The comment two functions away states the threat model and the audience correctly and the stdio path was simply never given the same treatment, so the protection reads as complete while covering one of two transports. The result is that any self-registered project member can read internal host filesystem paths (and, for an `MCP_SERVERS` entry with an absolute `command`/`cwd`, the operator's deployment layout) out of a status endpoint.
confirmed.fix: Wrap the stdio branch the way the HTTP branch is wrapped: catch around `client.connect(...)` at client.ts:255 and rethrow a `ServiceUnavailableError` naming only `config.id` and a bounded reason (`could not be started`, `did not complete the handshake`, `timed out`), with the raw error logged. Cheaper belt-and-braces alternative: move `lastError` behind `requireSystemAdmin` in platform.ts and leave `status`/`transport`/`toolIds` on `project:read`.
confirmed.verdict: Restated from source: openClient's stdio branch (backend/packages/mcp/src/client.ts:253-265) calls client.connect(new StdioClientTransport(...)) with no wrapper, while the http branch (277-310) routes every failure through describeHttpFailure, whose own docstring at 336-337 says only origin+path may go in the message because "lastError is readable by anyone with project:read". McpManager stores the raw message (manager.ts:221-229 and again at 270-281 in checkHealth) into a process-global states map, and GET /api/v1/mcp returns it (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:141) behind only requireProject(..., "project:read") at :127 — while the reconnect route immediately below uses requireSystemAdmin with a comment explaining that ctx.mcp is process-wide. The raw pass-through is pinned by a test: packages/mcp/src/manager.test.ts:99 expects lastError to match /ENOENT/. grep of docs/26_DECISIONS.md for mcp/lastError/sanit shows ADR-067, 083, 089, 097, 136, 143, 144 — none addresses this, so it is not already fixed. Two corrections to the report: the spawn citation is wrong (it is backend/src/index.ts:1086-1087, not backend/src/server.ts:181-183 — the file has no such lines), and the impact is narrower than the HTTP rationale implies, since a stdio config carries no user:password@ or query-string token; what actually leaks is host filesystem layout (spawn <absolute node path> ENOENT, or an operator's absolute command/cwd from MCP_SERVERS) to any authenticated self-registered project member, deployment-wide. Real asymmetry, real cross-tenant path disclosure, no escalation — P2 as reported.

confirmed.title: The Terraform API service cannot boot as documented: no LLM provider is configurable anywhere in infrastructure/, and three places claim the opposite

Leave unset to run on the mock LLM provider, exactly like local dev (docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-006/010)."`; terraform.tfvars.example:14 — `# Optional — leave blank/unset to deploy on the mock LLM provider, same as local dev.`; main.tf:146 — `# infrastructure: an empty var means the deployed API runs on the mock provider, exactly`. The created directory is also dead: main.tf:336 and :506 both set ASSETS_BUCKET, and index.ts:601-603 selects CloudStorageAssetStore whenever it is set, so assetsRoot is never used in either deployed unit. No coverage: backend/src/role-boot.test.ts:82 sets SANDBOX_ROOT and grep shows no ASSETS_ROOT anywhere in that file, and the CI container boot runs on Docker's writable layer. One correction to the finding's framing: the EROFS outcome itself cannot be executed here (no GCP project; the read-only-root premise is an external claim the repo asserts rather than one I can run), which is why this stays P1 rather than P0 — the internally provable defect is the inconsistent treatment of two identical adjacent calls plus a directory created for nothing, unobservable to every existing test.

confirmed.title: Nothing in the deployment consumes either health endpoint: no Cloud Run startup or liveness probe, and the CI boot gate only checks that the process has not exited
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn "api/health" infrastructure/ .github/` returns NO matches, and `grep -n "startup_probe\|liveness_probe\|ports {" infrastructure/terraform/main.tf` returns NO matches — the api and web `containers` blocks (main.tf:285-402, 434-438) define no probes and no ports. The one endpoint that actually reports whether the database and the pg-boss queue are reachable is admin-gated and therefore unreachable to any infrastructure caller, so an instance whose Cloud SQL socket or job queue is dead is still routed live traffic, and a hung event loop is never restarted. Both the readiness machinery and the liveness route are built and have no consumer anywhere in infrastructure/ or CI.
confirmed.fix: Add `startup_probe { http_get { path = "/api/health" } }` and a `liveness_probe` to the api service's container in main.tf (an explicit `ports { container_port = 8080 }` alongside, matching backend/Dockerfile's EXPOSE). Either expose an unauthenticated readiness route that reports the database/queue checks (without the stats payload), or state in main.tf why a liveness literal is the deliberate probe target. Extend the CI boot gate to curl /api/health rather than only polling `docker ps`.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, with two corrections to the framing.

Verified from the files myself:
- `C:\Users\Saurabh.kumar\Desktop\AI\infrastructure\terraform\main.tf` is the only .tf with resources (549 lines; siblings are outputs.tf/variables.tf/tfvars.example). My own `grep -n "startup_probe\|liveness_probe\|ports {\|container_port" infrastructure/terraform/*.tf` returns NOTHING. The api `containers` block (main.tf:285 onward, image + volume_mounts + ~12 env entries) and the web `containers` block (main.tf:434-438) define no probe and no `ports`. `grep -rn "api/health" infrastructure/ .github/` matches only the vendored provider .exe binary — no text match.
- `backend/src/routes/health.ts:4` is exactly `app.get("/api/health", async () => ({ status: "ok" }))` — a literal, no DB/queue touch. `backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:290` calls `requireSystemAdmin(request)` before awaiting `ctx.health.database()`/`ctx.health.queue()`, so it genuinely cannot serve as an unauthenticated infra probe.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:316-331` is as described: 30×`docker ps --filter status=running`, `docker logs`, `docker stop`. No request is issued.
- `backend/Dockerfile:84` has `EXPOSE 8080` and no `HEALTHCHECK`. `grep -rn "probe" docs/26_DECISIONS.md` finds no ADR about Cloud Run health probes — nothing prior fixes this.

Supporting evidence the finding did not cite, which strengthens it: `docs/15_API_ARCHITECTURE.md:27` describes `/api/health` as the "Unversioned liveness/**readiness** probe for Cloud Run / local dev". The infra wires no such probe, and the route performs no readiness check — `CURRENT_STATE.md:563` concedes "a health check passes against a dead or unmigrated database". That is a documented claim the deployment does not honour.

Corrections (why I did not raise it above P2):
1. The "unreachable machinery / no consumer anywhere" framing is partly wrong. `/api/health` IS consumed — `frontend/playwright.config.ts:61` uses `http://127.0.0.1:8790/api/health` as the webServer readiness URL, and the e2e job (ci.yml:217-239) runs it. `/api/v1/admin/health` IS consumed — `frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:104` fetches it. Neither endpoint is dead code; the accurate claim is narrower: no *infrastructure or deployment* caller consumes either.
2. The impact is a real hardening gap, not a broken capability. Cloud Run v2's implicit default is a TCP startup probe on the container port, so the service still deploys and serves; what is lost is DB/queue-aware gating and liveness restart. The Terraform has also never been applied (main.tf's own comments state no GCP project exists in this environment), so nothing is currently mis-serving traffic.

Also note the proposed fix is partly unworkable as written: the CI boot gate runs `ROLE=worker`, and the worker role starts no HTTP listener (per the ADR at docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2242), so curling `/api/health` against that container would fail — the gate would have to add an api-role container to make that assertion.

confirmed.title: The speech dead-letter replay quota test can only ever take the 404 path — the branch it claims to prove is never entered
confirmed.evidence:
spend-guards.test.ts:202-217 posts to `/api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/audio.generate.dlq/7d8f3c2e-1b4a-4c6d-9e8f-0a1b2c3d4e5f/replay` — a UUID that is never inserted — then asserts `expect([429, 404]).toContain(res.statusCode)` and, on 404, only `expect(JSON.stringify(res.json())).toMatch(/not found/i)`.

Contrast the image test two `it`s above (line 182-192), which asserts `toBe(429)` strictly because the image branch runs before the payload lookup.

The assertion is doubly unfaithful: even with a real dead letter present, `checkSpeechCharacters` (backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:186) compares `used + characters > daily`, so `dailySpeechCharacterLimit: 0` with a 0-character read would return `allowed: true` — the comment "Zero budget refuses even a zero-character replay" describes behaviour the manager does not have.

Absence proof: `grep -rn "replay" --include=*.test.ts backend` returns only jobs/dead-letter.test.ts (queue-level, no pricing) and spend-guards.test.ts. No test anywhere constructs a real `audio.generate.dlq` or `video.generate_scene.dlq` dead letter and drives the replay route through it.
confirmed.why_it_matters: ADR-130's headline fix was that replaying a speech job or a video scene "went through no budget at all, which made the dead-letter screen a way to spend past a ceiling that the create routes enforce". Both of those branches (platform.ts:241-263) can be deleted today and the whole suite stays green — the only test naming the property passes on a 404 that proves nothing about quota. That is a paid-work spend boundary with zero real coverage while reading as covered.
confirmed.fix: Seed a real dead letter: enqueue an `audio.generate` job with a `generationId` pointing at a real `audioGenerations` row whose `text` has a non-zero length, fail it into `audio.generate.dlq`, set `dailySpeechCharacterLimit` below that length, and assert `toBe(429)` with `error.code === "QUOTA_EXCEEDED"`. Do the same for `video.generate_scene.dlq` against `monthlyVideoSecondsLimit`. Delete the `[429, 404]` disjunction — an accepted 404 makes the assertion unfailable.
confirmed.verdict:
Verified against the code; I can restate the defect independently.

1. Deterministic 404. `backend/src/routes/v1/spend-guards.test.ts:202-217` POSTs to `/api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/audio.generate.dlq/7d8f3c2e-.../replay` with an id that is never inserted (the test's beforeEach only builds the app; nothing enqueues or dead-letters an audio job — `grep -rn "replay" --include=*.test.ts backend` returns only `packages/jobs/src/dead-letter.test.ts`, which is queue-level and never touches quota or the route, and this file). In the handler (`backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:230-271`), `getDeadLettered` (`backend/packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:431-443`) selects `where name=$1 and id=$2 and data->>'projectId'=$3 and state in ('created','retry')` and returns `row?.data ?? null` → null. The audio arm is guarded `else if (sourceQueue === "audio.generate" && payload)`, so it is skipped; `replayDeadLettered` then returns null and the handler throws `NotFoundError` (platform.ts:268-270) → 404 on every run. The assertion `expect([429, 404]).toContain(res.statusCode)` plus a 404-only `toMatch(/not found/i)` therefore asserts nothing about quota, and cannot fail if the whole `audio.generate`/`video.generate_scene` pricing block (platform.ts:242-261) were deleted. Contrast line 182-192, which asserts `toBe(429)` strictly — correct there because the `image.generate` arm runs unconditionally, before the payload is consulted.

2. The comment is also wrong. `checkSpeechCharacters` (`backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:175-199`) compares `used + characters > daily`; with `dailySpeechCharacterLimit: 0`, `used = 0` and `characters = 0` gives `0 > 0` → false → `allowed: true`. So the in-test claim "Zero budget refuses even a zero-character replay" describes behaviour the manager does not have; even if the 404 were avoided the test as written would not get a 429 with a zero-length payload.

3. No ADR covers it. `docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2136-2148` (ADR-130) introduced exactly these two branches and names "+5 tests across dead-letter.test.ts and spend-guards.test.ts"; its own "checked by removing the guards" argument is made only for the queue-name/state predicate in `dead-letter.test.ts`, not for the speech/video pricing. ADR-131..ADR-144 do not revisit replay pricing. So the finding is not already fixed and is not a misread.

Severity lowered from P0 to P2. The production guard itself is present and correct for a real dead letter (it reads `audioGenerations.text.length` / `videoScenes.durationSeconds` and calls the same quota methods the create routes use — `audio.ts:56` uses the identical call), so nothing is exploitable today and no shipped capability is broken; ADR-130's spend hole is genuinely closed in the code. What is real is a test-integrity defect: a spend boundary that reads as covered has an unfailable assertion, so a future regression that deletes or breaks those two arms ships green. That is "real but non-blocking" = P2. The proposed fix (seed a real dlq entry, drop the `[429, 404]` disjunction, assert `toBe(429)` and `error.code === "QUOTA_EXCEEDED"`, and a matching `video.generate_scene.dlq` case against `monthlyVideoSecondsLimit`) is the right shape.

confirmed.title: ADR-128's claim windows have no test at all; the file named for them covers only the second half
confirmed.evidence:
The claim windows that ADR-128 was written to fix live only in the composition root: backend/src/index.ts:558-561 (`const imageProviderDeadlineMs = Math.max(config.IMAGE_SD_TIMEOUT_MS, 180_000)` → `expireInSeconds: Math.ceil(imageProviderDeadlineMs / 1000) + 120`) and :577-582 (`expireInSeconds: Math.ceil(DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000) + 300`).

`grep -rn "expireInSeconds|IMAGE_SD_TIMEOUT_MS|DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS" backend/src/*.test.ts backend/src/routes/**/*.test.ts` returns nothing. `grep -rn 'from "./index.js"|from "../index.js"' backend/src/*.test.ts` returns nothing — no test imports the composition root at all. role-boot.test.ts runs `dist/index.js` as a child process but only greps stdout for `/Server listening/` and `/job workers registered/`; it never inspects queue options.

The file that carries the ADR's name, backend/packages/media/src/job-deadlines.test.ts, says so itself at line 33: "The window is derived from the provider's own deadline now; this covers the other half, the guard that makes a re-claim harmless". Its three image tests exercise `processImageGeneration`'s terminal-state guard; its three ffmpeg tests exercise `runFfmpegForTest`. Neither touches `ensureQueueWithDeadLetter`.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The exact defect ADR-128 records — a 60-second claim window over a provider given up to 600 seconds, so "every real generation outran its window and was generated a second time", with the usage row's idempotency key hiding the second charge — can be reintroduced by editing one literal in index.ts, and every suite stays green. The guard covers `image.generate` only; `audio.generate` (300s, fixed) and `video.generate_scene` (900s, fixed) have neither a window test nor an equivalent already-terminal guard test, so a widened provider deadline there re-opens double execution silently.
confirmed.fix: Extract the queue registrations into an exported pure function (e.g. `mediaQueueOptions(config)`) and assert the invariant rather than the literals: for each paid queue, `expireInSeconds * 1000` must exceed the corresponding provider/render deadline by the stated margin. A test that fails when `IMAGE_SD_TIMEOUT_MS` is raised without the window following is the one that would have caught the original bug.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. The ADR-128 claim windows exist only in the composition root, backend/src/index.ts:558-561 (image.generate, derived from Math.max(config.IMAGE_SD_TIMEOUT_MS, 180_000)) and :577-582 (video.render, from DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS). `grep -n "^export" backend/src/index.ts` returns nothing, so the values are unreachable from a test; `grep -rn "IMAGE_SD_TIMEOUT_MS|DEFAULT_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_MS" --include=*.test.ts backend/` returns zero hits, and every `expireInSeconds` in a test file (packages/jobs/src/dead-letter.test.ts, queue.test.ts, media/src/video-pipeline.integration.test.ts) is a hard-coded literal never compared to a provider deadline. backend/src/role-boot.test.ts is the only test that runs the entrypoint, and its assertions at lines 109-157 are exit codes and stdout regexes only. backend/packages/media/src/job-deadlines.test.ts states the limitation itself at line 33 and its six tests call processImageGeneration (81/105/126) and runFfmpegForTest (167/179/183); ensureQueueWithDeadLetter is never referenced. The finding's secondary claim also holds and is understated: image-generation.ts:70 has the already-terminal guard, but audio-generation.ts has only a cancelRequestedAt pre-check with no succeeded/cancelled guard, and video-orchestration.ts guards the render at :156 while the scene path at :221 checks only cancelRequestedAt — so a re-claim on those two paid queues re-executes work. Severity lowered from P1 to P2: the shipped code is currently correct (windows derived, image guard present), so nothing is broken now; the defect is an unenforced invariant that lets an expensive, already-occurred double-execution regression return while every suite stays green. That is a genuine test-integrity gap but not a live failure in a shipped capability.

confirmed.title: The audit-row test asserts a hand-written copy of the production sink, so ADR-139's truncation is unverified
confirmed.evidence:
tool-audit-rows.test.ts:8-14 claims it "proves the other half: that what the composition root does with it produces a row an auditor can query". It drives `ctx.toolRegistry` from `buildTestApp()`, whose `auditSink` is defined in backend/src/test-app.ts:104-134 and writes `detail: { outcome: entry.outcome, durationMs: entry.durationMs, arguments: entry.arguments }` (line 127) — raw arguments, no `serverId`, no `error`.

The production sink is backend/src/index.ts:316-347 and differs in three ways: `arguments: truncateForAudit(entry.arguments)` (line 340), `...(entry.serverId ? { serverId: entry.serverId } : {})` (line 337), `...(entry.error ? { error: entry.error.slice(0, 1_000) } : {})` (line 341), plus a `logger.warn` on insert failure.

`grep -rn "truncateForAudit" backend --include=*.ts` returns exactly two lines, both inside index.ts (340 and 1675). The function is not exported and has no test. ADR-139 states as fact: "Arguments are truncated at 500 characters per field ... an audit table that grows with the traffic becomes an audit table nobody queries."
confirmed.why_it_matters: A claim in the ADR that the code is asserted to honour is honoured only in a file no test imports. Delete `truncateForAudit(...)` and every `fs.write_file` call's entire `content` lands in `audit_log.detail`; nothing goes red. The test that reads as the proof is exercising a fixture written for the test, which is the "duplicate written for the test" failure mode — and the same divergence means the MCP `tool.call.mcp` action label and the `serverId`/`error` detail fields are untested too (`toolRows()` filters `action = "tool.call"` only).
confirmed.fix: Export `truncateForAudit` (and ideally the whole sink factory) from a module both `index.ts` and `test-app.ts` import, so the harness cannot drift. Add a direct test: a 2000-character `content` argument produces a stored value of 500 chars plus the `… (N characters)` suffix, and an MCP-origin call stores `action = "tool.call.mcp"` with `detail.serverId`.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, restated from the code. The test at C:\Users\Saurabh.kumar\Desktop\AI\backend\src\routes\v1\tool-audit-rows.test.ts drives `ctx.toolRegistry` from `buildTestApp()`. That registry's `auditSink` is a hand-written duplicate in C:\Users\Saurabh.kumar\Desktop\AI\backend\src\test-app.ts:112-132, whose detail is `{ outcome, durationMs, arguments: entry.arguments }` (line 127) — raw arguments, no truncation, no `error` field. The production sink is C:\Users\Saurabh.kumar\Desktop\AI\backend\src\index.ts:316-347 and differs: `arguments: truncateForAudit(entry.arguments)` (340), `...(entry.serverId ? { serverId } : {})` (337), `...(entry.error ? { error: entry.error.slice(0, 1_000) } : {})` (341), and a `logger.warn` on insert failure instead of a silent `.catch(() => undefined)`.

`grep -rn "truncateForAudit" backend --include=*.ts` (excluding dist) returns exactly two hits, both in index.ts: the call site at 340 and the definition at 1675. The function is module-private (`function truncateForAudit(...)`, no `export`) and `grep -rn "from \"../index|src/index.js\"" backend/src --include=*.test.ts` returns nothing — no test imports the composition root. `grep -rn "characters)" backend --include=*.ts` finds the truncation suffix only at index.ts:1680, never in an assertion. So deleting `truncateForAudit(...)` from line 340 leaves every test green while `fs.write_file`'s entire `content` lands in `audit_log.detail` — exactly the outcome ADR-139 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2249ff) states as settled fact ("Arguments are truncated at 500 characters per field ... an audit table that grows with the traffic becomes an audit table nobody queries") and whose proof it names as "a route-level test [that] proves a real call through the real registry leaves a real row". The real registry is real; the sink under it is a fixture written for the test. Same for the `error` detail field and `detail.serverId`: no test constructs an MCP-origin entry, and `toolRows()` (test line 30) filters `action = "tool.call"` only, so a `tool.call.mcp` row would be invisible to it anyway.

One correction to the finding's evidence, which does not change the verdict: the test fixture DOES carry the action label — test-app.ts:120 has `action: entry.serverId ? "tool.call.mcp" : "tool.call"`, identical to index.ts:323. That label is untested, not divergent. The divergences are truncation, `serverId`, `error`, and the failure logging.

Severity P2 is correct and I would not raise it. Nothing is exploitable now and no shipped capability is broken, so it is not P1/P0; it is more than INFORMATIONAL because the ADR asserts the guarantee and the "duplicate written for the test" pattern is the documented failure mode the harness was supposed to avoid (test-app.ts:108-111 comment claims it is "the same audit sink the real composition root wires (ADR-139)", which is a comment the code does not honour).

confirmed.title: Backend test files and the test harness are excluded from typecheck; real type errors exist and one weakens a fail-closed quota test
confirmed.evidence:
Every backend tsconfig excludes tests: backend/tsconfig.json:10 `"exclude": ["src/**/*.test.ts", "src/test-app.ts"]`, backend/packages/quota/tsconfig.json:9 `"exclude": ["src/**/*.test.ts"]` (same in tools, security, shared, …). `npm run typecheck` therefore never sees a backend test, and vitest transpiles without checking types.

`npx tsc --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.test.ts`
→ `quota-manager.test.ts(334,7): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'sumLlmTokensSince' does not exist in type 'QuotaUsageLedger'.`
→ `quota-manager.test.ts(257,9): error TS2353: ... 'createdAt' does not exist in type 'Omit<UsageRecord, "createdAt">'.`

`QuotaUsageLedger` (backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:16-24) requires `sumLlmTokensForTenantSince`, `countImagesForTenantSince`, `sumVideoSecondsForTenantSince`. The literal at line 333-337 supplies the pre-ADR-126 per-project names instead, so the ledger under test is missing every required aggregate — not just the speech one. The sibling helper `ledgerWithoutEmbeddingTotals` (line 58-64) uses the correct names, which is how the drift is visible.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The test "refuses speech, rather than silently allowing it, when the ledger cannot measure it" reads as isolating one missing optional aggregate; it actually stands on a ledger that implements none of the interface. It happens to still exercise the speech branch, but nothing stops the next such fixture from silently testing a different object than the author intended — and `test-app.ts`, the harness that stands in for the composition root for ~100 route tests, is excluded from typecheck too, so `AppContext` drift there is invisible until runtime. Frontend does typecheck its tests (frontend/tsconfig.json includes `**/*.ts(x)` with no test exclusion), so this is a backend-only gap.
confirmed.fix: Add a `tsconfig.test.json` per backend workspace that includes `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/test-app.ts` with `noEmit`, and run it from `npm run typecheck`. Then fix the two errors: use the `*ForTenantSince` names at quota-manager.test.ts:334-336 and drop the stray `createdAt` at :257.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed by reading the code and reproducing the compiler errors. quota-manager.test.ts:333-337 annotates the literal as QuotaUsageLedger but supplies the pre-ADR-126 per-project names (sumLlmTokensSince/countImagesSince/sumVideoSecondsSince); the interface at quota-manager.ts:17-24 requires sumLlmTokensForTenantSince/countImagesForTenantSince/sumVideoSecondsForTenantSince, so the fixture implements none of the three required members. The test nevertheless passes because checkSpeechCharacters (quota-manager.ts:175-182) short-circuits on the absent optional sumSpeechCharactersForTenantSince and never dereferences the others. The sibling helper ledgerWithoutEmbeddingTotals (test:58-64) uses the correct names, confirming drift rather than an intentional shape. The typecheck exclusion is repo-wide and real: backend/tsconfig.json:10 excludes src/**/*.test.ts and src/test-app.ts, and 24 package tsconfigs carry the same test exclusion, while typecheck is a plain `tsc --noEmit`; frontend/tsconfig.json includes **/*.ts(x) and excludes only node_modules, so the backend-only asymmetry holds. Running tsc directly on the file reproduces TS2353 at 334,7 and at 257,9 ('createdAt' not in Omit<UsageRecord,"createdAt">, matching usage-record-repository.ts:45). No ADR fixes it: ADR-126 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2078) renamed the aggregates and touched this test file without catching the fixture, and the lint ADR at line 1341 explicitly acknowledges the test exclusion as a workaround, never closing it. Severity P2 is correct: the fail-closed speech assertion still holds and no shipped capability is broken, but the class of defect is proven live, and the same blindness covers test-app.ts, the harness standing in for the composition root in the route tests.

confirmed.title: The new admin-gating source check only looks for the string "SystemAdminOnly" anywhere in the file, not around the control
confirmed.why_it_matters: The test is the ADR-144 generalisation of ADR-143's defect and is written to cover "screens nobody thought to write a test for, including ones added later". A screen that already renders one guarded control — which both current screens do — can gain a second, ungated admin-only control and stay green, which is precisely ADR-136's failure repeating inside a file that has since been fixed. `platform/page.tsx` is the likely next site, since it already imports `SystemAdminOnly` and already makes a raw `apiFetch("/api/v1/admin/health")`.
confirmed.fix: Check containment rather than presence: locate each `SystemAdminOnly` JSX region (or parse with a light TSX parser) and require the call site's offset to fall inside one, or require the handler to be referenced only from JSX within the guard. Make the fourth case call the real walker against a temporary fixture file so a regression in the walker itself fails.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed by reading the code. frontend/app/lib/session-context.admin.test.tsx:53-62 reads each file whole and decides compliance on `/SystemAdminOnly/.test(source)` — a file-level substring presence test with no link between the call site and the guard; the route check at 77-88 is identical. The cited offsets are exact: tasks/page.tsx:190 calls setToolEnabled with the guard at 235-244, platform/page.tsx:150 calls reconnectMcpServer with the guard at 256-266. Because both screens already contain the string, either can gain a second ungated admin-only control (SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_CLIENTS is ["setToolEnabled","reconnectMcpServer"], so a reconnect button on tasks/page.tsx would pass) and stay green — the ADR-136 failure the test was written to prevent. The fourth case (93-105) does not exercise the walker; the walker is inline in the it-block with no extracted function, and the case retypes both predicates against a synthetic string, so it proves the regexes match, not that an offender would be pushed. Not already fixed: ADR-144 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:2314-2329) is the ADR that ADDED this test and claims it "covers screens nobody thought to write a test for, including ones added later", which lines 50-65 do not establish; no later ADR touches it. One additional weakness the finding missed: line 83's `if (route === "/api/v1/admin/health") continue;` is keyed only on the route, not the file, so the read-only exemption written for platform/page.tsx exempts that route in EVERY file. P2 stands rather than P1: the shipped guards are actually correct, and a wholly new screen with no SystemAdminOnly would still be caught, so this is a regression-detection gap in a test whose ADR overstates its coverage, not a live authorization hole.

confirmed.title: "documents every route the server registers" asserts only that the table has ≥50 rows
confirmed.evidence:
api-contract.test.ts:103-108 is titled "documents every route the server registers" and asserts `rows.length >= 50`, one `auth === "public"` row, and one `auth.startsWith("system administrator")` row. It never enumerates the server's route table, so it cannot detect a route missing from docs/API.md.

Every other test in the file iterates `rows`, i.e. drives requests FROM the document. A route registered in code but absent from API.md is therefore exercised by none of the auth, permission or rate-limit checks — and the row count stays ≥50 either way. (Today they do agree: I extracted 66 `app.<method>("...")` registrations under backend/src/routes and 66 matching rows from docs/API.md, diff empty both directions.)

The only thing enforcing completeness is the CI step "Verify docs/API.md matches the routes" (.github/workflows/ci.yml:60-66), in a workflow whose own header at line 5 states "this workflow has still never executed on GitHub Actions — the repository that authored it has no remote". Nothing in `npm test` runs `scripts/generate-api-docs.py`.
confirmed.why_it_matters: The generator and the contract test are meant to be each other's check — ADR-112's point is that "a scraper can be wrong while agreeing perfectly with itself". As wired, a new route that its author forgets to document gets zero contract coverage (no 401-for-anonymous check, no viewer-permission check, no rate-limit check) while a test whose name claims full coverage stays green, and the only backstop has never run.
confirmed.fix: Have the test read the registered route table from the built app (`app.printRoutes({ commonPrefix: false })` or Fastify's `onRoute` hook via a probe registration) and assert set equality with the parsed rows in both directions. That makes the assertion fail on the first undocumented route, in `npm test`, without depending on CI.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed from the code. backend/src/routes/api-contract.test.ts:103-108, titled "documents every route the server registers", asserts only rows.length >= 50 plus the existence of one "public" row and one "system administrator" row; its own inline comment admits the real purpose is guarding against a regex that matched nothing. It never enumerates the app's route table, so it cannot fail on an undocumented route. The three substantive tests (lines 110, 122, 146) all iterate `rows` parsed from docs/API.md, so a route missing from the document receives no anonymous-401 check, no viewer-permission check and no rate-limit check, and the >=50 count is unaffected. Absence proven by grep -rn "printRoutes\|onRoute\|generate-api-docs" over *.ts/*.json/*.yml/*.py excluding node_modules: the only hits are .github/workflows/ci.yml:72, package.json:28 ("docs:api"), scripts/generate-api-docs.py:43, and two unrelated onRoute uses in the rate-limit store. npm test (root package.json:19 -> backend/package.json:12 `vitest run`) never invokes the generator, so the sole completeness gate is ci.yml:68-73, in a workflow whose own header at lines 5-8 states it "has still never executed on GitHub Actions - the repository that authored it has no remote". ADR-112 (docs/26_DECISIONS.md:1868-1881) is the governing ADR and asserts exactly that never-run CI step as the drift check; no later ADR adds a route-table assertion. Verified there is no drift today: `python scripts/generate-api-docs.py` reports 66 routes in 23 groups and leaves docs/API.md unchanged, and all route registrations live under backend/src/routes (grep for app/fastify/server .get|.post|.put|.patch|.delete outside that directory returns nothing), so the generator's glob covers the full surface. P2 is correct rather than P1: nothing is currently undocumented and no shipped capability is broken - the defect is that the only mechanism enforcing that property has never executed, while a test whose name claims the property stays green regardless.

informational.title: Working tree currently contains a deliberately disabled SystemAdminOnly guard that the new source-text test cannot detect
informational.evidence: HEAD is 95a4aa3 and all backend sources are unmodified, but the tree is being edited by a concurrent process during this audit (`git status --porcelain`: M frontend/app/lib/api.ts, M frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx, M frontend/app/platform/page.tsx, M frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx, ?? frontend/app/lib/session-context.admin.test.tsx, ?? frontend/e2e/admin-boundary.spec.ts). session-context.tsx:193 currently reads `const { user } = useSession(); void user; void fallback; return <>{children}</>; // temporarily ungated` — the component returns its children unconditionally — while tasks/page.tsx:235 and platform/page.tsx:256 have just been migrated off their working ad-hoc `user?.isSystemAdmin` checks onto it. The new guard test, session-context.admin.test.tsx:59 and :84, only checks `/SystemAdminOnly/.test(source)` — it never renders the component and never asserts it hides anything — and its "fails when a control is added without the guard" case (:93-105) re-implements the check inline against a synthetic string rather than invoking the real one, so it would still pass if the assertion at :64 were neutered.
informational.why_it_matters: The `// temporarily ungated` comment and the accompanying new e2e spec read as an in-flight mutation check (the repo's stated practice of re-running a fix with the fix removed), so I am reporting this as context rather than as a defect — but if it reaches a commit it is a P0 fail-open: every system-admin-only control in the interface would be offered to every user, and the suite would stay green, because the only test of the guard is a source-text grep. Worth a second look before that change lands. Separately, whether or not the line is reverted, the guard test's file-level substring check does not honour its own docstring claim at session-context.tsx:157-158 that it "finds the calls, and fails if one is rendered outside `SystemAdminOnly`" — a file with one gated and one ungated admin control passes.
informational.fix: Before committing, restore `return <>{user?.isSystemAdmin ? children : fallback}</>` and add a render test that mounts `<SystemAdminOnly>` with `isSystemAdmin: false` and asserts the children are absent — that single test fails against the current line, which the source-text checks do not.

informational.title: safeEqualHex has no callers, and could not be used by the one comparison it names
informational.evidence: `grep -rn "safeEqualHex" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v "/dist/"` returns exactly one line: the definition at tokens.ts:37. Its docstring says "Constant-time compare for the rare path that compares two hashes in application code." The only such path, `assertCsrf` in backend/src/plugins/auth.ts:126, uses `cookie !== provided` — and could not use `safeEqualHex` as written anyway: `generateCsrfToken` (tokens.ts:47) returns base64url, while `safeEqualHex` parses its arguments with `Buffer.from(x, "hex")`.
informational.why_it_matters: Not exploitable — the CSRF token is compared in the same request that carries it and a remote timing attack on a string compare is impractical, and both session tokens and API keys are looked up by indexed SHA-256 rather than compared in application code. It is worth knowing only because the helper's presence, and its export from @ai-platform/security, reads as a guarantee that secret comparisons in this codebase are constant-time when in fact none of them go through it.
informational.fix: Either delete it, or make it accept the encoding actually used (base64url) and call it from assertCsrf so the export matches what the code does.

informational.title: Client functions and a response field with no caller: `readWorkspaceFile`, `getImage`, and the ignored `truncated` flag
informational.evidence:
`grep -rn "getImage\|readWorkspaceFile" frontend --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` returns only the two definitions — api.ts:154 (`readWorkspaceFile`) and api.ts:196 (`getImage`). No screen, no test, no e2e spec calls either. The route behind `readWorkspaceFile` is backend/src/routes/v1/workspace.ts:104, whose docstring is 'One file\'s contents, for confirming what the agent will actually see' — nothing confirms anything; the `WorkspaceSeed` card (tasks/page.tsx:263-281) lists paths and sizes and offers no way to open one.
Separately, `listWorkspaceFiles` returns `{ files, truncated }` (api.ts:152-153; workspace.ts:100 `truncated: files.length >= MAX_LISTED_FILES` with `MAX_LISTED_FILES = 500`), and tasks/page.tsx does `.then((r) => setFiles(r.files))` — `truncated` is dropped, so a workspace over the cap silently shows a partial list.
Also a shape mismatch with no runtime effect today: `POST /api/v1/workspace/files` replies `{ file: { path, sizeBytes } }` (workspace.ts:146-148) while `WorkspaceFile` (api.ts:146-150) declares `modifiedAt: string` as required; the caller discards the response and re-lists, so nothing reads the missing field.
informational.why_it_matters: ADR-142's decision line is that the routes 'seed and inspect the per-project workspace'; the inspect-one-file half shipped a client function and no consumer. Not a user-visible failure today, but it is the shape that becomes one — the next screen to use `readWorkspaceFile` will be the first to discover whether it works.
informational.fix: Either wire `readWorkspaceFile` into the WorkspaceSeed card (click a path to view its contents, which is what the route was built for) or delete it and `getImage`; surface `truncated` as a 'showing the first 500 files' line; add `modifiedAt` to the write route's reply or make it optional on `WorkspaceFile`.

informational.title: Six authenticated screens render and fetch before the session resolves, contradicting the rule session-context.tsx states it enforces
informational.evidence:
session-context.tsx:18-27 states 'Two rules this enforces for every screen: 1. **No page renders user data before the session is known.**' The guard that implements it is `RequireSession` (L131-149). `grep -rln RequireSession frontend/app --include="*.tsx"` lists ask, memory, platform, settings, usage and agent/task-detail-loader. Iterating the page files, these do NOT use it: frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx, frontend/app/chat/page.tsx, frontend/app/chat/[conversationId]/page.tsx, frontend/app/images/page.tsx, frontend/app/videos/page.tsx, frontend/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx, frontend/app/audio/page.tsx, frontend/app/files/page.tsx.
The hazard is spelled out in a sibling file — frontend/app/agent/task-detail-loader.tsx:14-19: 'the project id `apiFetch` sends is re-validated by `SessionProvider` against what the account can actually see, so fetching before the session resolves would send a stale project from a previous login — the request either 403s or, worse, names a project the user no longer belongs to.' Those eight screens all fire their first fetch from a mount effect with no such gate.
informational.why_it_matters: In practice the damage is bounded — `login()` overwrites the stored project (auth-client.ts:160) and the polling screens re-read `localStorage` every 2s — so the visible symptom is a flash of a raw `ApiError` before the redirect to /login, plus the non-polling /tasks and /chat staleness reported separately above. It is listed here because the docstring asserts the rule holds 'for every screen' and it holds for five of eleven, which is the kind of drift the next screen inherits.
informational.fix: Wrap the eight screens in `RequireSession` (they are already client components, so it is a one-line change each), or amend the docstring to say which screens the rule is enforced on and why the rest opt out.

informational.title: applyUnifiedDiff's default `fs` argument has no `rmSync`, so a `+++ /dev/null` deletion reports action "deleted" while the file stays on disk
informational.evidence: patch.ts:193-197 declares the default as `fs: { readFileSync: typeof readFileSync; writeFileSync: typeof writeFileSync; rmSync?: (p: string) => void } = { readFileSync, writeFileSync }` — the default literal has no `rmSync`. The write loop then does `if (item.content === null) fs.rmSync?.(item.absolute); else fs.writeFileSync(...)` (patch.ts:234-235): with the default, the optional call is a no-op, and the function still returns `{ path, action: "deleted", hunksApplied, offsets: [] }` staged at patch.ts:207. Today's only caller is safe — coding.ts:101-105 passes `rmSync: (p: string) => rmSync(p, { force: true })` — so this is latent, not live. The unit test for deletion (patch.test.ts:177-190) supplies its own fake fs, so it would not catch a caller that omits one.
informational.why_it_matters: applyUnifiedDiff is exported from the package and its signature advertises a working default, so the next caller that relies on it gets a patch applier that reports a deletion it did not perform — the specific failure mode the module's own docstring says it was hand-written to avoid ("a patch either applies completely or not at all"). The model would be told the file is gone and reason from that.
informational.fix: Either include `rmSync` in the default object (`rmSync: (p) => rmSync(p, { force: true })`) or make the parameter required and drop the optional call, so a caller that cannot delete fails loudly instead of returning a false "deleted".

informational.title: terminal.run_command rejects any argument beginning with "-", and neither its description nor its input schema says so
informational.evidence: terminal.ts:134-140 returns `{ ok: false, error: 'Argument "..." looks like a command-line flag, which this tool never legitimately needs — rejected.' }` for any arg starting with "-". The description (terminal.ts:73-78) names only the command allow-list and explains that a non-zero exit code is not a tool failure; the inputSchema (terminal.ts:80-89) gives `args: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }` with no description and no constraint, and `cwd` with none either. The model is handed only `{name, description, inputSchema}` (registry.ts:129), so the flag rule is discoverable only by being refused.
informational.why_it_matters: `node --test`, `node --experimental-vm-modules x.js` and similar are the first things a model reaches for when told to run a test, and each one costs a turn out of AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS to discover a rule that could have been stated in the description. The error is legible enough that the model recovers, so this is a budget and reliability cost rather than a correctness defect.
informational.fix: State it in the description and the `args` field description: arguments must be file paths or plain values relative to `cwd`; flag-shaped arguments (leading "-") are rejected, and only `node <script>` is supported. The same sentence belongs on the `runTestCommand` allow-list in backend/src/index.ts:1247-1255, which enforces the identical rule.

informational.title: `supportsPermissionModel` exists "so the caller can refuse" and has no non-test caller
informational.evidence: sandbox.ts:191 says "one that understands neither gets no containment, which `supportsPermissionModel` reports so the caller can refuse." `grep -rn "supportsPermissionModel" .` (excluding node_modules/dist) returns only sandbox.ts:191/200 and sandbox-permission.test.ts:5,33-36,49. Neither `createSandbox` (sandbox.ts:346) nor the boot guard in backend/src/index.ts:283-296 consults it — that guard keys only on `NODE_ENV === "production" && sandbox.isolation === "process"`. On a runtime where `permissionFlagFor` returns null, `processSandboxArgs` returns `args` unchanged (sandbox.ts:220) and `ProcessSandbox` silently degrades to the pre-ADR-117 posture (cwd + scrubbed env, no filesystem containment) with nothing logged and nothing refused.
informational.why_it_matters: The escalation is currently blocked only by `package.json`'s `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }`, which npm does not enforce without `engine-strict`, and by `backend/Dockerfile`'s `FROM node:24-bookworm-slim`. A deployment on Node 18 — or any future runtime where the flag is renamed again — gets the exact end-to-end escape ADR-117 records (write a script with `fs.write_file`, run it with `terminal.run_command`, read the host) with no signal that containment is absent.
informational.fix: Have `createSandbox` refuse (or at minimum log at WARN, the way the missing-clamd path does) when `options.runtime === "process" && !supportsPermissionModel()`, so the function that reports the gap is actually wired to the decision it was written for.

informational.title: `projectWorkspace`'s docstring states containment is checked against the deployment root; every caller now passes the project workspace
informational.evidence: workspace.ts:20-24: "Containment still runs on top of this (ADR-088 resolves symlinks before checking), and it checks against the DEPLOYMENT root rather than the project's subdirectory. That is deliberate and worth stating... Narrowing containment to the project directory as well would be stricter still, and is a separate change." Every call site passes the project workspace as `root`: filesystem.ts:51,82,120,151; terminal.ts:117,145; coding.ts:72-73; search.ts:275; backend/src/routes/v1/workspace.ts:68,109,143; backend/src/index.ts:1244-1256; backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:163-164. `grep -rn "resolveSandboxedPath"` finds no caller passing a deployment root.
informational.why_it_matters: The comment is wrong in the safe direction, but it is the file a reviewer reads to answer "can one tenant's agent traverse into another tenant's workspace?" and it answers yes. Worse, it frames the stricter behaviour as future work, which invites someone to 'implement' it by loosening a call site back to the deployment root — the exact regression ADR-090 and ADR-095 exist to prevent.
informational.fix: Rewrite lines 20-24 to state that containment is checked against the project workspace by every caller, and note that this is what makes the cross-tenant walk impossible rather than deferring it.

informational.title: Native filesystem tool handlers return raw `fs` errors, leaking the absolute host path of `SANDBOX_ROOT` to the model
informational.evidence: None of the four handlers wraps its `fs` call: filesystem.ts:52 (`readFile`), :83-88 (`readdir`/`stat`), :121 (`writeFile`), :152 (`unlink`). The throw propagates to `ToolRegistry.invoke`'s catch (registry.ts:296-301), which returns `{ ok: false, error: err.message }` verbatim to the model. Observed (scratchpad probe7.mjs): `fs.write_file src/new.ts -> THREW: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'C:\Users\SAURAB~1.KUM\AppData\Local\Temp\nomkdir-YrS5FY\p1\src\new.ts'`. `assertContained` (sandbox.ts:92) likewise echoes the full workdir. This is the information sandbox-path.ts:51-54 deliberately withholds: "The message deliberately does not echo the resolved destination... telling the caller (a model, possibly following a prompt injection) where its symlink actually pointed hands back information the sandbox exists to withhold."
informational.why_it_matters: One `fs.read_file` on a nonexistent path hands the model the deployment's absolute sandbox root and its own project id — the layout it needs to aim a traversal, and a value the resolver's own refusal path is careful never to reveal. It also reaches the durable audit rows and the streamed activity log, so the host path ends up in per-tenant storage.
informational.fix: Catch in each handler and return `{ ok: false, error: <message naming only the caller-supplied relative path> }`, matching the style `resolveSandboxedPath` already uses.

informational.title: `realpathOfDeepestExisting` drops the first character of a path component whose parent is the filesystem root
informational.evidence:
sandbox-path.ts:108 is `missing.push(existing.slice(parent.length + 1))`, which assumes a separator sits between `parent` and the basename. When `parent` is the filesystem root that separator is already inside `parent`: `dirname("C:\\zzzz") === "C:\\"` (length 3), so `"C:\\zzzz".slice(4)` is `"zzz"`; on POSIX `dirname("/foo") === "/"` (length 1), so `"/foo".slice(2)` is `"oo"`.

PROVEN (scratchpad probe9.mjs) against the built resolver:
```
root=C:\zzzz        path=x  ->  REJECTED: Path "x" resolves outside the sandboxed root and was rejected.
root=C:\Users\zzzz  path=x  ->  C:\Users\zzzz\x
```
Identical requests, differing only in whether the missing component's parent is the drive root.
informational.why_it_matters: It fails closed here — a plainly-inside path is refused — so it is not an escape, but it is a silent miscomputation inside the one function that decides what is inside the sandbox, and it is reachable as a total outage: a `SANDBOX_ROOT` that is a direct child of `/` or of a drive root and does not yet exist (index.ts:262-263 mkdirs it at boot, so only a race or a root deleted underneath a running process gets there) makes every filesystem tool reject every path. Nothing in sandbox-path.test.ts covers a root whose parent is the filesystem root.
informational.fix: Use `basename(existing)` instead of the slice, or guard with `parent.endsWith(sep) ? parent.length : parent.length + 1`. Add a resolver test whose root is a non-existent direct child of the filesystem root.

informational.title: `usage_records.kind = 'tool'` is never written, though two comments state that tool usage is recorded
informational.evidence:
quota-manager.ts:27-29: "A subset of the ledger's `UsageKind`: `tool` usage is recorded but has no quota, because there is no unit of tool spend an operator could meaningfully budget yet." usage-record-repository.ts:5: "`embedding` and `tool` joined the ledger in ADR-049: both spend, so both are recorded."
`grep -rn 'kind: "tool"|kind: '\''tool'\''' --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/` returns nothing at all. Every `usage.create` call site — index.ts:441, 848, 909, 985, 1179; chat.ts:206, 445, 637; rag.ts:307, 408 — passes `"embedding"`, `"image"`, `"speech"`, `"video"` or `"llm"`.
informational.why_it_matters: Not a spend leak — ADR-139 gives tool calls their own durable record in `tool_calls`, which is the useful trail — but two comments in the billing layer assert a ledger fact that is false, and `UsageKind`'s `"tool"` member is an enum value nothing can produce. An operator or a later author reading either comment would reasonably believe `usage_records` answers "what did tools cost this project" and find an empty result rather than a missing feature.
informational.fix: Either drop `"tool"` from `UsageKind` and correct both comments to say tool calls are recorded in `tool_calls` rather than in the usage ledger, or write the row where tool execution completes (`backend/packages/agent-core` tool registry call path) if tool spend is meant to be metered.

informational.title: A failed subtitle mux is swallowed with no log — an operator cannot tell an MP4 with embedded captions from one without
informational.evidence: video-render.ts:417-422: `catch (subtitleError) { const detail = subtitleError instanceof Error ? subtitleError.message : String(subtitleError); void detail; }`. The message is computed and explicitly discarded with `void`. `VideoRenderDeps` (video-render.ts:66-79) has no logger field, and `VideoRenderOutcome` (lines 95-103) has no field distinguishing "captions embedded" from "sidecars only" — the outcome reports `subtitleAssetId`/`subtitleVttAssetId` identically either way, and `updateRender` (lines 444-451) persists nothing about it.
informational.why_it_matters: The comment says the degradation is deliberate ("A build without the mov_text encoder must not lose the whole render"), which is right — but the record of it is thrown away, so a deployment whose ffmpeg lacks `mov_text` ships every MP4 without an embedded track and nothing in the logs, the outcome or the database says so. Every other degraded path in this pipeline is reported (`skipped_no_ffmpeg`, `skipped_no_narration`, `scriptSource: "deterministic"` with a `fallbackReason`).
informational.fix: Add a logger to `VideoRenderDeps` (the scene path already has one — `VideoSceneProcessingDeps.logger`, video-orchestration.ts:198) and warn with `detail`, and/or add a `subtitlesEmbedded: boolean` to `VideoRenderOutcome` so the degradation is legible the way the others are.

informational.title: ADR-144 is cited in eight places across the ADR-144 work and does not exist in docs/26_DECISIONS.md
informational.evidence: `grep -n "ADR-144\|ADR-145" docs/26_DECISIONS.md` returns nothing; `grep -rn "ADR-144" docs/*.md` returns nothing. Meanwhile it is cited at frontend/app/lib/api.ts:162, frontend/app/lib/session-context.tsx:152 and :176, frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:140 and :251, frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx:232, and frontend/e2e/admin-boundary.spec.ts:4 and :103 — five of the eight spell it "docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-144". The last ADR in the file is ADR-143 at line 2305.
informational.why_it_matters: Every prior phase in this tree closes by writing the ADR, and the reasoning those eight comments point at (why `SYSTEM_ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES` exists, why the reconnect control was added, why the e2e spec mocks nothing) is currently recorded nowhere but in the comments themselves. A reader following the citation finds the file ends one ADR earlier.
informational.fix: Write ADR-144 in docs/26_DECISIONS.md covering the shared `SystemAdminOnly` guard, the reconnect control that gave `POST /api/v1/mcp/:id/reconnect` its first caller, and the e2e boundary spec.

informational.title: "Never inherited: an MCP subprocess must not receive the API's environment" is not what the transport does
informational.evidence: manager.ts:354-355: `// Never inherited: an MCP subprocess must not receive the API's environment (ADR-055).` followed by `env: e.env && typeof e.env === "object" ? (e.env as Record<string, string>) : undefined,`. `node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/stdio.js:66-69` spawns with `// merge default env with server env because mcp server needs some env vars` / `env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ...this._serverParams.env }` — unconditionally, whether or not `env` was supplied. `getDefaultEnvironment()` (same file, lines 28-40) copies `DEFAULT_INHERITED_ENV_VARS` from `process.env`: on win32 `APPDATA, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, LOCALAPPDATA, PATH, PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE, SYSTEMDRIVE, SYSTEMROOT, TEMP, USERNAME, USERPROFILE, PROGRAMFILES`; elsewhere `HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, TERM, USER`.
informational.why_it_matters: The security posture is fine in practice — the allowlist carries no secret this platform holds (no DATABASE_URL, no provider keys, no MCP bearer headers) — but the comment states an absolute the code cannot deliver, and an operator reading it would believe a `cwd`-relative or PATH-dependent spawn is impossible. It is also the kind of claim that stops being true silently if a future SDK widens the allowlist.
informational.fix: Reword to what actually holds: the API's own environment is not passed through, and the SDK adds a fixed allowlist (PATH/HOME/USER and equivalents) that carries no platform secret. Pin it with a test asserting no configured secret name appears in the spawned child's env.

informational.title: `chat-stream.ts` releases the reader instead of cancelling it (the exact ADR-140 defect), and the test that claims to prove cancellation cannot fail
informational.evidence: chat-stream.ts:125-128: `} finally { // Releasing the reader is what actually stops the server streaming into a page nobody is reading any more; without it an aborted chat keeps being billed. reader.releaseLock(); }`. `releaseLock()` detaches the reader from the stream; it does not cancel the body or close the connection. shared/src/sse.ts:47-51 states the opposite and correct rule for the same situation — "Cancelling the reader is what actually closes the connection" — with `await reader.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, and ADR-140 exists solely because that distinction was missed once already. The same wrong mechanism is repeated in frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx:166-168 ("Aborting releases the reader, which stops the server streaming"). The cancellation test asserts only plumbing: chat-stream.test.ts:135-145 `it("passes the abort signal through so a cancelled chat stops being billed")` ends with `expect(init.signal).toBe(controller.signal)` and never calls `controller.abort()`, so it would still pass if the finally block were deleted.
informational.why_it_matters: Cancellation happens to work today because the `signal` passed to `fetch` aborts the response body, so the `releaseLock` line is inert rather than harmful. But two comments and a test now attest to a mechanism that is not the one working, which is precisely how ADR-140's missing link survived four audits — and any refactor that drops the signal (or any caller that abandons the generator without aborting, which `ChatView`'s manual `.next()` driving would do without ever running the `finally`) would leave the upstream stream open and billing with no test to catch it.
informational.fix: Use `await reader.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` in the finally, matching shared/src/sse.ts, and add a test that aborts the controller mid-stream and asserts the underlying ReadableStream's `cancel()` was invoked — the shape shared/src/sse.test.ts:74-129 already uses.

informational.title: Neither hijacked SSE response honours backpressure
informational.evidence: chat.ts:332-337 `const send = (event) => { if (abort.signal.aborted || reply.raw.writableEnded || reply.raw.destroyed) return; reply.raw.write(...) }` and agent.ts:139-142, identically. The boolean returned by `write()` is discarded and neither route ever waits on a `drain` event; `grep -n "drain" backend/src/routes/v1/*.ts` returns no matches. The chat loop pulls from the provider as fast as it yields (chat.ts:384-402) regardless of whether the socket has accepted anything.
informational.why_it_matters: A slow or stalled reader (mobile radio, a paused tab, a proxy that stops draining) causes the whole remaining completion to accumulate in the Node process's socket write buffer rather than applying pressure back to the provider stream. With `max_instance_count = 3` and a 300/min global rate limit this is a memory-growth risk rather than an outage, and the tool-result previews are already capped at 500 bytes (engine.ts:869-875), which is why this is informational rather than a defect — but the mechanism ADR-140 built to stop paying for an unread stream does not engage for a reader that is slow rather than gone.
informational.fix: Have `send` return `reply.raw.write(...)` and, in the chat loop, `await once(reply.raw, "drain")` (racing `abort.signal`) when it returns false, so a stalled client pauses the provider pull instead of buffering it.

informational.title: Two usage aggregates exist on the Postgres implementation but are unreachable through the interface callers hold
informational.evidence: `PgUsageRecordRepository.sumEmbeddingTokensSince` (line 129) and `sumSpeechCharactersSince` (line 134) are declared on the class but not on the `UsageRecordRepository` interface (lines 39-60). backend/src/context.ts:69 types the shared handle as `usage: UsageRecordRepository`, so no route can call them. `grep -rn "sumEmbeddingTokensSince|sumSpeechCharactersSince" --include=*.ts backend/ frontend/ shared/ --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist` finds only the two definitions and two comment references in backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.test.ts. QuotaManager uses the tenant-wide variants instead (quota-manager.ts:128, 178), which is correct post-ADR-126.
informational.why_it_matters: Not a defect — the per-project variants were superseded by the ADR-126 tenant-wide ones. Worth knowing because the docstring on `sumEmbeddingTokensSince` still explains why `QuotaManager.checkEmbeddingTokens` needs it, which will mislead the next reader into thinking it is the live aggregate.
informational.fix: Delete the two superseded methods, or move their explanatory docstrings onto the `*ForTenantSince` methods that actually back the quota checks.

informational.title: Memory soft delete is project-scoped but not user-scoped, so a member can delete another member's user-scope memory they cannot read
informational.evidence: `PgMemoryItemRepository.softDelete` filters on `projectId`, `id` and `isNull(deletedAt)` only (memory-item-repository.ts:313-316) — no `user_id` predicate. Its caller, `DELETE /api/v1/memory/:id` (backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:518-523), passes only `scopeOf(authCtx)`. Both read paths do enforce ownership: `searchSemantic` (lines 226-228) and `listRecent` (lines 261-266) apply "mine, or the project's", and the repository's own docstring quotes docs/08 §6 — "a memory fact about User A must never be retrievable into a conversation with User B".
informational.why_it_matters: Exploitation requires knowing a v4 UUID that the reads deliberately never disclose to that member, so this is not practically reachable today. It is an asymmetry worth recording: the read side is carefully user-scoped and the write side is not, so any future path that surfaces memory ids project-wide (an admin listing, an export, a provenance field) turns this into a real cross-user delete.
informational.fix: Add the same ownership predicate the reads use — `or(eq(memoryItems.userId, userId), isNull(memoryItems.userId))` — to `softDelete`, and thread `authCtx.user.id` from the route.

informational.title: logging.ts's three exported field-shape interfaces are imported by nothing, and the log lines they describe have drifted
informational.evidence: `grep -rn "CorrelationFields\|ProviderCallFields\|ToolCallFields" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v /dist/` returns only their three declarations in logging.ts (lines 48, 55, 65). No importer anywhere — not backend/src, not agent-core, not model-router. The module docstring at logging.ts:1-5 nevertheless says these are "cross-process correlation helpers shared by backend's routes, job workers, and the agent-core/model-router call sites that log provider calls." Because nothing binds them, the real lines have diverged from the declared shape: `ProviderCallFields` requires `provider`, `model`, `latency_ms` and `status`, but the image worker's "provider call completed" line (backend/src/index.ts:831-840) emits only `request_id`, `job_id`, `project_id`, `provider`, `status` — no `model`, no `latency_ms` — while the chat route's line (chat.ts:510-524) does carry all of them plus `tokens_input`/`tokens_output`.
informational.why_it_matters: Two log lines with the same message string ("provider call completed") have different field sets, so any aggregation or dashboard built on that message silently drops the media calls from a latency panel. The types exist to prevent exactly that and are not applied anywhere, while the docstring asserts they are — so a reader checking whether the convention is enforced gets a yes from the comment and a no from the code.
informational.fix: Either type the call sites (`logger.info({ ... } satisfies ProviderCallFields, "provider call completed")` at chat.ts:511, index.ts:832, index.ts:894 and the agent path) — which will immediately flag the missing `model`/`latency_ms` on the media workers — or delete the interfaces and correct the docstring. The first is the better trade: it is the only mechanism that keeps the field names in docs/20 §1.2 honest.

informational.title: A provider that reports failure as an error event instead of throwing is never counted in provider_request_count
informational.evidence: In `streamChat`, the committed path closes the inner generator in a `finally` (router.ts:~258 `await iterator.return?.(undefined)`), but the three fallback branches do not. `if (first.value.type === "error") { ...report(...); continue; }` (router.ts:214-219) and `if (first.done) { ...report(...); continue; }` (router.ts:207-213) both `continue` while the `streamWithRetry` generator is suspended at its `yield first.value`. A suspended generator that is merely dropped never runs its `finally`, so the `settle(sawDone ? "success" : "cancelled")` at router.ts:~334 — the only thing that calls `reportCall` on that path — never executes, and `backend/src/index.ts:1118`'s `recordProviderCall` is never reached for that attempt. Latent today: `grep -rn 'type: "error"' --include=*.ts backend/packages backend/src` shows no shipped adapter yields an error event as its first event — llm-openai/src/index.ts:243, llm-google/src/index.ts:206 and the rest all `throw new ProviderError(...)`, which does go through the counted `catch` at router.ts:290-299. The only producers of a first `error` event are router.test.ts:86 and :164 and spend-guards.test.ts:237. The `first.done` (empty stream) branch is reachable in principle and is likewise uncounted.
informational.why_it_matters: ADR-132's whole point was that a failure which is not recorded as a failure but simply not recorded at all is "worse than no metric, because it looks like evidence". The guarantee stated at router.ts:73 ("Called once per completed provider call, whatever its outcome") has two holes in it; they are unreachable only because every current adapter happens to throw. A new adapter — or an adapter changed to surface a soft refusal as an error event rather than an exception — would reintroduce the exact 100%-success-during-an-outage dashboard ADR-132 fixed, with no test failing.
informational.fix: Add `await iterator.return?.(undefined);` before each `continue` in the three fallback branches (router.ts:203, 212, 218), which lets `streamWithRetry`'s `finally` run and `settle()` report the attempt. Add a router test that drives a provider yielding `{type:"error"}` first and asserts `onCall` fired exactly once with `status: "error"`.
